803910.description: Turfgrass management is the intentional care for low canopies of grass(es), family Poaceae. At the minimum, such care must involve mowing or cutting of leaf blades, usually with mechanical equipment. The possible purposes and benefits of turfgrass management may be recreation, esthetic appearance of the landscape, safety, evaporative cooling, conservation of soil or water, fire protection, and sanitation. If the purpose for caring for a grass canopy is a traditional agricultural product such as (1) feed, (2) fiber, or (3) food, then the appropriate category would be (1) Pastures and Forages, (2) Fiber Crops, or (3) Crops.

804001.title: Precision Farming
804001.description: Precision farming is the application of technology to manage the heterogeneity within a field. Traditional agriculture considers a field as a homogeneous unit. Fields used to be smaller and more uniform, and field boundaries were probably adapted to get uniform fields. As a result of mechanization, farmers are able to work bigger areas and fields became bigger and more variable. Farmers and agronomists are looking for tools to manage the local differences in fields.   Precision farming is a tool to handle the spatial and temporal variability and creates a framework to understand and control the (local) processes in the field. An ensemble of collected information (including yield maps, soil maps, multi-spectral satellite remote-sensing images, etc.) can be used to develop management strategies that reduce needed inputs, and result in higher profitability, environmental protection and/or higher yields.

803899.title: Soil Morphology, Classification and Survey
803899.description: # What are Soil Morphology, Classification and Survey? Soil Morphology, Classification and Survey are three intimately related sub-disciplines of soil science. They are used one after the other:   1. DESCRIBING and MEASURING soil properties in one or several places (for instance its physical, chemical and biological characteristics, or its internal organisation). Although each example is related to another "Soils" sub-discipline, the overall process is often related as "SOIL MORPHOLOGY"   2. Once soil properties have been measured, it is possible to try to interpret them: What are the main traits of the soil morphology? How does behaves this soil (water flow, etc.)? How the soil has been formed (that is its "pedogenesis") and on which parental materials? As there are infinite variations in soil properties, soil scientist often CLASSIFY soils in CATEGORIES/CLASSES. They have built CLASSIFICATION SYSTEMS that operates at various scales: international, national or regional.   3. What often interest farmers, agronomists or soil scientists is usually not a "local" description, but a more "global" view of soil (at the plot or the region scale): It is the soil MAPPING/SURVEY process. Not only soil mapping does rely on soil classification to present the survey results in a readable way, but it also involves a complex "interpolation" methods, aiming at predicting how is the soil in unsampled location.   # Dmoz users will find here resources on each of the above mentioned topic:   - Guidelines for soil description (see Soils sub-categories for more specific soil properties);  - Reference guides for soil classification;  - Reference guides for soil mapping;  - Soil survey information: Soil and soil properties maps and databases;   - etc. etc.   These reference are often available for various countries (and international institutions).  # It is good to keep in mind that soil survey/maps often serves as basis for DERIVED MAPS of specific soil properties, for various purposes: Soil aptitude to cultivation, waste amendment; Soil susceptibility to water logging or erosion; Aptitude of the soil to degrade mobile pollutants (or its contrary, risks of pollutant leaching); etc. etc. Such topic will only be placed in this category if they are not presented in other Dmoz categories.   # Finally, it worth citing a few synonyms or related topics for "Soil Morphology, Classification or Survey"   - Digital Soil Mapping (this term embraces all the new computer-based quantitative techniques being developed for mapping soils);   - Soil geography;   - Land resources (Soils are only one of these resources);   - Pedology (closely, but not exclusively related to soil morphology, classification and survey);   - Pedogenesis (idem)   [please e-mail the category editor for any suggestion about this Description]

803905.title: Biointensive Culture
803905.description: Using methods dating back thousands of years, it was formalized and brought to the US by famous English horticulturist, Alan Chadwick. Originally termed French Biodynamic Intensive, and then Biointensive gardening, it is now termed and promoted more properly as Biointensive Sustainable Mini-Farming. It is one of the most productive forms of agriculture extant, often exceeding standard culture methods by two to six times. Biointensive agriculture is almost always done using all-organic methods. It differs from more orthodox culture systems via combining five tactics, which almost always occur together:  1) Double-dug, raised beds: Usually 3-5 feet wide, separated by paths, digging to two feet deep. Planted soil is never walked on. This keeps soil uncompacted, gives plant roots maximum freedom to grow, lets soil absorb and retain far more water with far less erosion, makes weeding far easier.  2) Dense (intensive) planting: Instead of rows, arrange plants in hexagonal arrays so they grow to shade soil from direct sun, shade out weeds, conserve soil moisture, and shelter helpful creatures.  3) Composting: Fertilizes, aerates, and builds soil, raises water capacity.  4) Intercropping, companion planting: Grow some plants near each other to raise yields, repel pests, attract helpful creatures, build soil.  5) Whole system synergy: Use all tactics together for maximum results. If any tactic is omitted, results are poorer.  Overall, emphasis is less on growing plants, and more on growing soil, since it is the soil which ultimately feeds us.

811507.title: Velikovsky, Immanuel
811507.description: About the life, work, and theories of Immanuel Velikovsky (1895-1979), who developed and published a set of theories about earth's history that explained many historical events and events in geologic history as caused by interactions with other planets. The book Worlds in Collision asserted that around 3,500 years ago the planet Venus was ejected from the planet Jupiter as a comet. Comet Venus then started wandering through the solar system. Its gravitational field pushed other planets out of their orbits or changed their rotation. Velikovsky attributed many of the disasters recorded in ancient times to this strange interaction the Earth had with Venus. A psychiatrist by training, Velikovsky did not base his claims on astronomical evidence and scientific inference or argument. Instead, he argued on the basis of ancient cosmological myths from places as disparate as India and China, Greece and Rome, Assyria and Sumer.

links.title: The Immanuel Velikovsky Archive

links.description: Presents information on aberrations, obstruction effects, and reflecting, refracting, and catadioptric objectives, and the eyepiece and eye.

links.title: Mike Barrell's Astronomy Page
links.description: Equipment information, alignment tips, images, planet finder, ham radio/WB9DLC, and links.

812612.title: Chats and Forums
812612.description: This category deals with chat and forum websites that deal with specific brands of telescopes.  We also list generalized sites that would be of interest to any telescope owner.

812529.title: Astronomers
812529.description: This category is a listing of personal webpages related to astronomy. This includes webpages of astronomers and other people who have a strong interest in astronomy and which is shown on the website.

links.title: Dr. Patrick Hartigan
links.description: Research group at Rice University focused on young stars, stellar jets and shock waves.

links.title: Edward M. Sion
links.description: Specializes in white dwarf studies.  Includes curriculum vitae and research articles. Professor of Astronomy and Astrophysics at Villanova University.

links.title: George P. McCook
links.description: Specializes in mathematic analysis of astronomical data.  Professor of Astronomy at Villanova University.  Includes educational background and research.

links.title: Georgi Petrov
links.description: Fields of interest include extragalactic astronomy, spectroscopy, photometry, surface photometry, active galactic nuclei, open clusters, and the large scale structure of the Universe. In English and Bulgarian.

links.title: Glenn Schneider
links.description: HST/NICMOS and other recent astronomical  endeavors, professional and personal. Includes CV and publications. Steward Observatory, University of Arizona.

links.title: Dr. Melissa N. Hayes-Gehrke
links.description: Includes teaching and research and personal interests. University of Maryland.

links.title: Professor Irakli Simonia
links.description: Provides biographical information, research interests in astrophysics, cultural astronomy and archaeoastronomy and selected publications.

links.title: Rees, Martin
links.description: Professor of Cosmology and Astrophysics at the University of Cambridge. Includes CV, research interests and publications.

links.title: Courtney Seligman, Professor of Astronomy
links.description: Class materials, online astronomy text (work in progress), astronomical activities and information about Professor Seligman's fictional works.

links.title: Ashkbiz Danehkar
links.description: Post-Doctoral Fellow in the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics at Cambridge, Massachusetts. Includes research interests, resume and publications.

links.title: Nichi D'Amico
links.description: Chair Professor of Astrophysics at Cagliari University, in Sardinia, Italy. Includes CV, publications and research interests.

links.title: Roger Wesson
links.description: Astronomer working at Cardiff University, where he investigate the dust associated with core-collapse supernovae and their progenitors.

links.title: Randall Smith
links.description: Astrophysicist at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics, primarily working in high-energy astrophysics.

links.title: Roger Leiton-Thompson
links.description: Provides details of his interests and projects including globular clusters, NASA's space interferometry mission, supernova remnants and light pollution. Universidad de Concepcion, Chile

links.title: Charles Greeley Abbot
links.description: Presents a brief biography of the astrophysicist.

links.title: Time and Date
links.description: Information such as yearly and monthly calendars, counters, countdown, and the world clock which shows the current time in cities all over the world.

links.title: Blue Moon Myths
links.description: Second full moon in a month, or third full moon in a single season.

links.title: Maya Calendar 2000
links.description: The calendar was the center of Maya life and their greatest cultural achievement. To carry out their astronomical calculations they developed a sophisticated mathematical system. The Maya Calendar website is developing with the intent of providing a complete view of Maya culture.

links.title: The Difference Between the Millennium and Year 2000
links.description: Questions and answers to satisfy the hearts of true millennium buffs.

links.title: Calendars through the Ages
links.description: History and FAQs of calendars, from ancient Rome to outer space. Including Julian, Gregorian, Jewish, Islamic, Chinese, and Mayan.

links.title: Annus Novus Decimal Calendar
links.description: A proposal for a non-sectarian, culturally neutral calendar system.

links.title: Astronomy by JavaScript: Sun Calculators and More
links.description: Applets related to calendars and keeping time, including sidererial time.

links.title: The Calendar, Leap Years and the Year 2000
links.description: An explanation of the calendar including the origin of the day, week, month and year.

links.title: Astro Portal - CalSKY
links.description: The worldwide interactive online astronomical/space calendar and calculator - for friends of astronomy, as well as astronomers.

links.title: Lunisolar Calendar
links.description: Lunar calendar with lunations, from new moon to new moon, instead of months. Moon phase on each day. Chinese, Jewish, and Islamic months. Eclipses, meteors, planets, star charts. Christian, Pagan, Islamic, Hindu, and Jewish holidays.

links.title: The Julian and Gregorian Calendars
links.description: Explanations of the Julian Calendar, the Gregorian Reform, the adoption of the Gregorian Calendar, the length of the tropical year and related matters.

links.title: Julian Day Numbers
links.description: An explanation of the Julian day number system used by astronomers and calendricists.

links.title: Types of Calendars
links.description: An explanation of lunar, solar, lunisolar, rule-based and other calendars.

links.title: Hindu Calendar Dates 52nd Century
links.description: Explains the cosmological and astronomical influences in creating the Indian calendar.

links.title: Calendar Studies
links.description: Articles on the Gregorian and Julian calendars, the ISO date format, the Julian day number system, the Maya calendar, the Goddess lunar calendar, the Liberalia Triday Calendar and C functions for date conversion; plus software for calendrical conversion.

links.title: Calendopaedia
links.description: The encyclopaedia of calendars.

812649.title: Sundials
812649.description: Sundials are devices for telling time by measuring the position of the shadow of the sun. This category lists websites concerned with the theory of sundials.

links.title: The North American Sundial Society
links.description: Includes general information, links, a register of dials in North America, and a message board.

links.title: The British Sundial Society
links.description: Information on the society, links, beginner's pages, including simple sundial patterns and templates, online facilities to calculate hour lines for different sundial types.

links.title: The Analemmatic Sundial
links.description: Describes design and construction of a six meter wide analemmatic sundial in Canada.

links.title: Sundial Design Program
links.description: Software to design a vertical (wall mounting) sundial for walls that face up to 60 degrees away from due-south.

links.title: Solar Time
links.description: Describes sundials that can tell sunrise and sunset times, the angle of solar declination and the time at night. (Flash based site).

links.title: Frans Maes' Sundial Site
links.description: Describes a number of sundials of different types, mostly from  northern Europe.

links.title: A Photo Collection of Beautiful Painted Wall Sundials
links.description: Photographs with descriptions, showing a number of patterns painted on walls.

links.title: The Sundial Primer - Get "Hooked on Gnomonics"
links.description: Offers advice, instructions, and resources for creating a wide variety of sundials.

links.title: Sundial - Wikipedia
links.description: Account includes a description of the commoner types, an explanation of the relevant science and maths, and a history of sundial use.

links.title: Cadrans Solaire
links.description: Describes different types of sundials, has other technical and general information. Offers free Shadows software to compute sundials of a number of different types for anywhere in the world.

links.title: Sundials: the Art of Shadows
links.description: An essay on the use of sundials in gardens.

links.title: Analemmatic Sundials
links.description: Descriptions of these vertical post sundials, why they work, detailed account of the maths necessary to plot the hour lines.

links.title: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Sundials and Shadow Clocks
links.description: Animations of some of the historical stages of the development of sundials.

links.title: Sundials of Scotland
links.description: Descriptions with photographs of Scottish sundials, ancient, old and new as well as sundials from some other places. Includes registers of sundials seen, which are fully searchable by any criterion.

links.title: Macmillan Hunter Sundials
links.description: A range of sundials for measuring the hours and reading the season as well as astronomical instruments for complex calculations.

812617.title: Cosmology
812617.description: Cosmology is the scientific study of the structure and origin of the universe as a whole.

links.title: Ned Wright's Cosmology Tutorial
links.description: Site maintained by a UCLA astronomy professor, which features an introduction to cosmology (which uses no more than high-school level mathematics), links to resources, a section on "fads and fallacies", and comments on latest developments.

links.title: Faith and Reason: Cosmology
links.description: Companion site to the PBS mini-series "Faith & Reason". The cosmology section discusses the challenge to traditional Christian views posed by the scientific understanding of cosmological evolution, and ways in which they might be reconciled.

links.title: Runaway Universe
links.description: Companion website for a PBS NOVA program originally broadcast in 2000, which examines the size, future and fate of the universe. Contains background material on mapping the universe, supernovae as standard candles, and a virtual tour of the universe.

links.title: Introduction to Cosmology
links.description: Lecture notes by David H. Lyth (Lancaster University), with a special emphasis on large scale structure, the anisotropies of the cosmic microwave radiation, and inflation. Presupposes basic knowledge of physics at an undergraduate level, as well as some familiarity with particle physics.

links.title: The Big Bang (One More Time)
links.description: Article from Christian Science Monitor about Paul Steinhardt and his work on the "Ekpyrotic Universe", a speculative model which uses concepts of string theory to arrive at a periodically repeating series of big bangs.

links.title: Cosmology: A Research Briefing
links.description: Online book from the National Academy of Sciences, published in 1995 by the National Research Council's Board on Cosmology as a re-assessment of the cosmological research earlier examined by the Physics Survey Committee. Includes  chapters on the cosmic background radiation, the large scale structure of universe, and the physics of the early universe.

links.title: WMAP Introduction to Cosmology
links.description: Basic introduction to modern cosmology, aimed at a general audience. This NASA site is part of the outreach efforts for the WMAP space probe, which measures an "Echo of the Big Bang": the cosmic microwave background radiation.

links.title: LEVEL 5 - A Knowledgebase for Extragalactic Astronomy and Cosmology
links.description: Extensive collection of articles, monographs, data bases, tools and essays related to extragalactic astronomy and cosmology. Maintained by Barry F. Madore (Caltech and Carnegie Observatory).

links.title: Cambridge Cosmology - Public Homepage
links.description: Webpages created by the Cambridge University cosmology group for a general audience, with information about black holes, the big bang models, cosmic strings, galaxies and galaxy clusters, and inflation.

links.title: Cosmology
links.description: Entry in Eric Weisstein's World of Physics. Contains many links to related entries, and a list of useful materials.

links.title: Cosmological Models
links.description: Lecture notes for graduate-level lectures originally given at the 1998 Cargese summer school, by George Ellis and Henk van Elst.  The notes give a systematic presentation of a 1+3 covariant approach to studying the geometry, dynamics, and observational properties of the cosmological models of general relativity.

links.title: Introduction to Cosmology
links.description: Condensed lecture notes at graduate-student level on standard cosmology, the physics of the early universe, and inflation. Based on lectures given by G. Lazarides (Aristotle University of Thessaloniki) at the 1998 Corfu Summer Institute on Elementary Particle Physics.

812618.title: Articles
812618.description: Articles on specific cosmological topics (excluding those that have their own categories).

links.title: Multidimensional Gravity and Cosmology
links.description: Review article by V. N. Melnikov on exact solutions in multidimensional cosmology. Based on talks given at the eigth Marcel Grossmann Meeting, in Jerusalem.

links.title: Topology of the Universe
links.description: A simple introduction to the idea that the universe might have a more complicated shape than is usually assumed, and to the consequences of that idea. Written by Mark Baltovic; uses simple mathematical concepts only.

links.title: Cosmic Topology
links.description: Technical article by M. Lachieze-Rey and J. P. Luminet about cosmic topology: global properties of the universe that are not restricted by general relativity.

links.title: Minkowski Functionals in Cosmology
links.description: A brief (if technical) tutorial on the basic features of Minkowski functional, a new class of morphological measures. Includes information on their practical application for simulation data and galaxy redshift catalogues. By J. Schmalzing, M. Kerscher, and T. Buchert.

links.title: Current Trends in Mathematical Cosmology
links.description: Technical article which reviews current unsolved problems in mathematical cosmology, including the question of singularities, problems associated with the definition and asymptotic structure of the notion of cosmological solutions, and problems related to the qualification of approximations. By Spiros Cotsakis (University of the Aegean).

links.title: Universe Today: The Universe is Not Expanding Uniformly
links.description: Article about a finding by Mike Hudson of the University of Waterloo in Ontario, Canada, that different parts of the Universe are expanding at different rates.

812621.title: Cosmic Background Radiation
812621.description: Sites that deal with the "electromagnetic echo" of the big bang phase, the cosmic background radiation. Also includes observational missions specifically directed at observing the cosmic background radiation and its properties.

links.title: BOOMERanG (Caltech)
links.description: One of the homepages of the BOOMERanG project, a balloon-borne millimeter-wave telescope designed to study the anisotropy in the cosmic microwave background radiation. Includes a project overview, a blog, and data releases.

links.title: The Cosmic Microwave Background
links.description: Information about the cosmic microwave background radiation by Douglas Scott (University of British Columbia). Includes texts for a general audience, an FAQ, a number of images, and links to related sites.

links.title: Introduction to the Cosmic Microwave Background
links.description: Basic explanations of key concepts related to the cosmic background radiation, including the big bang models of an expanding universe and the ripples in the density of the early universe that led to the galaxies and stars that can be seen today. By Wayne Hu (University of Chicago).

links.title: Legacy Archive for Microwave Data Analysis
links.description: Contains both original data and descriptions for NASA's past missions to explore the cosmic background radiation, notably about the Cosmic Background Explorer (COBE) satellite.

links.title: Planck Satellite
links.description: Homepage of an ESA mission due to be launched in late 2008, and designed to make precision measurements of the cosmic background radiation. Includes an image gallery, a science overview, a technical overview and additional material.

links.title: WMAP Mission homepage
links.description: Homepage of the Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe, a NASA satellite launched in 2001. The goal of WMAP are precision measurements of the cosmic microwave background, the "electromagnetic echo" of the big bang phase of the early universe.

links.title: Archeops
links.description: A 1999 balloon-borne instrument dedicated to measuring the Cosmic microwave background (CMB) temperature anisotropies.

812628.title: Cosmological Constant and Dark Energy
812628.description: Sites dealing with explanations for the observed acceleration of our universe's expansion, which can be described either by what is called the cosmological constant or by assuming that empty space is filled with an energy form known as Dark Energy.

links.title: Supernova Cosmology Project
links.description: Homepage of a research project based at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, dedicated to using observations of supernova explosions to measure the distance of far-away galaxies; this, in turn allows one to map the properties of cosmic expansion.

links.title: Quintessence and the Cosmological Constant
links.description: A review of the basic idea of the cosmological constant, and of proposals to replace it by a time-varying field. By Michael Doran and Christof Wetterich.

links.title: Dark Energy Survey
links.description: Project aiming to understand why the universe is accelerating and not being slowed by the mass it contains.

812627.title: Courses and Tutorials
812627.description: This category hosts course descriptions and tutorials for (university-level) courses on cosmology.

links.title: Cosmology Course Notes
links.description: Information about the course Cosmology and Exobiology, read in the fall semester 1999 by E. and K. Oestaard, at the Physics  Institute of NTNU, Trondheim. In its current form, this contains lecture notes on the basics of cosmology, suitable for undergraduates.

812620.title: Dark Matter
812620.description: By observing galactic motions and from cosmology we know that there is a mass in the Universe that we cannot observe so far. It is called dark matter, as opposed to bright stars. It could be some kind of elementary particles.

links.title: Dark Matter Mystery
links.description: Elementary introduction to dark matter, suitable for a general audience. The pages are part of the public outreach effort of the Chandra X-Ray Observatory, and hosted by Harvard University.

links.title: Discussion about Dark Matter
links.description: Transcript of an on-air discussion between physicists Michio Kaku and Stuart Samuel on the subject of dark matter. Suitable for a general audience. Aired on WBAI's   "Explorations in Science" on December 3, 1997.

links.title: Dark Matter
links.description: Description of dark matter, its properties and consequences. Includes texts, plots, graphs and schematics. By Martin White (University of California, Berkeley).

links.title: The Early History of Dark Matter
links.description: Article about the discovery of, and early research on, dark matter by Zwicky, Smith, Babcock and Oort in the 1930's and 1940's. By Sidney van den Bergh (Dominion Astrophysical Observatory, Herzberg Institute of Astrophysics, National Research Council of Canada).

links.title: What is Dark Matter?
links.description: One-page explanation of dark matter from the Usenet Physics FAQ, written by Scott I. Chase.

links.title: CRESST
links.description: Homepage of the CRESST experiment (Cryogenic Rare Event Search with Superconducting Thermometers), a European collaboration to search for particle constituents of dark matter in the Gran Sasso laboratories.

links.title: Particle Dark Matter: Evidence, Candidates and Constraints
links.description: Review article on particle dark matter, with a focus on experimental searches. Suitable for graduate students or advanced undergraduates. By Gianfranco Bertone, Dan Hooper and Joseph Silk.

links.title: ZEPLIN-III
links.description: Homepage of a collaborative experiment that searches for dark matter constituents. Includes information about the experiment, the collaborators in the UK, Portugal, and Russia, and publications.

links.title: Is Dark Matter Theory or Fact?
links.description: As part of Scientific American's "Ask the Experts" series, physicists Rhett Herman of Radford University and Shane L. Larson of Montana State University give an accessible account of the evidence for dark matter.

812624.title: Earliest Universe
812624.description: Sites on physics in the earliest universe, where quantum gravity effects were important. Includes quantum cosmology and cosmological models based on string theory.

links.title: Cosmology II: From Planck Time to BBN
links.description: Graduate-level review of progress in models of the earliest universe, including the role of strings, extra dimensions, phase transitions, inflation and baryogenesis. Summary of a talk given by Keith Olive (University of Minnesota) at the 1999 David N. Schramm Memorial Symposium.

links.title: From Newton's Laws to the Wheeler-deWitt equation
links.description: Pedagogical paper at a level accessible to undergraduate students. Starting with Newtonian models of physics, the basic ideas of cosmology and quantum cosmology are developed. By John W. Norbury (University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee).

links.title: Quantum Cosmology and Eternal Inflation
links.description: Lecture by Alexander Vilenkin on quantum cosmology, focusing on the tunneling approach. One of the lectures given as part of Stephen Hawking's 60th birthday; suitable for graduate students and advanced undergraduates.

links.title: Quantum Cosmology
links.description: A non-technical one-page overview of quantum cosmology, suitable for a general audience. Part of the outreach pages of the relativity group at Cambridge University.

links.title: An Introduction to Quantum Cosmology
links.description: Lecture notes on quantum cosmology, from the 3+1 formalism to the question of the arrow of time. By David Wiltshire; based on summer school lectures given in 1995. Suitable for graduate students.

links.title: Quantum Cosmology and the Structure of the Inflationary Universe
links.description: Review by Andrei Linde, which considers several different issues related to inflation, from the wave function of the       Universe to stochastic models and the question of reheating. Suitable for graduate students and advanced undergraduates.

links.title: Quantum Cosmology Lectures
links.description: Lectures given by Don Page at the First Mexican School on Gravitation and Mathematical Physics: an introduction to quantum cosmology which pays particular attention to the question of the interpretation of quantum theory.

812626.title: String Cosmology
812626.description: Cosmological models for the very early universe that are based on string theory. Includes brane models such as the ekpyrotic universe or brane inflation.

links.title: String Cosmology: A Review
links.description: Review of cosmological models based on string theory, with a focus on large extra dimensions. Based on a talk by Gerald Cleaver (Baylor University and HARC) at COSPAR '02, Houston, Texas, October 2002. Presupposes previous knowledge in astronomy and particle physics.

links.title: A Simple Introduction to Pre-Big-Bang Physics/Cosmology
links.description: Introduction to pre-big bang scenarios based on string theory,   with a focus on physical motivations, considerations, and consequences. By Gabriele Veneziano (CERN); suitable for graduate students and researchers.

links.title: String Cosmology
links.description: An introduction to string theory-based cosmological models. Based on lectures given by Nick E. Mavromatos (King's College, London) at the First Aegean Summer School on Cosmology, Samos, in 2001. Suitable for graduate students and more advanced readers.

links.title: Elementary introduction to pre-big bang cosmology and to the relic graviton background
links.description: A self-contained introduction to string cosmology and, in particular, to the background of relic cosmic gravitons predicted in the context of the so-called "pre-big bang". The text is aimed at graduate and advanced undergraduate students, and based on notes for lectures held by M. Gasperini at two schools in 1997 and 1998.

links.title: Brane Cosmology
links.description: Lecture notes based on summer school lectures given in 2001 by E. Papantonopoulos (National Technical University of Athens). Suitable for graduate and advanced undergraduate students.

links.title: The Cyclic Universe
links.description: Introduction to the ekpyrotic universe, written by the model's creators, Paul J. Steinhardt and Neil Turok. Most of the text can be understood with basic physics knowledge; some sections require advanced knowledge.

812619.title: History
812619.description: Sites and articles dealing with the history of (modern, as opposed to ancient) cosmology

links.title: Cosmology: Methodological Debates 1932-48
links.description: Argues how cosmology between 1932-48 provides an excellent example for philosophical considerations directing the evolution of modern science.  Article by George Gale in the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy.

links.title: Great Debates in Astronomy
links.description: Background information, educational material, and published proceedings for a series of debates on fundamental questions of astronomy at the Smithsonian's Museum of Natural History between 1995 and 1998. Also includes material on the great debate between Harlow Shapley and Heber Curtis on the scale of the universe, held at the same location in 1920.

812622.title: Inflation
812622.description: Site dealing with the inflationary models of standard cosmology. Such models describe a period of rapid expansion that takes place a split second after the big bang.

links.title: An Exposition on Inflationary Cosmology
links.description: A pedagogical treatment of cosmological modeling and inflationary cosmology, suitable for graduate students. By Scott Watson (Brown University).

links.title: Introductory Review of Cosmic Inflation
links.description: Lecture notes by Shinji Tsujikawa (Univ. of Tokyo) about the basic concepts of inflation, the generation of density perturbations, and the mechanism for reheating after inflation. Based on lectures given at The Second Tah Poe School on Cosmology in 2003.

links.title: A Status Review of Inflationary Cosmology
links.description: Thorough review of inflationary cosmology which focuses on two areas of recent progress: reheating and the quantum theory of cosmological perturbations.  Suitable for graduate students and researchers.

812629.title: Large-Scale Structure
812629.description: Sites and articles dealing with the formation of the universe's large-scale structure. Includes both observations of that structure and simulations of structure formation.

links.title: Sloan Digital Sky Survey
links.description: Homepage of a major research project dedicated to producing a systematic map of a quarter of the sky, producing new catalogues for deep-sky objects and constraining the parameters for cosmological models. Includes a data archive, an image gallery, and outreach material.

links.title: Numerical Simulations in Cosmology I: Methods
links.description: A short introduction to the different numerical methods used in cosmology, with a focus on the major features of N-body simulations: equations, main numerical techniques, effects of resolution, and methods of halo identification. By Anatoly Klypin (New Mexico State University).

812623.title: Nucleosynthesis
812623.description: Sites about the formation of the first chemical elements - nuclei other than that of hydrogen - during the first few minutes after the big bang.

812630.title: Research Groups
812630.description: Homepages of research groups whose main focus is cosmology.

links.title: Caltech Observational Cosmology Group
links.description: Group homepage, with descriptions of the various missions the group is involved in (including BOOMERanG and Planck). Includes information about group members and seminars.

links.title: Tufts Institute of Cosmology
links.description: Group homepage which includes information about research areas, staff, recent events, and seminars, as well as a number of links to other cosmology sites.

links.title: Max Tegmark
links.description: Personal homepage of cosmologist Max Tegmark (MIT). Includes useful material about the cosmic background radiation (movies and data analysis efforts), but also about the foundations of quantum mechanics.

812632.title: Software
812632.description: Software that can be used either for learning cosmology or for cosmology research.

links.title: iCosmos Cosmology Calculator
links.description: Enter standard cosmological parameters (such as the overall matter density, the cosmological constant, and the redshift), and this calculator will present a number of cosmological quantities (particularly the various distances), including some helpful graphical representations. By Mihran Vardanyan.

links.title: Cosmic Strings and other Defects
links.description: Series of texts describing the basics and some of the consequences of topological defects in the universe. Part of the public pages of the relativity group at Cambridge University.

links.title: Formation, Interaction and Observation of Topological Defects
links.description: An introduction to the formation of defects in first-order phase transitions, the way these defects interact, and observational signatures of cosmic strings. Les Houches lectures by Tanmay Vachaspati, suitable for graduate students.

links.title: Topological Defects and Cosmology
links.description: Thorough review of the formation of defects and their consequences for cosmology. By Robert H. Brandenberger.

links.title: Cosmic Strings
links.description: Extensive review of the field-theoretical foundations and the dynamics of cosmic strings and other topological defects. Suitable for students with previous knowledge of field theory and cosmology. By M. B. Hindmarsh and T. W. B. Kibble.

links.title: Cosmology from Topological Defects
links.description: Alejandro Gangui's graduate-level lecture notes about the possible cosmological role and observational signatures of topological defects. Based on lectures delivered at the Xth Brazilian School on Cosmology and Gravitation in 2002.

links.title: SIMBAD Astronomical Database
links.description: The SIMBAD astronomical database provides basic data, cross-identifications and bibliography for astronomical objects outside the solar system. SIMBAD can be queried by object name, coordinates, other criteria (filters), and lists of objects.

links.title: SAO Telescope Data Center
links.description: Creates, and maintains software to process and archive data from optical telescopes at the Oak Ridge Observatory in Harvard, Massachusetts, Whipple Observatory, and Multiple Mirror Telescope on Mt. Hopkins in Arizona. The Smithsonian Astrophysical Observatory (SAO) is part of the Harvard- Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics (CfA) in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

links.title: The Aladin Sky Atlas
links.description: Provides an interactive sky atlas allowing users to visualize digitized images of any part of the sky. Includes astronomical catalogs, personal user data files, and interactive access to related data from the Simbad database, and Vizier service.

links.title: Centre de Données astronomiques de Strasbourg
links.description: (CDS) Astronomical databases, bibliography, documentation, and directory.

links.title: DSS - The Digitized Sky Survey
links.description: Comprises a set of all-sky photographic surveys in E, V, J, R, and N bands conducted with the Palomar, and UK Schmidt telescopes at the Space Telescope Science Institute.

links.title: The VLA FIRST Survey
links.description: Faint images of the radio sky at the wavelength of 20 centimeters.

links.title: ESO/ST-ECF USNO-A1.0 Catalogue Server
links.description: Archive provides access to the all-sky catalogue from the set of ten CD-ROMs produced by the US Naval Observatory within the Precise Measurement Machine Project.

links.title: SIMBAD Astronomical Database
links.description: Offers data, cross-identifications, observational measurements, and bibliography for celestial objects outside the solar system including stars, galaxies, and nonstellar objects within our galaxy, or in external galaxies.

links.title: Personal Web pages
links.description: A list of the personal web pages of professional astronomers from around the world. Extensive.

links.title: MAST: Multimission Archive at STScI
links.description: MAST supports a variety of astronomical data archives, with the primary focus on scientifically related data sets in the optical, ultraviolet, and near-infrared parts of the spectrum.

links.title: Supercosmos Sky Surveys
links.description: Provides images, and catalogues of the southern sky in three colours. Includes access to digitised images, and the data derived from SuperCOSMOS scans of photographic Schmidt survey plates.

links.title: Solar Data Analysis Centre
links.description: Contains solar data, and images. Includes SDAC Data-Finder, current solar images, and TRACE analysis guides.

links.title: NVSS Postage Stamp Server
links.description: This postage Stamp server for NRAO/VLA Sky Survey (NVSS) returns radio images of the sky in FITS or JPEG  format.

links.title: Astronomy: Data Archives
links.description: Patrick Shopbell's Astronomy Resources. Contains data archives, astronomical catalogs, atlas of nearby dwarf galaxies, and links.

links.title: HEASARC
links.description: High Energy Astrophysics Science Archive Research Center. Provides an archive of data on (and software for analyzing) gamma-ray, X-ray, and extreme ultraviolet observations of  cosmic (non-solar) sources.

links.title: Microsoft Research and the SDSS SkyServer
links.description: A project to develop an Internet data resource in astronomy. Includes journals, reading, the sky server, team information, and links.

links.title: ESO, and Space Telescope Science Archive Facilities
links.description: A joint venture of The European Southern Observatory(ESO), and the Space Telescope European Coordinating Facility(ST-ECF). Includes a shared archive server, services, news, updates, digitized sky images, links, and public datasets.

links.title: Astronomy Picture of the Day Archive
links.description: Daily archive of interesting astronomy photos by NASA.

links.title: NED
links.description: The NASA/IPEC Extragalactic Database is built around a list of extragalactic objects with cross-identifications of names, positions and redshifts.

links.title: The ELODIE archive
links.description: Hosts more than 16000 Echelle spectra of 2000 objects from  the ELODIE spectrograph at OHP observatory.

links.title: DARTS

812441.title: History
812441.description: Astronomy is the scientific study of objects and phenomena beyond the earth's atmosphere by means other than visiting them or sending probes. The history of astronomy is the study of the development of astronomy from the earliest written records to somewhere very near the present time.    Astrology is not astronomy, but it did play a role in the development of astronomy. Babylonian astrologers' determination of the positions of stars may be found here, their study of the effects of those positions on human affairs will not.    The history of the scientific search for extra-terrestrial intelligence may be found here. UFOs visiting earth will not.    This category is not limited to Western astronomy. The written history of other astronomical traditions will be listed here.

812672.title: Software
812672.description: Software related to astronomy. This includes desktop planetarium and sky charting software, astronomy databases and observing utilities, simulation software, image processing and data analysis, education and multimedia software, and software reviews.  Please note that, even though only software with dedicated web pages is included in this directory, there are many programs (mainly shareware/freeware) that have no web sites dedicated to them and are only available from a number of online software repositories (links to such repositories are included in this directory).

links.title: Linux for Astronomy cdrom
links.description: Astronomical software precompiled for the Linux operating system. Applications include general purpose image and signal processing tools, as well as algorithms in use at observatories and universities worldwide. Facilities for processing the data products of the major space-based instruments are also included.  [Commercial - Linux]

links.title: Cartes du Ciel / Sky Charts
links.description: Freeware allowing one to draw charts according to the data of 15 catalogs of stars and nebulae, as well as the position of planets, asteroids, and comets.   Available in English and is translated in 8 other languages.

links.title: Astronomy Common Object Model (ASCOM)
links.description: Promoting the use of open scriptable tools for amateur and educational astronomy.

links.title: Astronomy Formulas
links.description: Lunar and solar periodicity formulas, definitions, time formulas, notation, astronomical constants with computer code for a programmable HP 48 by James Q. Jacobs.

links.title: Orrery
links.description: Review of the solar system simulator (by Spacetech) for RISC OS workstations.

links.title: Lunar Calendars and Eclipse Finder
links.description: Windows software for converting dates in various lunar and other calendars and for finding lunar phases and eclipses of various kinds.

links.title: AstroMB
links.description: Advanced software for astrometry, photometry, robotic observations. Huge database of images and catalogs. Works with MaximDL and ASCOM. Free downloads.

links.title: Alcyone Software
links.description: Features the following programs: an ephemeris calculator, a collection of astronomical data in electronic form, Planet Orbits, C88, and Planetary, Lunar, and Stellar Visibility.

links.title: Observation Manager
links.description: Free and open java based astronomical logging tool. It stores data in an XML format called COMAST, a tool which provides a free schema definition for all kinds of astronomical observations.

links.title: DanIDL
links.description: Provides a library of functions and routines written in the Interactive Data Language (IDL). Developed mainly for use in astronomy, the library also supplies general scientific and programming applications.

links.title: Kairos General Calendar Conversion Program
links.description: [commercial, demo available -- Win95/98/NT] Includes calendars required by historians of astronomy and general historians. Many details are provided for Indian and Jewish calendars. There is also a display of positions of the Sun, Moon and planets, effectively replacing Tuckerman's tables. A horoscope display, and details of lunar visibility, are calculated from modern parameters.

links.title: ShiningStar Software
links.description: This is a digital sky map software which demonstrate the universe in solar space mode, equator mode, and horizon mode. You can view the whole solar system, look at any of the planets nearly, see the whole sky as standing at anywhere on the earth.

links.title: Astropy
links.description: A community Python library for astronomy.

links.title: Instrument Neutral Distributed Interface (INDI)
links.description: The INDI library provides a framework for control and automation of astronomical instruments.

links.title: Caglow Central
links.description: A free project repository for [semi-]open astronomical software.

812673.title: Computational Astrophysics
812673.description: Contains links to research-grade web sites, projects and programs related to computational astrophysics. These are typically (though not necessarily) hosted by university research groups. Sites that contain educational or entertainment software related to solar-system and N-body simulators can be found in Science/Astronomy/Software/Space_Simulation.

links.title: Barnes & Hut Treecode Algorithm
links.description: [open source - multiplatform] A guide to a tree code algorithm implementation, used for astronomical N-body simulations.

links.title: ORSA - Orbit Reconstruction, Simulation and Analysis
links.description: ORSA is a C++ framework for the development of algorithms and programs oriented to the simulation and analysis of the orbital evolution of bodies in space.

links.title: Stellar Astrophysics Software
links.description: [open source - Windows] Various programs for stellar astrophysics. Includes CHANDRA stellar structure software for collapsed objects including rotating white dwarfs and neutron stars, and STARCAL for nuclear astrophysics and the stellar structure of main sequence stars with supernova forecasting.

links.title: Gadget-2
links.description: The Gadget-2 code is an SPH simulation code designed for cosmological simulations but can be used for a wide variety of astrophysical hydrodynamics simulations with self-gravity.

links.title: A TIPSY file viewer with MPI capabilities
links.description: [Open source - Linux] "Hubble in a bottle!" is visualization software for N-body simulations, which can be run in parallel  using MPI for visualizing very large simulation results.   Simulation output must be in TIPSY format.

links.title: Cloudy & Associates
links.description: Cloudy is an extensive, well-established, large-scale spectral synthesis code designed to simulate fully physical conditions within an astronomical plasma and then predict the emitted spectrum.  The web page contains links to papers published with cloudy, the most recent version of the software itself, and a discussion board.

links.title: COSMOMC-- Monte Carlo evaluation of CMB parameters
links.description: COSMOMC calculates a fast Markov Chain Monte-Carlo exploration of cosmological parameter space for an input set of constraints.

links.title: Grav-Sim
links.description: Grav-Sim is for astronomy and physics enthusiasts to conduct gravity simulations at home. It models a set of bodies gravitating under Newton's laws of motion.

links.title: Radex
links.description: A free computer program to calculate the strengths of atomic and molecular lines from interstellar clouds which are assumed to be homogeneous. Includes installation and running instructions and explains the output.

links.title: MegaStar Sky Atlas
links.description: Resource for deep-sky observing. [Commercial, demo available - Win3.1/95]

links.title: SkyMap

links.title: SkyTools
links.description: Observation planning, charting and logging software. [Commercial - Win95/98/NT]

links.title: Navigator Light
links.description: Celestial navigation software with star finder, vetor chart and GPS interface. [Commercial, demo available. Windows]

links.title: Jovian Satellite Simulator
links.description: JupSat95 calculates and displays the positions of Jupiter's four Galilean moons. [Shareware Win9x/NT]

links.title: EasySky
links.description: Planetarium with orrery, and animation. Commercial, demo available - Win95/98/Me/NT/2000/XP.

links.title: Hallo Northern Sky
links.description: Planetarium program which includes the Tycho-2 and SAC 7.2 catalogues. Can access the GSC CD-ROMs. [Freeware - Win95/98/NT/XP]

links.title: Starry Night
links.description: Planetarium program which lets you view the sky from anywhere in the universe. [Commercial - Windows XP/Vista, Mac OSX]

links.title: Bubba's Bits
links.description: Offers the picoSky cellular telephone planetarium application which runs on most phones that allow Java game downloads.

links.title: Dutch Occultation Association
links.description: Free version of Lunar Occultation Workbench ( LOW ).

links.title: Project Pluto
links.description: Desktop planetarium and charting program. [Commercial - Dos, Win3.1/95/NT]

links.title: Stellarium
links.description: Shows a realistic sky in 3D, as with the naked eye, binoculars or a telescope, including fisheye projection for domes. [Free open source (GPL) - Windows, Mac, Linux]

links.title: Perseus Astronomy Simulation Software
links.description: Perseus is a complete desktop planetarium. Software features 3D solar system objects and scripting function for lecturers, plus ASCOM support. Italian and English versions are available.

links.title: Alcyone Ephemeris
links.description: Astronomical ephemeris calculator covering the period 3000 BC to AD 3000. Includes star charts, graphs and orbit diagrams.

links.title: GeoAstro Applet Collection
links.description: Interactive Java applets display the position, daily and annual path of the sun and the moon, for any time and location. [Online - not available for any PC platforms]

links.title: Astro-Mania
links.description: Eight interactive levels covering various aspects of the universe. [Commercial - Windows]

links.title: Project CLEA
links.description: Provides laboratory exercises that illustrate modern astronomical techniques using digital data and color images. They are suitable for high-school and college classes at all levels. Each CLEA laboratory exercise includes a dedicated computer program, a student manual, and a technical guide for the instructor. [Freeware - Windows, Macintosh]

links.title: Starry Night Education
links.description: Interactive astronomy curriculum to help teachers inspire and engage astronomy and space science students across all levels of knowledge and ability.

links.title: ESO-MIDAS: Image Data Analysis System
links.description: [open source - Linux/Unix, VAX/VMS/OpenVMS] General tools for image processing and data reduction with emphasis on astronomical applications including stellar and surface photometry, image sharpening and decomposition, as well as imaging and special reduction packages for ESO instrumentation.

links.title: Diffraction Limited
links.description: Image processing and CCD camera control software for astronomical imaging. Supports Apogee, Celestron, FLI, HiSIS, Meade, SBIG, and Starlight Xpress CCD cameras; video cameras, autoguiders, and filter wheels. ASCOM compliant.

links.title: Auriga Imaging
links.description: Auriga Imaging's program RegiStar automatically registers (aligns) astrophotos -- no user intervention required.

links.title: ISDA - Irregularly Spaced Data Analysis
links.description: [Free - MSDOS, dosemu] Program to analyse irregularly spaced time series -  variable star light curves.

links.title: Picture Window Image Editing Software
links.description: Picture Window is a popular tool among serious amateur astrophotographers. By Digital Light and Color.

links.title: Voyager Image Display
links.description: A  shareware Windows 95/98/NT/2000 based image processing program that can read and enhance images from various NASA spacecraft.

links.title: AstroArt
links.description: [commercial, demo available - Win95/98/NT] A complete software product for analysis and processing of astronomical images. With the built-in star atlas based on the Guide Star Catalogue, it is also  possible to perform astrometric and photometric calibration on your images.

links.title: Pleiades Astrophotro: PixInsight
links.description: Modular, open-architecture, portable image processing software platform specializing in technical image processing tasks such as astronomical imaging. It is available for Linux/UNIX, Mac OSX and MS Windows.

links.title: The Imaging Source
links.description: Offers IC Capture.AS, control and acquisition software for astronomy cameras. Capture single frames and uncompressed image sequences.

links.title: IRIS
links.description: Free astronomical images processing software.

links.title: FITS Image Viewers
links.description: [free/open source - Windows, Macintosh, Unix] Download FITS viewers for various platforms.

links.title: FITS archive at NRAO
links.description: This is an archive for the Flexible Image Transport System [FITS], the standard data interchange and archival format of the worldwide astronomy community.

links.title: Flexible Image Transport System (FITS) Support Office
links.description: The format adopted by the astronomical community for data interchange and  archival storage. Responsible for documenting the FITS standard, participating in its evolution, and advising NASA astrophysics missions on how to present their data in this type of format.

links.title: IAU FITS Working Group
links.description: International control authority for FITS [Flexible Image Transport System].

links.title: Solar Kingdom
links.description: [commercial, demo available - Win95/98/NT] A solar system simulator and planetarium, with planetary encyclopaedia.

links.title: Solar System Applet
links.description: [online Java applet] This 3-d solar system applet can be rotated and zoomed with the mouse.  Below it are links to other online gravity simulators and resources for building solar system simulations.

links.title: Starry Night
links.description: [commercial - Win95/98/NT, Macintosh] A planetarium and solar-system simulator; lets you view the universe from anywhere in our planetary neighbourhood in the past, present, and future.

links.title: GrandTour
links.description: Accurate wireframe simulator for the Voyager and Giotto space missions, with animation capability. Developed at JPL for science/navigation, and filmed by the BBC/NOVA. Conveniently runs from any Windows/DOS. Freeware.

links.title: Spacesimulator.net
links.description: Provides tutorials on how to program a 3d engine for a space simulation.

links.title: AstroFly
links.description: [freeware - Win 98/ME/2000/XP] Three-dimensional models of the Milky Way neighborhood.

links.title: Gravity Simulator
links.description: [freeware - Win 9x/NT/2k/XP] Simulates orbits of planets and other celestial bodies.

links.title: ChView
links.description: [Freeware - Win3.x/95] A three-dimensional aid to viewing some of the nearer stars of our galaxy, navigating the distances between them, and accessing basic stellar information.

links.title: 3D Solar System Simulator
links.description: A free Java application that shows an interactive 3D representation of the planets and satellites of the solar system.

links.title: Universe Sandbox
links.description: Interactive space simulator created by Dan Dixon. It includes the solar system, the nearest 1000 stars, the local group of galaxies and an unlimited number of fictional scenarios.

links.title: MPL3D Solar System
links.description: Interactive 3D space simulation of the close universe in real time.

links.title: The Celestia Motherlode
links.description: The addon repository for the 3-D space simulator Celestia. It includes tours, spacecraft, asteroids and fictional universes.

links.title: AstroGrav
links.description: A precision solar system simulator that calculates the gravitational interactions between all astronomical bodies, so that the motions of asteroids and comets are accurately simulated. Superb interactive 3D views, and a huge range of features. [Commercial, free demo, multilingual]

links.title: Copernic Space Simulator
links.description: A freeware program that allows the user to navigate through the solar system neighbourhood at different times in past or future and see the sky in a stereographic projection.

links.title: Orbiter Space Flight Simulator
links.description: ORBITER is a free flight simulator that goes beyond the confines of Earth's atmosphere. It is not a space shooter, and aims to be as realistic as possible.

links.title: Deepsky 99 - Software for Observers
links.description: [shareware - Win95/98/NT] Deepsky 99 solves an important need for amateur and professional observers. The software allows the user to  plan a productive observing session and record what was  observed quickly and easily.

links.title: JPL Planetary and Lunar Ephemerides
links.description: [commercial - multiplatform] This CD contains three Jet Propulsion Laboratory Planetary and Lunar Ephemerides along with a toolbox of FORTRAN subroutines that allow the user to obtain the coordinates of the Sun, Moon, and nine major planets.

links.title: Multiyear Interactive Computer Almanac

links.title: GeoAstro Applet Collection
links.description: [commercial and freeware - multiplatform] Interactive Java applets display the position, daily and annual path of the sun and the moon, for any time and location.

links.title: Starchart - Star mapping software
links.description: [opensource - POSIX] There is a sky. There are things in the sky. This program draws maps of things in the sky.

links.title: Moon Tool
links.description: [Windows] A desktop application that displays the times of the various phases of the moon and a picture of the current phase of the moon.

links.title: Epoch_2000 Temporal Epoch Calculator
links.description: Excel spreadsheet calculates temporal variation in astronomic constants, obliquity of the ecliptic, and illumination angles at any specified latitude. You need only input a date or the latitude.

links.title: Automated Variable Star Observing
links.description: [freeware - Linux] Command-line program to automate reduction of variable star CCD images.

links.title: Deep-Sky Planner
links.description: Astronomical observation planning, logging, reporting, and telescope control software for imagers and visual observers.

812461.title: Solar System

Sites discussing whether Pluto should be properly considered a planet, a Kuiper Belt object, or some other form of Trans-Neptunian Object (TNO).

810883.title: Biomolecules
810883.description:
This category classifies sites according to the molecules of primary interest. These molecules differ from Organic Chemicals in that they were discovered from their synthesis within living cells. Originally these would be extracted from plants or animals. Many biomolecules can now be produced synthetically from simple chemicals; sugars, amino acids, steroids or drugs that mimic their effects.

More often the term biomolecule, applies to macromolecules which are polymers of
sugars: oligosaccharides
amino acids: peptides and proteins
nucleotides: oligonucleotides, DNA and RNA
Sites primarily covering translocation of DNA and translation of RNA, may be found in Gene_Expression
For sites on the role of cyclic nucleotides and phosphoinositols in their biochemical role, see Signal_Transduction

810884.description:
This category deals with cytobiology;
protein interactions at the cellular level, such as cytoplasm or organelles
in contrast to those at the nuclear level,
which are dealt with in Gene Expression.
The established pathways, also known as Enzymology, are currently dealt with in the Metabolism category
However, structural aspects are included in Proteins and Enzymes: Structure.
where there are also links about the enzymes of transcription and translocation.
Whereas intracellular events related to cytoplasm are contained in this category,
intercellular events effecting membrane, signaling mechanisms and second messengers,
should be found in Cell_Biology,
or perhaps Developmental_Biology.
Biochemical events between organs should be found in Physiology,
or perhaps Endocrinology.

810878.title: Retroviral
810878.description: Retrovirus contain RNS strings carrying their genetic code and reverse transcriptase, an enzyme that allows the code of the RNA to be translated to DNA in the cell cytoplasm. The DNA strings are transported into the cell nucleus and inserted in the cellular DNA to form part of the cellular gene set-up. The normal cellular mechanisms and components are used to replicate the viral genes, convert them to RNA strings, synthetize the other components required by the intact virus and to set the virus free. The reverse transcription of the RNA string by reverse transcriptase is thus the first step in retroviral gene expression.
