links.description: Understand Biology helps everyone to clearly grasp the essence of concepts in biology

links.title: Biology, Geography and Health
links.description: Provides 36+ million biology, geography and health sciences articles from the beginning of the 18th century.

links.title: Europe PMC
links.description: Provides comprehensive access to life sciences literature from trusted sources.

811201.title: Research Funding
811201.description: This category is for organizations that provide grants and funds for research in biology.

links.title: BBSRC: Building The Economy
links.description: The Biotechnology and Biological Sciences Research Council in the UK offers grants, studentships, awards, bursaries and funding opportunities.

811129.title: Research Groups and Centers
811129.description: Most research activities will either occur in academic departments or in research institutes (which may either be in universities or external). Both of these are included in this category.

links.title: The Salk Institute for Biological Studies
links.description: The Salk Institute is a private, non-profit, research organization dedicated to fundamental research in biology and its relation to health, studying such challenging problems as the organization and operation of the brain, the control of gene activity, and the molecular origins of cancer, AIDS, and other diseases.

links.title: Howard Hughes Medical Institute
links.description: Biomedical research, grants. HHMI investigators              contributed to the discovery of genes related to diseases such as cystic fibrosis and obesity, and to basic understanding of cell development and communication.       Scientists are employed by HHMI and conduct their work at HHMI facilities at leading research institutions nationwide. Web site has extensive news and information on recent research findings.

links.title: Institute of Systematics and Evolution of Animals.
links.description: The main task of the Institute are researches devoted to different aspects of animal systematics, paleontology, faunistics, and cytology. All scientific projects carried out in the Institute's departments are focused on three main disciplines: zoology of vertebrates, zoology of invertebrates and experimental zoology.

links.title: Whitehead Institute for Biomedical Research
links.description: The Whitehead Institute is a non-profit, independent basic research and teaching institution recognized worldwide for pathfinding programs in cancer and AIDS research, developmental biology, structural biology, infectious disease, and genetics.

links.title: Stowers Institute for Medical Research
links.description: conducts basic biomedical research into complex genetic systems to unlock the mysteries of disease and find the key to their causes, treatment and prevention.

links.title: Institut Curie
links.description: The main research activities - ranging from the physical chemistry of organized molecular complexes to basic biological  research and cancer genetics - are conducted in the Research Division of the Curie Institute.    This basic research is targeted to the development new diagnostic methods and cancer treatments.

links.title: NCBI Coffee Break
links.description: Interactive articles that show how the application of bioinfomatics tools from the NCBI contribute to scientific discoveries.

links.title: Muka Head Research Station
links.description: The research arm of Malaysian Science University, studying tropical marine and coastal science.  Current projects include studies of clams, oysters, and marine biodiversity.

links.title: Kewalo Marine Laboratory
links.description: Includes access to the Marine Invertebrate Reproduction Database as well as information about sponsored research, events, and scientists.

links.title: Samuel Roberts Noble Foundation
links.description: Information and links to research, grants, and extension activities in agriculture, forage biotechnology, and plant biology.

links.title: Woods Hole Marine Biological Laboratory
links.description: Information about the programs and resources available at the laboratory, including publications, databases, specimens, grants, and library services.

links.title: University of Michigan Life Sciences Initiative
links.description: Information on the Life Sciences Institute, the Life Sciences Corridor, the Life Sciences Values and Society program, and educational programs and events.

links.title: Michael Rosbash's Laboratory Website
links.description: Includes a list of lab personnel and alumni, research objectives, publications, and contact information.  Research focuses on RNA splicing, nuclear export and the study of mechanisms affecting circadian rhythms.

links.title: Stazione Zoologica Anton Dohrn
links.description: Research center in Naples, Italy. Includes descriptions of current research projects.

links.title: Institute for Medical Physics and Biophysics University of Leipzig
links.description: Homepage of the Institute for Medical Physics and Biophysics University of Leipzig: staff, research, publications, scientific events, teaching and history.

links.title: CIRAD
links.description: Information about the agricultural, veterinary, forestry, and food sciences research, carried out by the French scientific organization based at research centers around the world.  In French and English.

links.title: National Academy of Sciences (U.S.) Division on Earth and Life Sciences
links.description: Advancing the life sciences and applying science to analysis and alleviation national problems. Site has information on and reports from NAS boards on Biology, Environmental Studies and Toxicology, and Radiation Effects Research, and the Institute for Laboratory Animal Research.

links.title: Vascular Biology Laboratory
links.description: Information on research on stimulating angiogenesis to reduce hypertension.  Includes publication list, newsletter and resource links.

links.title: National Centre for Biological Sciences
links.description: Part of the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research and located in Bangalore. Carries out basic research in the frontier areas of biology and trains to Ph.D. level.

links.title: Algae Research Laboratory, University of Malaya
links.description: Prof. Phang Siew Moi's lab is the premier algal research initiative in Malaysia. Provides details of the laboratory, research programs and publications.

links.title: Cold Spring Harbor Laboratory
links.description: Research in cancer biology, plant genetics, genomics and bioinformatics, and neurobiology.

links.title: Friedrich Miescher Institute
links.description: Research institute in Basel undertaking fundamental biomedical research, employing new technologies to explore basic molecular mechanisms of cells and organisms in health and disease.

links.title: Center for Integrative Biology
links.description: CIBIO, at the University of Trento, Italy, aims to merge classical cellular and molecular biology approaches with systems and synthetic biology. Provides details of the research activities in its core laboratories and the research network.

links.title: University of Belgrade Institute for Biological Research
links.description: Information about the institute's activities, research, and staff.  In English and Serbian.

811183.title: Search Engines
811183.description: This category lists engines which search databases of life science information and literature.

links.title: VADLO
links.description: Biology and medical search engine and biology research cartoons.

810811.title: Sociobiology
810811.description: Sociobiology is an area of study combining biology and sociology that attempts to explain social behavior in all species by considering the evolutionary advantages the behaviors may have.

links.title: Behavioural Ecology Research Group, Oxford
links.description: Research group studying animal learning, memory, and decision-making, using experimental psychology and evolutionary biology as tools.  Department of Zoology, University of Oxford.

links.title: Sociobiology
links.description: Explains major concepts of Sociobiology, including Ethology, Evolution, Attraction, Sexual Dimorphism, Imprinting, Kin Selection, Reciprocal Altruism, and Dominance Hierarchies. Contrasts the roles of Sociobiology and Culture.

links.title: Archive site for Kenan Malik
links.description: Essays, papers, lectures and reviews on Darwinism, evolutionary psychology, race, philosophy and history.  Also extracts from Kenan Malik's books 'Man, Beast and Zombie' and 'What is it to be Human?'.

links.title: Demonic Males: Apes and the Origins of Human Violence
links.description: Chapter one of the book by Richard Wrangham and Dale Petersen.

links.title: Digit Ratio: A Pointer to Fertility, Behavior and Health by John T. Manning
links.description: Michael Mills examines the claim that digit ratio allows us infer whether an individual is likely to have homosexual inclinations, be highly fertile, may eventually suffer from a heart attack or breast cancer, have musical aptitude or sporting prowess, and a surprisingly long list of other characteristics.

links.title: Great Ideas in Personality - Evolutionary Psychology and Sociobiology
links.description: Includes links to research papers, web sites, and other reference sources.

links.title: Against Sociobiology
links.description: Tom Bethell speculates on what future generations will make of the controversy surrounding human sociobiology.

links.title: Survival of the Surliest
links.description: Article from Guardian Unlimited on a supposed argument between Gouldians and Dawkinsians.

810812.title: Memetics
810812.description: Memetics is a neo-Darwinian approach to evolutionary models of cultural information transfer based on the concept of the meme, which can be defined as any unit of cultural information, such as a practice or idea, that is transmitted verbally or by repeated action from one mind to another.

links.title: Memetics
links.description: A meme is a cognitive or behavioral pattern that can be transmitted from one individual to another one. References, links.

links.title: Memetics UK
links.description: Includes texts by Dr Susan Blackmore and links to other articles online.

links.title: Structure of Memes
links.description: The main criticism that can be raised against the memetic approach is that memes are difficult to define. What are the elements or units that make up a meme? Does a meme correspond to a complete symphony, or to a symphonic movement, a melody, a musical phrase, or even a single note?

links.title: Meme Central
links.description: FAQ, links, and a bookstore. (By Richard Brodie, author of the popular book on memetics, "Virus of the Mind".)

links.title: Anders Transhuman Pages: Memetics
links.description: Collection of links and essays about memes: ideas and concepts viewed as living organisms. Includes sections on memetic theory, examples and applications, controversial issues, a lexicon and a brief bibliography.

links.title: Colorless Green Homunculi by William L. Benzon
links.description: Essay/review of The Electric Meme: A New Theory of How We Think.

links.title: Memes and Tremes - Susan Blackmore
links.description: A detailed site maintained by the psychologist and memeticist Susan Blackmore.

links.title: Chapter 11 from Richard Dawkins, "The Selfish Gene''
links.description: The text that started off the science of memetics.

links.title: Memetics
links.description: A senior thesis on memetic selection criteria.

links.title: The Church of Virus
links.description: Virus is a collection of mutually-supporting ideas (a meme-complex) encompassing philosophy,  science, technology, politics, and religion.

links.title: Memetics
links.description: Information from Wikipedia on this neo-Darwinian approach to evolutionary models of cultural information transfer based on the concept of the meme.

links.title: Memes to be Discussed
links.description: Blog discussing what memes are, what can we do with them, who controls who, what drives them and are memes real?

810813.title: Wilson, Edward O.
810813.description: Entomologist considered to be the father of sociobiology. Wilson has elucidated much about human behavior from his studies of ants.

links.title: Edward O. Wilson
links.description: An interview with the author of 'Sociobiology'.

links.title: From a Key Observer of Life: A Plea to Save Biodiversity
links.description: Edward O. Wilson talks with the Christian Science Monitor on topics revolving around his new book "The Future of Life".

links.title: SaveAmericanForests.com: Wilson Presentation
links.description: Presentation slide show on the effects of deforestation.

links.title: Look!
links.description: Jerry Fodor reviews 'Consilience' by E. O. Wilson.

links.title: E. O. Wilson
links.description: The Guardian profiles "Darwin's natural heir" Edward O. Wilson.

811187.title: Software
811187.description: This category is for sites about software aimed primarily at research, evaluation or education in biology. Many branches of Biology have their own category for software which can be reached through the appropriate link.    Please submit general-purpose LIMS to the Lab_Computers_and_Software category.    Please submit software focused on *clinical* biology to its appropriate category in health or medicine.

links.title: Flocker 1.1
links.description: This free software quantifies and compares statistical measures of group size. It differentiates between outsiders' view (group size) versus insiders' view (crowding) measures, controls for the ties among data points in the latter case and handles biased distributions correctly.

links.title: Biosoft
links.description: Programs for data analysis, graphics, and statistics. [Windows]

links.title: VassarStats
links.description: Online software from Vassar College for calculating probability, linear correlation and regression, chi-square, t-procedures, and ANOVA. [Web-based]

links.title: Stat-Ease, Inc.
links.description: Statistical software, training, and consulting on Design of Experiments for scientists and engineers. [Windows]

links.title: LemnaTec
links.description: Image processing software for biotests (Lemna, Bonit, Daphnia). Distributor for various software firms.

links.title: FEI:  Amira 3D
links.description: Software platform for visualizing, manipulating and understanding life science and bio-medical data coming from all types of sources and modalities. [Windows/Linux/Mac]

links.title: SimBiotic Software
links.description: Provides a range of interactive software for biology education including virtual labs which simulate real life experiments. [Windows/Mac]

links.title: MetaSystems
links.description: Manufacturer of automatic microscopy imaging systems for research and routine labs.

links.title: BioVis3D
links.description: Software for reconstructing 3D models from histological serial sections. [Windows]

links.title: Ruro, Inc
links.description: Software for research, biotechnology, pharmacology, and healthcare laboratories. [Web-based]

links.title: Biospecimen Inventory System
links.description: BSI-II is customizable specimen inventory management software. [Windows]

links.title: DNA Dragon
links.description: Sequence assembly and editing software for DNA sequences which also processes trace data and next generation sequencing data. [Windows]

links.title: Serf Software Suite
links.description: Offers software for immunocytochemistry micrograph analysis, electrophysiology analysis, and genetic data clustering. [Windows]

links.title: HVS Image
links.description: Animal tracking software and related accessories for use with the Morris Water Maze and the Barnes Maze. [Windows]

links.title: Buritrack
links.description: Open-source drosophila behavior analysis and tracking software for use with Buridan's Paradigm. [Windows/Mac]

links.title: SimThyr
links.description: Simulator of thyrotropic feedback control for thyroid homeostasis. [Mac/Windows/Linux]

links.title: HemocyTap
links.description: App for manually counting cells using a hemocytometer in culture labs. [iPhone]

links.title: EPath3D
links.description: Online package for the diagramming of signaling pathways in biological systems. [Web-based]

links.title: Morpheus
links.description: Modeling and simulation environment for multi-scale and multi-cellular systems. [Windows/Mac/Linux]

805148.title: Taxonomy
805148.description: Taxonomy is the practice and science of classification. This category is for sites about the taxonomy of living and extinct organisms. It includes classical Linnaean taxonomy and phylogenetic taxonomy or cladism, which groups taxa using derived traits.

links.title: DELTA: Description Language for Taxonomy
links.description: A flexible format for encoding taxonomic descriptions for computer processing. It can be used to produce natural-language descriptions, conventional or interactive keys, classifications, and information-retrieval systems.

links.title: Tree of Life
links.description: A project containing information about the diversity of organisms on Earth, their history, and characteristics. The information is linked together in the form of the evolutionary tree that connects all organisms to each other.

links.title: Integrated Taxonomic Information System
links.description: Authoritative taxonomic information on plants, animals, fungi, and microbes of North America and the world.

links.title: Biomedical Ontology
links.description: About two dozen links collected by the Ontology Project at the philosophy department of State University of New York at Buffalo.

links.title: Taxonomy
links.description: Information from Wikipedia on the practice and science of classification, the arrangement of organisms in a hierarchical structure.

links.title: NCBI Taxonomy Homepage
links.description: Provides a taxonomy browser, taxonomy resources and other information.

links.title: American Society of Plant Taxonomists
links.description: Promotes research and teaching in the taxonomy, systematics, and phylogeny of vascular and nonvascular plants.

805149.title: Cladistics
805149.description: Cladistics involves the reconstruction of evolutionary phylogenies by analyzing the development, retention, and loss of morphological features from ancestor taxa to their descendants.

links.title: Introduction to Cladistics
links.description: Cladistics is a particular method of hypothesizing relationships among organisms based on the idea that members of a group share a common evolutionary history.

links.title: Willi Hennig Society
links.description: Society of scientists studying cladistics.

805150.title: Publications
805150.description: This category is for any website about publications dealing with the science of cladistics.

805151.title: Journals
805151.description: This category is for websites dealing with professional journals publishing papers on the subject of cladistics.

links.title: Cladistics
links.description: Published on behalf of the Willi Henning Society. The journal covers theory, method, the philosophical aspects of systematics, and the role of systematic and evolutionary studies in the investigation of biogeographical and other general biological phenomena.

links.title: PHYLIP
links.description: Joe Felsenstein's suite of programs implementing perhaps the widest range of phylogenetic inference package. The most widely distributed phylogeny software. Includes distance, likelihood and parsimony methods for a wide range of different types of data, and runs on most platforms.

links.title: Tree Puzzle
links.description: Computer program to reconstruct phylogenetic trees from molecular sequence data by maximum likelihood.

links.title: NONA - A Quick Guide to the Commands
links.description: A brief overview of using NONA for phylogenetic analysis.

links.title: Phylo-Win
links.description: Graphical color interface for molecular phylogenetic inference. It performs neighbor-joining, parsimony, and maximum likelihood methods and bootstrap with any of them.

links.title: PAML
links.description: Phylogenetic analyses of DNA or protein sequences using maximum likelihood.

links.title: MrBayes
links.description: Open source software for estimation of phylogenies using Bayesian inference.

links.title: MACAW
links.description: Multiple sequence alignments, for both Windows (3.1, NT on Intel and Alpha chips) and Macintosh. Based on pattern-matching algorithms that attempt to identify blocks of local alignment similarity, rather than on the common Needleman and Wunsch global alignment algorithm.

links.title: MacroCAIC
links.description: MacroCAIC is a CAIC derivative for testing correlates of species richness using comparative tests.

links.title: CAIC
links.description: Comparative Analysis via Independent Constrasts. Software for Macintosh implementing  the independent constrasts method for phylogenetically correct comparative methods.

links.title: Joe Felsenstein's list of phylogeny programs
links.description: Probably the most comprehensive

links.title: Genetics Software from the Slatkin Lab
links.description: Links to sites for downloading phylogenetic software.

links.title: PaleoTax
links.description: The program can give an overview of taxonomic and other information of a taxa group. Recorded data can be assessed or exported as RTF or HTML document.

links.title: PICKEY
links.description: An interactive multi-entry polychotomous key for identification of organisms by intensive use of images.

links.title: Lucid
links.description: A system for creating, maintaining, distributing and playing interactive identification keys.

links.title: Meka
links.description: An interactive Multiple-Entry Key Algorithm to enable rapid identification of biological specimens.

811206.title: Theoretical Biology
811206.description: Theoretical biology attempts to explain the biological world using mainly mathematical and computational tools. Though ultimately based on observations and experimental results, the theoretical biologist's product is a model or theory.

links.title: Honig Lab at Columbia University
links.description: Research combines computational biophysics and bioinformatics to aid in understanding the structural, physical, and chemical basis of a wide range of biological phenomena, with a focus on protein structure and function. Includes publications list and information on software developed by the group.

links.title: Theoretical Biology at Utrecht University, Netherlands
links.description: Formal models in ecology, spatial pattern formation, (molecular) evolution, immunology, and ethology.  Formalisms range from mathematical models, cellular  automata, genetic algorithms, to discrete-event individual-oriented simulation models.  Bioinformatic approach typically involves spatial, multi-leveled models with many interacting entities whose behavior is determined by local information.

links.title: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam
links.description: Department of Theoretical Biology.  A do-it-yourself online course in 'methods in theoretical biology' and yearly organised online courses on the Dynamic Energy Budget (DEB) theory of the development and growth of organisms.

links.title: Theoretical Biology Groningen
links.description: Focuses on competition and natural selection, more specifically evolutionary game theory, life history theory, sexual selection, sex allocation, metapopulation genetics, resource competition, and interference competition.

links.title: University of Vienna
links.description: Department of Theoretical Biology.  Staff, research projects and resources.

links.title: Theory of Asynchronous Evolution
links.description: Vigen A. Geodakian puts forward his theory which contradicts  Darwin’s theory of sexual selection and explains and predicts sexual dimorphism.

links.title: Dr. Till Bretschneider
links.description: Homepage of Dr. Bretschneider, researcher in the field of theoretical biology. It includes research activities and publications.

links.title: Navier-Stalks
links.description: Exploring the wonderful world of systems biology research through the eyes of an outsider.

links.title: VackvSuG
links.description: Blog for researchers interested in systems biology domains and system factors and mechanisms and in particular, bioinformatic annotation.

links.title: Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology: Princeton University
links.description: Carries out research in a range of areas including molecular evolution, behavioural ecology, the dynamics of communities and populations, and conservation biology. Includes details of graduate and undergraduate programs.

links.title: Immunoligical Identification of Gut Pathogens and Commensals
links.description: Article discussing how the lining of the gut distinguishes harmful from beneficial gut microbes in a nonmolecular way by detecting how they interact with the epithelium.

811208.title: Associations
811208.description: This category is for societies and professional bodies which do not themselves conduct scientific research but which promote and support theoretical and mathematical biology. They organize meetings, publish journals and provide research grants for scientists in this field.

links.title: Netherlands Society for Theoretical Biology
links.description: Information about the NVTB; abstracts of annual NVTB meetings; many theoretical biology links; conference calendar; journal finder.

811207.title: Journals
811207.description: Journals and Publications devoted to, or largely concerned with, theoretical biology.

links.title: Journal of Theoretical Biology
links.description: This journal is the leading forum for theoretical papers that give insight into biological processes. It covers a very wide range of topics and is of interest to biologists in many areas of research.

links.title: Acta Biotheoretica
links.description: International journal on the mathematical and philosophical foundations of biological and biomedical science. Papers cover a range of biological theories including the philosophy of biology, biomathematics, computational biology, genetics, ecology and morphology.

links.title: Theoretical Population Biology
links.description: This journal presents articles on the theoretical aspects of the biology of  populations, particularly in the areas of ecology, genetics, demography, and epidemiology.

811143.title: Toxicology
811143.description: Toxicology is the study of the adverse effects of chemicals on living organisms. A poison is defined as any substance that causes a harmful effect, either by accident or design, when administered to a living organism.

811156.title: Associations
811156.description: This category is for organizations which do not themselves conduct scientific research but aim to spread information about such research. They organize meetings, publish journals and provide research grants for scientists in the field.

links.title: Society of Toxicology
links.description: Professional organization of scientists from academic institutions, government, and industry representing toxicologists. Includes public outreach, members services, meetings and contacts in Reston, Virginia.

links.title: California Association of Toxicologists
links.description: Professional and educational association of forensic and clinical toxicologists, with quarter proceedings. Includes literature review, meetings, employment opportunities, related links and contacts for offices throughout the USA.

links.title: Eurotox
links.description: Association of European Toxicologists and European Societies of Toxicology. Aims to foster toxicology, both scientifically and educationally in all countries of Europe.

links.title: International Society on Toxinology
links.description: Advance knowledge of the properties of toxins and antitoxins and to bring together scholars interested in these substances through a common society.

links.title: Society of Forensic Toxicologists
links.description: An organization composed of practicing forensic toxicologists and those interested in the discipline for the purpose of promoting and developing forensic toxicology.

links.title: Society of Toxicologic Pathologists
links.description: Non-profit association of pathologists for advancement of pathology as it pertains to changes elicited by pharmacological, chemical and environmental agents.

links.title: American College of Medical Toxicology
links.description: ACMT is a professional, nonprofit association of physicians with recognized expertise in medical toxicology.

links.title: European Society of Toxicologic Pathology
links.description: ESTP organization, activities, meeting, openings, details of membership, their journal  Experimental and Toxicologic Pathology. Includes member login.

links.title: British Toxicology Society
links.description: International forum to foster research relating to chemical effects on the environment, and protecting public health. Details of register of toxicologists, training programs, meetings, abstract submission, membership and secretariat in Macclesfield, England.

links.title: British Society of Toxicological Pathologists
links.description: Forum for changes in pathology, elicited by pharmacological, chemical and environmental agents. Includes calendar of meetings, job vacancies, related links, details of membership and educational modules held at the University, Cambridge, England.

links.title: Society of Toxicology of Canada
links.description: Promoting acquisition, dissemination, study and use of toxicological data. Includes links to training, meetings, job openings, membership and committee details, with contacts in Beaconsfield, Québec. [English and French]

links.title: International Society of Regulatory Toxicology and Pharmacology
links.description: ISRTP provides a public forum for policy makers and scientists promoting toxicologic and pharmacologic sciences, for regulation affecting human safety, health and the environment. Includes events, membership details, member login and contacts for officers throughout the USA.

links.title: NORMAN
links.description: EU-funded project building a network of reference laboratories, research centers and related organisations to monitor emerging environmental pollutants. Includes substance databases, details of quality activities, workshops and events, with contacts for newsletter and member countries.

links.title: European Centre for Ecotoxicology and Toxicology of Chemicals
links.description: ECETOC provides a scientific forum for manufacturers and users to identify, evaluate and help the industry to minimise any potentially adverse effects on human health and the environment that may arise from the manufacture and use of chemicals.

links.title: Society for Toxicologic Pathology in India
links.description: Provides information on the objectives of the Society, membership, the newsletter and conferences.

links.title: International Dose-Response Society
links.description: Provides information on the Society, its membership, the newsletter, the online journal and the annual conference.

links.title: Mutagenesis and Experimental Pathology Society of Australasia
links.description: MEPSA aims to bring together people interested in all aspects of experimental pathology including environmental mutagenesis, to promote scientific discussion and exchange and the advancement of knowledge.

links.title: EC:  Reference Laboratory for Alternatives to Animal Testing
links.description: EURL-ECVAM validates, accepts and recommends deletions for regulatory acceptance of pharmaceuticals, and related products. Includes new submission of tests for phototoxicity, skin corrosivity, inhibition of toxin binding for tetanus vaccines, embryotoxicity assays, using embryonic stem cell, and growth in cell cultures.

811147.title: Organizations
811147.description: Organized body of people aimed at the advancement of knowledge, exchange of information or group activities in the field of toxicology.

links.title: International Union of Toxicology
links.description: Aims to foster cooperation among toxicologists and promote global acquisition, dissemination and utilization of knowledge in the world of science of toxicology.

links.title: Toxicology Excellence for Risk Assessment
links.description: Non-profit corporation dedicated to the best use of toxicity data for risk assessment. Includes toxicity data, information on risk methodologies, and contacts in Cincinnati, Ohio, USA.

links.title: Reactive Surfaces Ltd.
links.description: Developing enzyme-based additives for paint to detoxify neurotoxins, including nerve agents and pesticides. Research at Austin, Texas, with corporate headquarters in Washington, DC.

811154.title: Consultants
811154.description: Sites for businesses or individuals who offer expertise in the field of Toxicology, toxins and their pharmacology, but do not themselves provide facilities for analysis or research.

links.title: Daniel L. Sudakin, MD, MPH
links.description: Medical toxicologist with experience in occupational, environmental, and pharmaceutical fields.  Introduction to mycotoxins, publications, and services available from Corvallis, Oregon.

links.title: Gad Consulting Services
links.description: International practice serving the pharmaceutical, medical device and consumer product industries. Based in Cary, North Carolina.

links.title: Lauterbach and Lupcho Consulting Services

links.title: Intox Pvt. Ltd.: Institute for Toxicological Studies
links.description: CRO offering toxicological studies on drugs, agrochemicals, biological, according to national and international guidelines. Includes mutagenicity testing, details of in-vivo species, including ecotoxicity models, and contacts in Pune and Mumbia, India.

links.title: MB Research Laboratories

links.title: Bio-Test Labor GmbH.

Overview includes list of publications from Sagerheide, Germany.

links.title: Cyprotex
links.description: Contract research organization focused on in vitro toxicity screening of potential drug candidates and chemicals, based near Macclesfield, England.

links.title: Envigo

811153.title: Reagents and Kits
811153.description: Sites which list and describe chemicals or biological products available for immediate purchase, which are designed and packaged to assay, analyze, or aid research to determine the toxicity of a product or identify toxins.

links.title: Molecular Toxicology Inc
links.description: Manufacturer of media and metabolic activation products for in vitro research and product testing to GMP. Includes contacts for Asian and European distributors, and facilities in Boone, North Carolina.

links.title: Latoxan
links.description: Company specializing in the production of venoms and toxins for research and industry. Lists alkaloids, ion channel and receptor ligands and toxins, worldwide distributors and their laboratories in Valence, France.

811152.title: Testing Services
811152.description: Sites for companies or individual analytical laboratories that have established procedures in place to perform tests on submitted samples, to identify, assay, analyze, or aid research in toxins and toxicity measurement.

links.title: Rocky Mountain Laboratories
links.description: Offers GLP characterization of proteins, peptides, drugs and their metabolites, using FT/IR, GC-MS and LC-MS/MS, for pharmaceutical and forensic applications. Includes tests performed, certification and contacts in Fort Collins, Colorado.

links.title: Environmental Enterprises USA, Inc.
links.description: Consulting and aquatic toxicity biomonitoring for NPDES  permits, offering sample pick up and kit delivery service  across the Gulf Coast from Mobile to Cameron, based in Slidell, Louisiana.

links.title: Marinco Bioassay Laboratory, Inc.
links.description: Performs aquatic toxicity bioassays for NPDES water quality monitoring permits in Sarasota, Florida.

links.title: BioDetection Systems BV.
links.description: Offer in vitro assays for analysis of dioxins, PCBs, estrogens, POPs in food, environmental and other samples, as licensing of technology or contract analytical work in Amsterdam, The Netherlands.

links.title: Institute for In Vitro Sciences Inc.

links.title: New England Bioassay

links.title: Randox Testing Services

links.title: Journal of Pharmacological and Toxicological Methods

links.title: Regulatory Toxicology and Pharmacology

811146.title: Research Groups and Centers
811146.description: Most research activities will either occur in academic departments or in research institutes (which may either be in universities or external). Both of these are included in this category.

links.description: Graduate intake, areas of emphasis; neurotoxicology, immunotoxicology, osteotoxicology, carcinogenesis, and molecular, pulmonary, reproductive and developmental toxicology. Details of faculty at the University of Rochester Medical Center, New York.

links.title: Industrial Toxicology Research Centre

links.title: Research Institute of Hygiene, Toxicology and Occupational Pathology
links.description: Projects, software, symposia, and role for the Russian Ministry of Health, at RIHTOP in Volgograd, Russia.

links.title: WUR: Toxicilogy
links.description: Education and research in the field of toxicity in food, nutrition, and environmental exposure in the Department of Agrotechnology and Food Sciences, Wageningen University, The Netherlands.

811148.title: Software
811148.description: This category is for sites concerned with software developed for analyzing or studying toxicity.

links.title: Lhasa
links.description: Not-for-profit company and educational charity offering software including Derek, for predicting toxicity, Meteor for predicting metabolic fate and Vitic, providing a database of toxicological information.

810983.title: Zoology
810983.description:
This category is for sites about zoology which is the branch of biology concerned with the study of animals including their anatomy, morphology, embryology and the function of their parts.
Sites about individual species or groups of species should be submitted to the appropriate category of Animalia.

links.title: Animal Diversity Web
links.description: Online database of animal history, distribution, classification and conservation biology provided by the University of Michigan.

links.title: AnAge: Animal Ageing Database
links.description: Curated database of ageing and life history in vertebrates, including extensive longevity records and observations.

811096.title: Academic Departments
811096.description: Listed sites are the official homepages, as found by visiting the university or institution main page and then following links to the department of Zoology.

links.title: Michigan State University Department of Zoology
links.description: Listing of graduate, undergraduate and interdisciplinary programs.

links.title: Oregon State University Department of Integrative Biology
links.description: Graduate and undergraduate program listings as well as department information.

links.title: University of Aberdeen School of Biological Sciences
links.description: Includes zoology facets, staff list, research themes and general data. Located in the United Kingdom.

links.title: University of Lincoln Department of Biological Sciences
links.description: Provides research and course information concerning the department, located in Lincoln, United Kingdom.

links.title: Animal Biodiversity Resource Center at the University of Barcelona
links.description: Practical courses on zoology, permanent and temporary exhibitions, zoological collections and wildlife photography courses.

811085.title: Animal Behavior
811085.description:
This category contains sites covering the many kinds of interactions that occur between animals, their physical habitat and their biological world. Behavior is the interface of the animal with its environment. The scientific study of animal behavior is Ethology.
Ethologists ask such questions as: By what means is the behavior produced? Of what use is it to the animal? How did it develop? What is its evolutionary history?

links.title: Movie Archives of Animal Behavior
links.description: An online animal behavior video database available in various formats. Most clips filmed in Japan.

links.title: The Ryan Lab
links.description: Situated at the University of Texas, this lab is addressing questions concerning the evolution and function of animal behavior. Most of the work centers on frogs and fish.

links.title: Research Projects in the Mammal Research Unit
links.description: Details of the current research projects being undertaken at the Mammal Research Unit at Bristol University, England.

links.title: The Arts of Deception - Mimicry and Camouflage
links.description: Article by Rhett Butler on camouflage as used by animals and the three forms of mimicry utilized by both predator and prey.

links.title: Consciousness in Animals and People with Autism
links.description: Temple Grandin discusses her views on animal consciousness, using comparisons from her experience with autism, citing scientific evidence on other neurological disorders which affect consciousness.

links.title: About Gender: Ethology
links.description: An introduction to animal reproduction, maternal strategies, living in groups, dominance and male behavior. The rest of the site deals with human gender roles, variance and identity.

links.title: Causes and Consequences of a Lack of Coevolution in Mullerian Mimicry
links.description: Article by James Mallet in which he discusses whether the unpalatable species that copy one another for their mutual benefit evolved together.

links.title: Warning Colour and Mimicry
links.description: Mimicry is a great example of evolution by natural selection. Outline of a lecture on the subject from the Evolutionary Genetics course at University College, London.

links.title: Animal Behavior/Sensory Biology
links.description: Article from Wikibooks explaining that, by learning how the senses gather information, a better understanding of behavior is gained.

links.title: Animal Behavior
links.description: A free online textbook from Wikibooks.

links.title: Animal Cognition Network
links.description: Provides links to current scientific literature in the field of animal cognition. Includes journal articles, reviews, books and relevant websites.

links.title: World on the Move: Great Animal Migrations
links.description: BBC's Natural History Unit gathers information from correspondents, scientists and amateur naturalists to monitor migrating mammals, birds and insects as they travel.

811090.title: Associations
811090.description: This category contains sites covering professional and academic societies and associations concerned with animal behavior.

links.title: Animal Behavior Society
links.description: Includes Applied Animal Behavior Certification information and selected web resources.

links.title: International Society for Behavioral Ecology
links.description: Contains information about the society and its journal, Behavioral Ecology.

links.title: Australasian Society for the Study of Animal Behaviour
links.description: Caters for individuals from Australia and New Zealand who are interested in the study of animal behavior.

links.title: International Society for Applied Ethology
links.description: Promotes research and education on the behavior and welfare of domestic and captive animals.

links.title: Association for the Study of Animal Behaviour
links.description: Details of forthcoming meetings, job advertisements, links to related sites and data about the society.

links.title: Comparative Cognition Society
links.description: A scientific society dedicated to studying the mechanisms and evolution of cognition in animals.

links.title: International Society for Neuroethology
links.description: ISN offers a platform for information and discussion in neuroethology, the field that describes the world of animal behavior in terms of how the nervous system works.

links.title: International Society for Anthrozoology
links.description: Promotes studies of human-animal relationships through published research, meetings and disseminated data.

links.title: Czech and Slovak Ethological Society
links.description: The Society provides a forum for exchange of knowledge relating to behavior and behavioral problems in farm, companion and free living animals.

links.title: Bioacoustics Research Program
links.description: A unit in the Cornell Lab of Ornithology, developing recording equipment, software, and algorithms to study animal communication and to monitor wildlife populations.  Information about their research, products, and publications.

links.title: Wildlife Sound Recording Society
links.description: Formed to encourage collecting and understanding of wildlife sounds.  Includes information about membership, events, articles, audio samples, and reviews of equipment. [UK]

links.title: Bioacoustics
links.description: Information from Wikipedia on this cross-disciplinary science which combines biology with acoustics. It involves the investigation of the sounds produced by animals, their dispersal, reception and use.

links.title: Bioacoustics Journal
links.description: This international journal, devoted to the study of animal sounds, publishes original research and review articles. There are also links to other relevant sites.

links.title: Interdisciplinary Center for Bioacoustics
links.description: CIBRA provides extensive links to other sites on underwater bioacoustics and marine mammals, general bioacoustics, equipment, consultancy, services and related projects and organizations.

links.title: International Bioacoustics Council
links.description: IBAC aims to promote international participation throughout the field of bioacoustical activity.

links.title: Laboratory of Aquatic Bioacoustics
links.description: Research is mainly focussed on the study of hearing by fish and other aquatic organisms, behavioral investigations and responses to human-generated noise.

links.title: Animal Communication Project
links.description: Dedicated to the science of communication between animals. Covers many branches of the animal kingdom with links to both past and present research projects.

links.title: Center for the Integrative Study of Animal Behavior
links.description: Information from Indiana University's program on animal behavior.

links.title: Compass Education and Training
links.description: Offers home study courses in animal behavior at intermediate and advanced level, and equine, feline, canine, reptile and parrot behavior and psychology studies.

811088.title: Journals
811088.description: Journals are intended for professionals and normally publish reports of original research, while magazines are directed to a general or popular audience. Both are listed here.

links.title: Animal Cognition
links.description: Interdisciplinary journal offering current research from many disciplines on all aspects of animal cognition with archives back to 1998. Registration needed.

links.title: Animal Behaviour
links.description: International publication containing critical reviews, original papers and research articles on all aspects of animal behaviour. Provides guidance for authors and subscriber information.

811089.title: Personal Pages
811089.description: Homepages of scientists involved in the study of animal behavior.

811103.title: Arthropoda
811103.description: This category is for sites devoted to the scientific study of the largest of all animal phyla, Phylum Arthropoda. This phylum includes the insects, spiders, mites and ticks, crustaceans, centipedes, millipedes, isopods, and trilobites.

links.title: American Arachnological Society

links.title: International Society for Arachnology

links.title: The Spiders Web

links.title: European Society of Arachnology

links.title: Arachnos.eu
links.description: Articles on venomous and non-venomous spiders.

links.title: British Arachnological Society (BAS)
links.description: Promotes study of arachnids. Provides access to publications, recordings and general information about the society.

links.title: AFRAS

links.title: Australasian Arachnological Society

links.title: Systematic and Applied Acarology Society
links.description: Promotes the study of ticks and mites. Includes organization information and several online journals.

links.title: European Water Mite Research

links.title: Acarology Laboratory

links.title: Acarological Society of Japan

811104.title: Entomology

links.title: University of Nebraska Department of Entomology

811112.title: Associations
811112.description: This category is for the homepages of entomological societies, organizations dedicated to the study and preservation of insects.

links.title: Entomological Society of America
links.description: Serves the professional and scientific needs of entomologists and people in related disciplines.

links.title: Florida Entomological Society

links.title: Entomological Society of Latvia

links.title: Entomological Society of Canada
links.description: Information from Wikipedia about the organization.

links.title: British Entomology and Natural History Society
links.description: Provides information on membership, the journal, other publications, grants, research and the collecting code.

links.title: Entomological Society of Israel
links.description: Provides information on the society and its aims, meetings, members and the peer-reviewed journal, the Israel Journal of Entomology.

links.title: Ontario Insects

links.title: Beetles and Coleopterists

811108.title: Forensic Entomology

links.title: Wikipedia: Forensic Entomology
links.description: Online encyclopedia article provides information on the topic.

links.title: Societas Europaea Lepidopterologica
links.description: European society for the study and conservation of moths and butterflies. Features council data, projects and links.

811111.title: Products and Services

links.title: Australian Entomological Supplies Pty.Ltd
links.description: Mail order entomological supplies specialists providing books and equipment for both the professional and amateur entomologist.

links.title: Bioquip Products
links.description: Equipment, supplies and books for the entomologist.

links.title: ALS: Anglian Lepidopterist Supplies
links.description: Specialists in moth traps, generators, and microscopes, but also offering the full range of products required by the amateur naturalist.

links.title: Annual Review of Entomology
links.description: Table of contents, abstracts, purchasing information and data about the journal.

links.title: Deutsche Entomologische Zeitschrift

links.title: European Journal of Entomology

links.title: Journal of Insect Science
links.description: Publishes papers on all aspects of the insect and arthropod biology, from the molecular to the ecological.

links.title: Bulletin of the Natural History Museum

811107.title: Research Groups and Centers

links.title: Society for Invertebrate Pathology

links.title: Royal Zoological Society of New South Wales

links.title: Canadian Society of Zoologists
links.description: Provides events, bulletins, news, publications and contact information.

810991.title: Chordates
810991.description: This category is for sites about the study of organisms in the Phylum Craniata (our phylum), Phylum Cephalochordata and Phylum Urochordata. Included in this category are the vertebrate classes fish, amphibians, reptiles, mammals and birds.

links.description: Clips recorded by Doug Von Gausig of the sounds made by various amphibians, reptiles, mammals and birds.

810998.title: Herpetology

Reptiles are cold-blooded, air-breathing vertebrates having the skin covered with scales. The class includes tortoises, turtles, lizards, snakes and the Crocodilia.
Amphibians are cold-blooded vertebrates with smooth skin. The class includes salamanders, frogs, toads and newts.
Herpetology is the scientific study of reptiles and amphibians.

815589.title: Chemistry
815589.description: Chemistry is typically defined as the science that studies the composition, structure, and transformation of matter.   It has been called "the central science" because of the way it is related with all the other sciences. Chemistry bridges the gap between physics and biology; it is a "helper science" in almost many technical disciplines; and it occupies a prominent position in industry between the extraction of raw materials and the manufacture of finished products. Of course, it is chemists who call it this way; other scientists may have different perspectives.   Chemistry is also distinguished from some other sciences because it creates its own object of study: chemists can imagine and create new compounds that have never existed in nature, so they are not constrained to what already exists, but only to what can be done.

815606.title: Bioanalytical Chemistry
815606.description:
This category links to categories with sites in which the topic is analysis of chemicals from living things. Nowadays, many of these analytes can be synthesized with out the need for a biological source.
The term is also used in cases where the analyte may be inorganic but the matrix is biological, such as iron in blood.
For cases of the presence of biological or inorganic contaminants in water, or effluent, see Environmental_Chemistry.

815654.title: Mass Spectrometry
815654.description:
Mass Spectrometry is the technique in which the analyte is ionized, separated from its matrix and mixture components, according its mass–to–charge ratio (m/z}, and detected to determine the molecular weight of component isotopes.
Common Abbreviations:
ESI - ElectroSpray Ionization
FAB - Fast Atom Bombardment
ICP - Inductively Coupled Plasma
MALDI - Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption Ionization
MS/MS - Mass Spectrometry repeated, typically within an ion trap
TOF - Time Of Flight

after being charged as with detergents such as SDS,

816033.title: Catalysis
816033.description: Catalysts are materials that promote or accelerate a chemical reaction, by associating with one or more of the reacting chemicals, and thereby lowering the energy barrier for reaction to occur. The association can be by adsorption or chemisorption (as is the case for solid, heterogeneous catalysts) or by complexation or coordination (as is the case for homogeneous catalysts, including enzymes). Catalysts can repeatedly promote the same reaction, without themselves being converted. The science of catalysis involves itself with developing new or improved catalysts, and with understanding the fundamental processes involved with catalytic reactions.

815921.title: Nonmetals
815921.description: Welcome to the home of NonmetalS!  Nonmetal elements possess high ionization energies and have high electronegativities.  They tend to gain electrons when in combination with metals, or to share electrons when in combination with other elements.  They tend to be brittle in the solid phase, to have low thermal and electrical conductivities, and to lack metallic luster.  Here  you can find information about the chemical and physical properties of nonmetals!

815768.title: Environmental Chemistry
815768.description:
Environmental chemistry is the study of chemicals, which by their absence or presence in critical amounts, influence life on land and in water.  Environmental chemistry includes the chemicals that influence the levels of critical chemicals such as oxygen and carbon dioxide.  Hence environmental chemistry is concerned with contamination of the atmosphere and water resulting from industrial pollution.  Environmental chemistry includes methods of detection, quantifying the presence, and measuring differences from the natural state, as well as their effects.

This category and its sub-categories includes sites about promoting and aiding this study.

815845.title: Process Research and Development
815845.description: Process Research and Development work in organic chemicals spans a wide spectrum of industries - from pharmaceuticals to petrochemicals.    Process Research is done essentially by organic chemists. It involves developing better, cost-effective, environment-friendly and safe processes for molecules that come out of discovery research.   Process Development involves optimizing chemical processes so that they are robust, repeatable and reproducible. This is essential to ensure problem-free scaling up from lab scale to pilot scale and then to commercial scale. This activity is the domain of chemical engineers.   Though the functions of the chemists and chemical engineers seem distinct, in reality chemists and chemical engineers need to work in tandem.   This section will include sites that are related to any aspect of Process research and process development. This will include various techniques used for process optimization - such as Design of Experiments, tools for creative process development - such as TRIZ, and other such areas.
