815842.description: This category contains sites from research groups mainly interested in various aspects and facets of chemistry. This may include but is not limited to link lists, research and information pages, pages concerning a single element (such as Boron).

links.title: Hites Group
links.description: Environmental chemistry.

links.title: Grinstaff Group
links.description: Novel biomaterials.

links.title: Dalton Group
links.description: Interdisciplinary research into materials chemistry with specific emphasis on electronic, electro-optic, and nonlinear optical materials along with nanoscale materials and nanoconstruction. A detailed research profile is available along with a full list of publications.

links.title: Schrock Group
links.description: Synthetic and mechanistic organotransition metal. Inorganic chemistry. Catalysis. Polymers.

links.title: Bowser Group
links.description: Biotechnology laboratory specializing in bioanalytical chemistry, specifically neuromessenger monitoring and in-vitro evolution of functional biomolecules. A list of people and contact information is available along with a list of publications.

links.title: Chemical Sciences Division
links.description: Carries out both basic and applied research. The full range of physical, inorganic and organic chemistry disciplines is represented. Emphasis is given to analytical chemistry, and the specialty areas of radiochemistry, geochemistry and materials chemistry are well represented.

links.title: Davis Group
links.description: Synthetic methodology. Molecular recognition. Supramolecular chemistry. Catalysis. Computer-aided molecular design.

links.title: Griesbeck Group
links.description: Photooxygenation of organic compounds. Photocycloaddition reactions: stereoselectivity and spinselectivity. Photodecarboxylation, photoisomerization, and photocyclization reactions of imides. Photochemical macrocyclization reactions. New photochemical reactors and technologies.

links.title: Laboratory of Biotransformation
links.description: Integrates both chemical and biological disciplines, including chemical modifications and biotransformations.

links.title: Hartgerink Group
links.description: Supramolecular chemistry. Autowiring nanocircuits. Self-assemblying ECM. Biomineralization.

links.title: Deiters Group
links.description: Biological Chemistry, Organic Chemistry, Organometallic Chemistry, DNA and RNA Chemistry, Photochemistry.

links.title: Jin Group
links.description: Materials chemistry research, with a focus on nano-scale materials.

links.title: Volkmer Group
links.description: Biomimetic and bioinorganic chemistry.

links.title: Environmental Organic Chemistry and Technology Group
links.description: Environmental and analytical organic chemistry, odour nuisance, physical-chemical waste gas treatment, biological waste gas treatment, advanced oxidation technologies, membrane assisted processes, clean technology, and exergy.

links.title: Whitesides Research Group
links.description: Physical and organic chemistry, materials science, biophysics, complexity, surface science, microfluidics, self-assembly, micro- and nanotechnology, science for developing economies, origin of life, and cell-surface biochemistry.

links.title: Bertozzi Group
links.description: Bioorganic chemistry group with interests in cell adhesion and cell surface recognition. A biography of Carolyn Bertozzi is presented along with a publications list. A detailed discussion of research interests is available along with group lists and photo gallery.

links.title: Meier Group
links.description: Renewable raw materials. Fats and oils. Polymers. Block-polymers. Living/controlled polymerization. Metathesis. Catalysis. Mass-spectrometry

links.title: Bluemel Group
links.description: The research covers immobilization of catalysts with phosphine linkers, surface organometallic chemistry and solid-state NMR spectroscopy. A C.V of Janet Bluemel along with a publications list and a detailed presentation of research interests is given.

links.title: Jaekle Group
links.description: Research onorganometallic and polymer chemistry, lists group members, publications and recent collaborations.

links.title: Ananikov Laboratory
links.description: Physical and organic chemistry group with research interests broadly divided into catalysis and organic synthesis, theoretical calculations and development of experimental techniques in NMR. Includes a research overview, publications and group members in Moscow.

links.title: The Grela's Group
links.description: Organometallic reactions and metathesies and their use in organic synthesis of natural products and pharmaceutically relevant compounds.

links.title: Janda Group
links.description: Understanding molecules, clusters, liquids and solids from the most fundamental point of view and applying this to the problem of gas hydrates.

links.title: Strouse Group
links.description: Integrated design and optical spectroscopy of nanometer-scale materials.

links.title: Dmochowski Group
links.description: Biochemical and chemical biology group developing small molecules, proteins and spectroscopic techniques for studying complex biomolecular systems.

816005.title: Software
816005.description: This category lists software used in Chemistry. This includes chemical engineering software, visualization software, chemical database software and specialized types of chemical software.

links.title: Linux for Chemistry CD-ROM Project
links.description: Bundles over one gigabyte of chemistry software, pre-built for the Linux operating system. Contents, screenshots, and ordering.

816009.title: Calculation
816009.description: Software that can be used to make various chemical calculations, such as molecular weight, pH, and redox potentials.

links.title: Physicochemical Calculators
links.description: Simple online and offline calculators for boiling point at reduced pressure, unit conversion, and molecular mass.

links.title: MS Tools
links.description: Online exact mass calculator, mass spectrum generator, and isotope distribution calculator.

links.title: Norgwyn Montgomery Software
links.description: NGMSI sells software for 3-D molecular modeling, chemical database creation and manipulation, 2-D publication quality drawing, calculation of over 100 physical properties from structure, automatic chemical internet database generation, and QSAR and QSPR analysis as well as chemical databases.

links.title: ChemBuddy
links.description: Calculators for pH, solution preparation and concentration conversion, acid-base equilibrium, buffer, hydrolysis, and dilution calculations.

links.title: Chemistry Functions
links.description: Molar conversions and an interactive periodic table directly on the webpage. Requires JavaScript.

links.title: ChemBalance
links.description: A windows program for balancing chemical equations.

links.title: ChemCalc
links.description: Online calculator for molecular formula, molecular weight, elemental composition, and isotopic distribution. Java recommended.

links.title: Formol
links.description: Open source command-line molar weight calculator. C++ source code and Linux packages available.

links.title: Molecular weight and elemental analysis calculator
links.description: This Unix program calculates the formula weight and the element distribution for a given chemical formula.

links.title: Molecular Weight Calculation
links.description: Very simple web-based utility for finding the molecular mass, elemental composition, and degree of unsaturation given a chemical formula.

816013.title: Cheminformatics
816013.description: Many people view chemoinformatics as an extension of chemical information, which is a well-established concept covering many areas that employ chemical structures, data storage and computational methods, such as compound registration databases, on-line chemical literature, SAR (Structure-Activity Relationsip) analysis and molecule-property calculation. [Timothy Ritchie "Chemoinformatics; manipulating chemical information to facilitate decision- making in drug discovery" Drug Discovery Today 6(16): 813-814, Aug. 2001]

links.title: Molinspiration Cheminformatics
links.description: Web-enabled software for large-scale calculation of molecular properties and database searches. Free online molecular descriptor calculations.

links.title: IDBS
links.description: Integrated framework for discovery data, from initial data capture to results analysis and reporting, to long-term data management.

links.title: Cheminformatics.org
links.description: Links to cheminformatics programs and QSAR datasets. Most programs are free, at least to academics.

links.title: ilib diverse
links.description: Organic compound library generation program using Monte Carlo randomization and property filtering.

links.title: Virtual Computational Chemistry Laboratory
links.description: Free on-line calculation of lipophilicity, logP, aqueous solubility, logS, molecular indices using Java applets. Analysis methods include neural networks, partial least squares and unsupervised forward selection.

links.title: MayaChemTools
links.description: Free collection of Perl scripts to support day-to-day computational discovery needs.

links.title: LigandScout
links.description: A software tool for PDB interpretation, 3D pharmacophore creation, modeling and visualization.

links.title: Karypis Lab: AFGen
links.description: Software tools for generating fragment-based descriptors for chemical compounds with applications to similarity search, virtual screening and library design.

links.title: Osiris Property Explorer
links.description: Software to calculate various drug-relevant properties of chemical structures. Prediction results are given a value and color coded for such properties as toxicity and solubility.

links.title: GLARE
links.description: Free software that facilitates and improves the design of chemical combinatorial libraries. It automates the process of reducing vendor chemical lists based on desired product properties.

816014.title: Companies
816014.description: Companies that make or sell software or related services for chemical applications, including molecular modeling and computational chemistry.

links.title: Gaussian, Inc
links.description: Contains manuals and other useful information related to the Gaussian98 program for quantum chemical calculation.

links.title: Wavefunction, Inc
links.description: Producer of spartan, a quantum chemical calculation program with nice visualization opportunities.

links.title: Hypercube, Inc
links.description: Producer of HyperChem, a molecular modeling package for windows and HyperNMR, a program for prediction of one-dimensional NMR spectra.

links.title: Accelrys, Inc
links.description: Producer of various molecular modeling and simulation software for both life and materials science research, like cerius, catalyst, insightII, quanta.

links.title: Tripos, Inc
links.description: Producer of sybyl, a computational tool kit for molecular design and analysis.

links.title: CrystalMaker Software
links.description: Crystal structures visualization and diffraction software for Macintosh.

links.title: Molecular Discovery Ltd.
links.description: Producer of GRID, a program for determining energetically favorable binding sites on molecules of known structure, and other "tools to derive high quality 3D descriptors with the purpose to link Structure-Based Drug Design, Chemoinformatics and Bioinformatics."

links.title: Advanced Chemistry Development
links.description: Specializes in Windows and applet-based software for structure drawing, nomenclature, NMR processing and prediction, chemical databases, and prediction of physicochemical properties.

links.title: Scientific Instrument Services
links.description: SIMION ion optics software and more than 200 scientific software products in mass spectrometry, chromatography, quality control, chemical inventory, MSDS, molecular modeling, database, and plotting. Online ordering.

links.title: QuantumBio
links.description: Develops solutions for Computer-Assisted Molecular Modeling and Computer-Assisted Drug Design, with emphasis on semiempirical quantum mechanics and bioinformatics.

links.title: ChemAxon
links.description: Programs, Java applets and other Java tools for chemistry, client-server applications, chemical databases, web site development.

links.title: Q-Chem, Inc.
links.description: Developer and provider of quantum chemistry software for ab initio electronic structure calculations.

links.title: Daylight Chemical Information Systems
links.description: Offers an integrated set of programs and libraries for chemical information processing. Based on the SMILES linear notation.

links.title: Chemistry-Software.com
links.description: Sells software for organic chemistry, mass spectroscopy, quality control, and general chemistry.

links.title: Chemical Computing Group (CCG)
links.description: Develops MOE, the Molecular Operating Environment, a package for high throughput discovery, bioinformatics, and computer aided molecular design.

links.title: Semichem, Inc.
links.description: Develops programs, such as AMPAC and CODESSA, based on semiempirical molecular orbital methods.

links.title: Eidogen-Sertanty
links.description: Provider of knowledge-based drug discovery solutions to biotechnology and pharmaceutical organizations through software, content, and collaborative service arrangements.

links.title: Molsoft L.L.C.
links.description: Provider of tools, databases and consulting services in the area of structure prediction, bioinformatics, cheminformatics, molecular visualization, and rational drug design.

links.title: Parallel Quantum Solutions
links.description: Manufactures parallel computers for high-performance computational chemistry.

links.title: Molecular Networks GmbH
links.description: Software for drug design, combinatorial chemistry, organic reactions and synthesis, data mining, and data warehousing.

links.title: CHEMAPPS
links.description: Specializes in the development of life science applications for medicinal chemistry professionals.

links.title: gNova Scientific Software
links.description: Provides consulting services and CHORD, a database cartridge for adding substructure search and other chemical functions to PosgreSQL.

links.title: OpenEye Scientific Software
links.description: Provides software and toolkits for structure-based drug design.

links.title: Desert Scientific Software
links.description: Provides software for medicinal research. Focused in structure based drug design and developing methods for predicting protein-ligand binding affinities. Develops web applications for protein databases and visualization.

links.title: FQS Poland
links.description: Reseller of various packages for chemistry, biochemistry, and materials science, including Cache and ChemOffice.

links.title: Quantumwise
links.description: Producers of first-principles simulation software for nanoscience used to model the electronic structure of molecules, crystals and surfaces.

links.title: AKos Consulting & Solutions GmbH
links.description: Provides chemoinformatics software to search, mine, calculate, simulate, store, register, enter, display, print, publish and correlate structures, reactions and data.

816006.title: Database
816006.description: This category contains chemical database, chemical safety and chemical inventory software.

links.title: Introductory Guide to  Chemical Database Systems
links.description: Background notes describing a common technique used to index chemical structure information within modern (O)RDBMS systems. Discusses Oracle cartridges and subgraph isomorphism.

links.title: CHEMATIX
links.description: Chemical inventory management and tracking Java-based software.

links.title: Chemoventory
links.description: Web based chemical inventory software with bar coding, MSDS management, and automated emails. Uses PHP and MySQL.

816021.title: Development
816021.description: Libraries and toolkits for the development of chemical software.

links.title: Software Development Lohninger
links.description: Software and programming components for Delphi and C++Builder covering mathematics, statistics,  scientific graphing, and chemistry.

links.title: Open Babel
links.description: Open-source C++ library for molecule file conversion and pattern matching.

links.title: CACTVS System
links.description: A distributed client/server system for the computation, management, analysis and visualization of chemical information of any type. Tool collection for several Unix flavors; some of the tools are distributed freely in precompiled form.

links.title: PerlMol
links.description: Free Perl modules for molecular chemistry. Tutorial, reference manual, downloads and mailing list.

links.title: Frowns
links.description: Free chemoinformatics toolkit geared toward rapid development of chemistry related algorithms. Written in Python with a small portion written in C++.

816007.title: Directories
816007.description: Web pages with comprehensive lists of Chemistry software sites.

links.title: Computational Chemistry List - Software
links.description: Archive of chemistry software for Unix, MS-DOS, Windows, Mac. Includes source code in most cases.

links.title: Chemical Informatics Letters
links.description: The latest news in chemical informatics, links to relevant web sites, analysis and discussion.

links.title: Linux4Chemistry
links.description: An up-to-date directory of Linux software for chemistry. Lists more than 100 free and commercial programs.

816017.title: Educational
816017.description: This category contains software that can be used for education of students in the chemical arts and sciences.

links.title: Lab Check Laboratory Grading Program
links.description: A complete high school chemistry laboratory program. It includes 22 beginning level and ten advanced level chemistry experiments, and a computer program that evaluates student-entered data. Ordering information available.

links.title: Chem-It
links.description: Free Windows software for novice Chemistry students. Includes periodic table and conversion charts.

links.title: Chemware
links.description: Educational Windows software and shareware for General, Organic, Analytical and Physical Chemistry. For use in high school and college. Ordering information available.

links.title: Model Science Software
links.description: Develops simulation software for education, such as Model ChemLab, which can be used for distance learning over the Internet.

links.title: Chem1 Concept Builder
links.description: Instructional software for general chemistry. Provides access to demo version, frequently asked questions and support resources.

links.title: Academy Savant
links.description: Corporate training and college/university-level courses on CD and video on chromatography (HPLC, GC, LCMS, GCMS), spectroscopy, basic laboratory skills, safety and compliance.

816015.title: Materials Chemistry
816015.description: Software for Materials Chemistry. This includes, for example, polymers, glasses, alloys, and ceramics.

links.title: Ceramic Chemistry and Database Software
links.description: INSIGHT oxide chemistry glaze recipe  calculation and FORESIGHT ceramic database

816008.title: Periodic Table
816008.description: Software, usually interactive, that contains periodic table type presentation of elemental characteristics.

links.title: Atomic Mac
links.description: An electronic version of the periodic table of elements with detailed physical and nuclear information.

links.title: Periodic Spiral of the Elements
links.description: For Mac and PC, an alternative representation of the periodic table that aims to better place the lanthanoids, actinoids, and hydrogen. The program also includes extensive information about elements, their uses and their properties. Shockwave demo available online.

links.title: Kalzium
links.description: Free periodic table program for the KDE desktop environment.

816016.title: Physical and Theoretical
816016.description: Software for chemical thermodynamics, chemical kinetics, molecular dynamics, quantum chemistry, etc.

links.title: Thermodynamic Modeling
links.description: About equilibrium composition, thermodynamic modeling,  thermodynamic properties of substances,  real gas properties, and computational thermodynamics.

links.title: ADF
links.description: ADF, the Amsterdam Density Functional program for the treatment of complex chemical problems.

links.title: WebMO
links.description: Web interface for the quantum chemistry packages MOPAC, Gaussian, and GAMESS. Free version available for download; pro version also available.

links.title: Zeta Potential
links.description: Zeta is a free (GPL) computer program which can be used to calculate the zeta potentials.

links.title: Gamess
links.description: An ab initio quantum chemistry package GAMESS.  Developed by the Mark Gordon research group at Iowa State University. Site is not GAMESS-Uk.

links.title: YAeHMOP
links.description: Yet Another extended Huckel Molecular Orbital Package. Performs calculations and visualization for both molecular and extended materials in 1, 2, or 3 dimensions. Freely available in source form.

links.title: CRYSTAL Home Page
links.description: Unix program to compute the electronic structure of periodic systems within Hartree Fock, density functional or various hybrid approximations. Documentation, licensing, and downloads available.

links.title: Extensible Computational Chemistry Environment
links.description: Graphical user interface for Linux/Solaris/IRIX with visualization tools and a data management framework for setting up, submitting, and analyzing computational chemistry calculations.

links.title: GaussSum
links.description: Collection of Python scripts which parse the output of Gaussian or GAMESS calculations to extract information such as the progress of the SCF cycles, geometry optimisation, UV-Vis/IR/Raman spectra, MO levels, and MO contributions.

links.title: AOMix
links.description: A program for molecular orbital analysis. It calculates the MO compositions of the constituent chemical fragments from the output files of various quantum-chemical packages, analyzes chemical bonding using overlap populations, and generates density-of-states spectra. License required.

links.title: Moloc
links.description: Molecular Design Software Suite for Irix, Linux, and Windows. Includes features such as structure generation, molecular mechanics, conformational search, molecular dynamics, and similarity analysis. Free for academic users.

links.title: CASTEP - CAmbridge Serial Total Energy Package
links.description: Uses density functional theory to provide an atomic-level description of materials and molecules.

links.title: Atoms in Molecules (AIM2000)
links.description: Windows program for analyzing and visualizing molecules using the theory of Richard Bader. Demo version available.

links.title: MPQC
links.description: The "Massively Parallel Quantum Chemistry Program". Computes properties of atoms and molecules from first principles using the time independent Schrödinger equation. Free, available under the GPL.

links.title: PyQuante
links.description: Python Quantum Chemistry - an open-source suite of programs for developing quantum chemistry methods. Emphasis is on simplicity, rather than speed, but some bottlenecks are written in C.

links.title: CHEAQS Next
links.description: Windows program for calculating chemical equilibria, and solving speciation problems in aqueous systems. Includes database of equilibrium constants, publications list, terms, and free download from the Netherlands.

links.title: Argus Lab
links.description: Molecular modeling program for Windows9x operating systems with 3D-builder, ab initio calculation modules, and simple molecular mechanics. Includes version history, citations, and contacts in Seattle, Washington.

links.title: Kinetiscope
links.description: Interactive method for modeling the kinetics of a wide variety of chemical systems, including three-dimensional, compartmental and single reactor models. Electrochemical reactions and reactions controlled by an external stimuli can be entered in the reaction scheme. Includes history, package contents, FAQ, publications, user's manual, and download from the authors' web site.

links.title: MINEQL+
links.description: Chemical equilibrium modeling system for low-temperature applications. Useful in aquatic chemistry applications.

links.title: Agile Molecule
links.description: General purpose molecular modeling software that performs quantum mechanics calculations for initial molecular model development, molecular mechanics and dynamics simulations in the gas or in condensed phase.

links.title: Chemissian
links.description: GUI-based program to build electronic and spin density and molecular orbital contour maps, plot experimental and CIS/TDDFT-calculated spectra, draw MO diagrams, analyze composition of MOs and calculate populations. Supports GAMESS and Gaussian outputs.

links.title: OpenThermo
links.description: Open source program package for calculation of thermodynamic functions from molecular data.

links.title: Quantum Monte Carlo: CASINO
links.description: Provides highly accurate quantum-mechanical calculations for atoms, molecules, polymers, surfaces, crystals and various model systems. Developed at the Cavendish Laboratory, University of Cambridge and distributed free of charge.

links.title: PyVib2
links.description: Permits the automatic correlation of vibrational motions of molecules thereby allowing an understanding of Raman, Raman optical activity, infrared vibrational absorption, and vibrational circular dichroism spectra.

816018.title: Structural
816018.description: Software for the visualization and drawing of chemical structures.

links.title: MOLGEN
links.description: Program for the automatic generation of constitutional isomers and combinatorial libraries, for Unix/Linux and WinNT/95. Free demo available.

links.title: Computational Chemistry: Spartan
links.description: General purpose modelling tool that uses modern computational methods to provide quantitative data on molecular structure, energy, reactivity, selectivity and a wide range of molecular properties.

816020.title: Drawing
816020.description: Software for the generation of 2D chemical structure diagrams.

links.title: Chemtool
links.description: Free software for drawing organic molecules and storing them as an X-Bitmap, LaTeX and XFig file. For Linux/Unix, includes source code, screenshots, and downloads.

links.title: Gifcreator
links.description: Create GIFs and PNGs of 2D plots of chemical structures.

links.title: Chemical Drawing Programs Review
links.description: Detailed comparison between ISIS/Draw, ChemDraw, ChemWindow, ChemSketch, Chemistry 4-D Draw, WinPLT, MarvinSketch, ChemPen, WinDrawChem, and JChemPaint.

links.title: EasyChem
links.description: Free Linux structure drawing program, designed with emphasis on press quality, speed of, precision, and ability to add arbitrary ornaments such as orbitals.

links.title: WinDrawChem/XDrawChem
links.description: Free structure drawing software for Windows and Unix, with simple spectral predictions. Source code available.

links.title: PLT
links.description: Shareware drawing program for Windows; capable of exporting structures as metafiles, bitmaps, and HTML pages.

links.title: BKchem
links.description: Free, portable, and open-source structure drawing program. Written in Python.

links.title: JChemPaint
links.description: Free, open-source editor for 2D chemical structures. Written in Java and developed by an international team of opensource programmers.

links.title: ChemDoodle
links.description: Software tool for drawing chemical structures, diagrams and figures. Demo available for immediate download. ChemDoodle works on Windows, Mac OSX, and Linux.

816019.title: Visualization
816019.description: Programmes to view or analyze properties of small molecules or proteins. Some sites offer physical models.

links.title: OpenRasMol
links.description: Provided for the convenience of users and software developers of open source versions of RasMol.

links.title: VMD
links.description: A free program for visualization and analysis of biological systems such as proteins, nucleic acids, and lipid bilayer assemblies.

links.title: Historical Molecular Graphics
links.description: Digitized versions of 16mm movies of molecular structures produced in the early days of interactive molecular graphics.

links.title: Biodesigner and iMol
links.description: A molecular viewer for Windows9x systems with sequence editor and protein builder. Free for academic use. Additionaly the iMol molecule viewer is available for Mac OS X systems.

links.title: RasMol
links.description: Molecular visualization freeware for proteins, DNA, and macromolecules. Freely available for Windows, Macintosh, and UNIX.

links.title: Jmol
links.description: Open source molecule viewer written in Java. It runs as a standalone application and as a web browser applet.

links.title: Viewmol
links.description: An open-source graphical front end for computational chemistry programs such as Gaussian, Gamess, and Mopac. Available for Linux, FreeBSD, Mac OS X, and other Unices.

links.title: SweetMollyGrace
links.description: A suite of freeware tools for automating work of rendering and animating molecules. Generates high quality images of molecules from PDB, XYZ, or molfiles using raytracing tools (Povray and Raster3D).

links.title: ChemCraft
links.description: Windows-based program for visualization of molecular structures, vibrational modes, molecular orbitals, energy gradient and other properties from log files produced by the GAMESS and Gaussian packages.

links.title: Protein Explorer
links.description: A web-based viewer for the 3D structures of proteins, DNA and RNA.  Requires Netscape and the Chime plugin, which is only available for Windows9x.

links.title: UCSF Chimera
links.description: Highly extensible, interactive molecular graphics program. It is the successor to UCSF Midas and MidasPlus. Free of charge for academic, government, non-profit, and personal use.

links.title: PyMolWiki
links.description: User-contributed wiki to supplement the PyMOL documentation.

links.title: Nanotube Modeler
links.description: A program for generating and visualizing the xyz-coordinates for nanotubes, nanocones, nanosheets, and fullerenes. For Windows; free demo version available.

links.title: CueMol
links.description: Free molecular structure visualization and rendering program for Windows.

links.title: PyMOL
links.description: A free and flexible molecular graphics and modelling package which can be also used to generate animated sequences.

links.title: Santorini and Patmos, Molecular Viewer and Screensaver
links.description: Read XYZ or PDB files of atoms and display them in a 3-dimensional view on Windows PCs.

links.title: Review of Molecular Modelling Programs
links.description: Reviews, screenshots, and table of features comparing over a dozen freely available molecular modelling and viewing programs.

links.title: Avogadro
links.description: Open source advanced molecular editor designed for cross-platform use in computational chemistry, molecular modeling, bioinformatics, materials science and related areas. It offers flexible rendering and a powerful plugin architecture.

links.title: Jamberoo: Cross Platform Molecular Editor
links.description: Free cross-platform application for displaying, analyzing, editing, converting and animating molecular systems.

816012.title: Web Publishing
816012.description: Software for the display of chemical information on web pages. This includes chemical equations and structures.

links.title: GIF/PNG-Creator for 2D Plots of Chemical Structures
links.description: Creates pictures from structures in different formats. You can choose between GIF and PNG format.

links.title: VRML File Creator for Chemical Structures
links.description: Translates molecules from different formats to VRML.

links.title: VRML in Chemistry
links.description: Brief introduction to VRML and its application for displaying chemical data.

804125.title: Directories
804125.description: Contains Internet directories with links relating to the  field of science.  All directories pertaining to a particularly branch of science are to be found within the category for that branch.

links.title: SciCentral: News
links.description: Science portal includes breaking news from scientific journals, universities and government sources.

links.title: Nearctica: The Natural History of North America
links.description: Comprehensive site including education, natural history, conservation, environment, ecology, evolution, geology, paleontology, and systematics.

links.title: STN Easy
links.description: Web-based search engine that accesses more than 60 databases in the Scientific and Technical Information Network. Includes Scitech, regulatory information, MSDS, chemical inventories, toxicology, chemical suppliers, other topics.

links.title: Strategian
links.description: Descriptions, ratings and links for a few "top internet sites" in biology, chemistry, computer science, mathematics, medicine, physics, and psychology.

links.title: STN International on the Web
links.description: An online scientific and technical information service (subscription required) that provides access to more than 200 in-depth databases in science and technology to offer direct links to the scientific literature, patents, and chemical catalogs.

links.title: A Science Bibliography
links.description: Stanford University collection of scientific resources and publications.

links.title: The Science Page
links.description: Links to resources in all main science areas, plus newsgroups, constants, history, teacher resources and science analogies.

links.title: WebExhibits Museum
links.description: Virtual museum of science, humanities, and culture. Founded 1999.

links.title: First Gov for Science
links.description: Collection of information provided by U.S. government agencies, including research and development results.

links.title: Lab Finder
links.description: Searchable database for testing and calibration laboratory facilities by country and type of experiments.

links.title: Refdesk.com - Science Information Resources
links.description: Annotated collection of resource pages for chemistry, physics, technology, anthropology, biology, food science, genetics, geology, cosmology, science history, engineering, math, and related online magazines.

links.title: Virtual Library: Science
links.description: Directory of the Virtual Library, an expert-run catalog of sections of the web, which is particularly strong in science topics.

links.title: The Scout Report for Physical Sciences
links.description: Biweekly e-zine offers a selective collection of internet resources covering topics in the sciences, and related fields such as math and engineering, that have been chosen by librarians and content specialists in the given field of study.

links.title: Scholarly Societies Project: Health Sciences
links.description: Directory of learned societies and associations with members in a number of different health-related fields.

links.title: Dissertation CIS
links.description: Project to provide access to electronic versions of doctoral theses in a range of scientific disciplines translated from the original Russian.

links.title: Re3data.org
links.description: Registry of Research Data Repositories. Information about the schema and explantion of functions.

links.title: World Conference Calendar
links.description: The directory publishes information on academic conferences all over the world.

links.title: Museo Galileo - Virtual Museum
links.description: An online museum about the history of science. Italian and English language.

811619.title: Earth Sciences
811619.description: Earth science, also known as geoscience, is the study of the physical properties of the land, atmosphere, inland waters and oceans on earth.

links.title: Earth Science Australia
links.description: Earth science resources, images, freeware for students and teachers as well as general information about earth science in Australia.

links.title: NASA - Earth Science Division
links.description: Research center focusing on ecosystem science technology, atmospheric physics and chemistry, and airborne sensors.  Includes list of research projects, discoveries, education outreach efforts, news, seminars, and publications.

links.title: National Research Council (U.S.) Commission on Geosciences, Environment, and Resources
links.description: Scope includes atmospheric sciences, climate, oceanography, solid-earth sciences, radioactive waste management, polar research, environmental science and toxicology, natural disasters, and water science. Commission reports cover scientific/technical aspects of public policy issues in these areas.

812192.title: Hurricane Rita
812192.description:
Hurricane Rita started in the Key West area, which is located off the southern tip of Florida, USA. It moved westward and became a category 5 hurricane in the middle of the Gulf of Mexico. The path of the phenomenon finally met land between the Texas and Louisiana state borders at a category 3. The actual path of the storm and the weather predictions were fairly close to computer models.

The evacuation of major urban centers during a storm continued to be a problem as traffic congestion slowed travel down to 5 miles per hour. This is tough on motor vehicles and causes engines to warm up. This may or may not be the cause for the bus explosion with elderly patient evacuees.

The cities of Galveston, Beaumont and Port Charles took the worse hit from the initial storm. The oil refineries and chemical plants in Texas suffered only minor damage. On the negative side, several New Orlean's levees in Louisiana that were hard hit during Hurricane Katrina broke and caused flooding again to occur in certain neighborhoods.

Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and active military were prepositioned, this time, near the predicted affected areas.

811698.title: Geochemistry
811698.description: Geochemistry is the study of chemical elements and their isotopes, and their distribution and abundance within minerals, ores, rocks, waters, and the atmosphere.  Geochemistry also includes the dynamic aspects of reaction and circulation of the elements in nature.  While geochemistry is most often used in reference to the Earth, it also applies to the study of the chemical elements and their isotopes on the moon and other planets.

links.title: Martian Geochemistry
links.description: Summarizes the geochemical results obtained by NASA's Mars Pathfinder mission.  Includes plots of geochemical trends, and comparisons with earlier Viking mission data as well as with Earth geochemistry.

links.title: Archives of ISOGEOCHEM
links.description: Searchable archives of the e-mail group for stable isotope geochemistry.

links.title: Geochemistry
links.description: Wikipedia article on the branch of science involving the study of the chemical composition of the Earth and other planets, and the chemical processes and reactions that govern the composition of rocks and soils.

links.title: IMWA: Geochemistry
links.description: Online textbook by William M. White.

811706.title: Databases
811706.description: This category is for collections of geochemical data, whether natural or experimentally derived.

811708.title: Geochemical Analyses
811708.description: This category is for compilations of chemical or isotopic analyses of natural samples, including atmospheric (and other gaseous reservoirs), aqueous, and solid samples.

links.title: The Index to Marine Geological Seafloor Samples
links.description: Also known as the Curators' Database, this is a cooperative effort among nineteen oceanographic institutions and governmental agencies to provide information on the contents of their collections of seafloor samples to researchers. More than 100,000 samples can be searched on-line by specifying any combination of institution, cruise, ship, collection date, water depth, sampling technique, or geographic location.

links.title: Marine Minerals Bibliography and Geochemical Database
links.description: A computerized bibliography and geochemical database on offshore marine mineral deposits. Primarily contains chemical analyses of present-day marine deposits of ferromanganese nodules and crusts (more than 140,000 analyses), but also includes some data for heavy minerals (approximately 1400 analyses). Analyses can be downloaded from the website or ordered on a CD.

links.title: GEOROC Geochemical Database
links.description: GEOROC (GEOchemistry of Rocks of the Oceans and Continents) is a searchable collection of more than 50,000 analyses from different tectonic settings. Queries can be made based on bibliography, tectonic setting, geography, chemistry, and petrography.

811707.title: Thermochemical
811707.description: This category is for databases containing thermodynamic and other chemical data on elements and compounds of interest to researchers in all fields of geochemistry.

links.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook

links.title: Joint Expert Speciation System

links.title: WebElements Periodic Table of the Elements

811704.title: Economic Geochemistry

links.title: Geochemical Instrumentation and Analysis

links.title: Neuhoff, Philip

links.title: Petrology
links.description: Wikipedia article on this branch of geology that studies rocks, and the conditions in which rocks form, especially at the microscopic level.

811709.title: Products and Services

links.title: Isotech Laboratories, Inc. (Champaign, Il.)

Analysis price lists and turnaround times are also provided, along with information on sampling containers and procedures.

links.title: Exploration Geochemistry Services
links.description: Off-shore and on-shore geochemical sampling of gases, water, and sediments for oil and gas exploration. Provides example applications for geochemical exploration surveys.

links.title: Environmental Geochemistry Consulting
links.description: EGC is a consulting company specializing in advanced chemical fingerprinting for identification, differentiation and source-allocation of hydrocarbon contaminants, environmental forensic geochemistry and litigation support.

links.title: Chemostrat Ltd
links.description: Chemostratigraphy is an intuitive stratigraphic technique that utilises changes in the bulk inorganic geochemistry of sediments to map out changes in provenance, diagenesis, palaeoclimate and facies. Includes scientific rationale and description of practical applications.

links.title: Geotrack International
links.description: Laboratory facilities provide a range of analytical and electron and optical microscope services to the mineral exploration industry. Includes case histories and research publications on thermal history reconstruction.

links.title: Integrated Geochemical Interpretation Ltd

links.title: Petrophase Ltd

links.title: TDI-Brooks International, Inc.
links.description: Provides an analytical laboratory facility and marine research vessels for field services related to geochemistry and environmental chemistry.

links.title: Chris Clayton Geochemistry Services
links.description: Consultancy specializing in geochemistry as applied to petroleum exploration and production, with subsidiary groundwater chemistry and mineral exploration projects.

links.title: PHREEQC

811700.title: Publications

Tables of contents and indices, and on-line access to articles for subscribers.

links.title: Chemical Geology
links.description: The official publication of the European Association for Geochemistry, with organic and inorganic research from around the world. Searchable indexes and on-line access to articles (subscribers only).

links.title: Marine Chemistry
links.description: International journal focusing on all chemical aspects of the marine environment, including theoretical and experimental research. Tables of contents and indices, and on-line access to articles for subscribers.

links.title: Applied Geochemistry
links.description: Journal of the International Association of Geochemistry and Cosmochemistry. Tables of contents, abstracts, and on-line access to articles (subscribers only).

links.title: Organic Geochemistry

links.title: Ore Geology Reviews
links.description: Publishes recent advances from fields related to the study of, and search for, ore deposits. Tables of contents, author index, ordering information, and on-line access to articles for subscribers.

links.title: Journal of Geochemical Exploration
links.description: Publishes research on all aspects of geochemistry of the environment and the application of geochemistry to mineral resource exploration. Tables of contents, indices, and on-line access to articles for subscribers.

links.title: Environmental Geochemistry Group

links.title: GeoSmitty's Geology and Outdoor Pages

812255.title: Geophysics
812255.description: Geophysics involves the application of physical theories and measurements to discover the properties of the earth. The discipline dates to antiquity, mainly as a scientific approach to earthquake prediction (a problem still unsolved), but major progress began in the late 1500s with initial work in such areas as magnetism and gravity. Tremendous improvements in instrumentation in the early years of the 20th century generated rapid progress in geophysics and ultimately led, in the 1960s, to the theory of plate tectonics.  Plate tectonics, the study of the interior structure of the earth, and such related areas as global and regional processes are known collectively as solid earth geophysics. The subdiscipline known as exploration geophysics involves the use of geophysical theory and instrumentation to locate petroleum and other mineral sources. Unlike solid earth geophysics, exploration geophysics generally concentrates on finding lateral heterogeneities in a relatively small part of the earth's crust.  Geophysics is considered by some to be a branch of geology, by others to be of equal rank. It is distinguished from the other earth sciences largely by its use of instruments to make direct or indirect measurements of the parts of the Earth being studied, in contrast to the more direct observations which are typical of geology.   The following definitions are from Robert E. Sheriff's Encyclopedic Dictionary of Applied Geophysics.      1. The study of the earth by quantitative physical method, especially by seismic reflection and refraction, gravity, magnetic, electrical, electromagnetic, and radioactivity methods.    2. The application of physical principles to studies of the earth. Includes the branches of (a) seismology (earthquakes and elastic waves); (b) geothermometry (heating of the earth, heat flow, volcanology, and hot springs); (c) hydrology (ground and surface water, sometimes including glaciology); (d) physical oceanography; (e) meteorology; (f) gravity and geodesy (the earth's gravitational field and the size and form of the earth); (g) atmospheric electricity and terrestrial magnetism (including ionosphere, Van Allen belts, telluric currents, etc.); (h) tectonophysics (geological processes in the earth); and (i) exploration and engineering geophysics. Geochronology (the dating of earth history) and geocosmogony (the origin of the earth) are sometimes added to the foregoing list.    3. Often refers to solid-earth geophysics only, thus excluding (c), (d), (e), and portions of other subjects from the above list.    4. Exploration geophysics is the use of seismic, gravity, magnetic, electrical, electromagnetic, etc., methods in the search for oil, gas, minerals, water, etc., with the objective of economic exploitation.
