links.title: Volcano Data at NGDC
links.description: Volcano data, volcano slide sets available from National Geophysical Data Center.

812053.title: Personal Pages
812053.description: Journals, images, and personal experiences regarding volcanoes.

links.title: Volcanoes of the Cascades
links.description: Their eruptive history and hazards.

links.title: Indonesia-Adventure
links.description: Information on volcanoes in Indonesia including, Bali, Java and Lomobok. Includes photographs, background information.

links.title: Burgh's Volcanoes
links.description: Photos, webcams and links to volcano information.

links.title: Galapagos Volcanology
links.description: Research on geology and volcanoes by Dennis Geist.

812049.title: Research
812049.description: Sites about research on volcanoes, or on some aspect of volcanology.

links.title: Merapi Volcano, Java
links.description: Bibliography, monitoring techniques and photos about one of the most dangerous volcano in the world.

links.title: Killer Lake Nyos in Africa
links.description: Carbon dioxide gas outbursts from lakes Nyos and Monoun in Cameroon, West Africa, killed hundreds of people. A controlled degassing operation is scheduled to begin in January, 2001, for reducing the risk of future carbon dioxide suffocation.

links.title: Lake Nyos, Cameroon, West Africa
links.description: Eruption of carbon dioxide from Lake Nyos killed hundreds. A controlled degassing experiment is planned to reduce this hazard.

links.title: Vhub
links.description: An online resource for collaboration in volcanology research and risk mitigation.

links.title: The Electronic Volcano
links.description: A pioneer site started by Professor Dick Stoiber at Dartmouth College providing information on active volcanoes. Not well updated since 1997, but older information is excellent.

links.title: International Association of Volcanology and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior
links.description: Represents the primary international focus for research in volcanology, efforts to mitigate volcanic disasters, and research into closely related disciplines, such as igneous geochemistry and petrology, geochronology, volcanogenic mineral deposits, and the physics of the generation and ascent of magmas in the upper mantle and crust.

812052.title: Videos
812052.description: Videos on tapes, CDROMs, and DVDs of volcanoes and volcanic eruptions.

links.title: Fire Work Studios
links.description: Explore Kilauea Volcano, Hawaii on CDROM with maps, video, and guides.

links.title: Volcano Video Productions
links.description: Known for their spectacular close-up footage of volcanic eruptions in Hawaii.

links.title: Hawaiian Volcano Video
links.description: Footage of Hawaii's Kilauea, the most active volcano on earth.

links.title: Stromboli On-Line videos
links.description: Many videos about volcanic activity of Stromboli, Etna, Ol Doinyo Lengai, Erta Ale, Karimski and other volcanoes.

links.title: Natural Disaster Early Warning Network
links.description: The Disaster Warning Network will provide early warnings of natural disasters                    before they impact people and property.

links.title: FEMA: USA Federal Disaster Declarations
links.description: Sortable by state or by year.

links.title: Fire Area Landscaping
links.description: Landscaping advice for homes in fire areas, using California Native Plants.

links.title: Forest Fire Lookout Association
links.description: Organization involved in research of former forest fire lookout sites, ground cabins and early forest fire detection methods.

links.title: The Global Fire Monitoring Centre (GFMC) - Fire Globe
links.description: Reports on fires from around the world, fire models, historical fire data.

links.title: National Wildfire Coordinating Group
links.description: Operational group coordinating programs, policies, standards and training of participating wildfire management agencies. Contains information on teams, calendar, and list of publications.

links.title: Alberta Fire Bans
links.description: Portal to FireBan information in the province of Alberta. Administrators of cities, counties and municipal districts can login to add, update and remove firebans.

links.title: USGS: A Global Perspective on Wildfires
links.description: Provides information on a study of the global implications of wildfires and the many influences fire has on ecosystem processes.

links.title: Canadian Wildland Fire Information System
links.description: Features daily weather, fire behavior and hot spots maps. Offers regional  satellite   images, historical analysis, publications and links. In English and French.

links.title: National Interagency Fire Center: Fire Information
links.description: Find news, maps, statistics, weather information, assessments and outlooks.

811697.title: News and Media
811697.description: RSS (Rich Site Summary - Really Simple Syndication) or Atom are XML-based formats for the distribution of information comprising headlines, descriptions and links back to a webpage with the detailed references.

links.title: Earthweek
links.description: Weekly "Diary of the Planet" featuring current information on natural events around the globe.

links.title: Oil IT Journal
links.description: Monthly headlines from Oil IT Journal.

links.title: ScienceDaily Headlines: Earth & Climate
links.description: Daily headlines about discoveries in the earth sciences, including geology and geophysics, climatology and meteorology, oceanography, and the environment, from the world's leading universities and research centers.

links.title: ScienceDaily Headlines: Fossils & Ruins
links.description: Daily headlines about discoveries in fossils and ruins and other topics in paleontology and archaeology, including dinosaurs, early humans, and lost civilizations, from the world's leading universities and research centers.

links.title: USGS Newsroom
links.description: Latest press releases and science picks from the United States Geological Survey.

links.title: Phys.org: Earth Sciences News
links.description: Provides daily earth science news updates.

links.title: Geobulletin: News from the Geoblogosphere
links.description: Collects and presents news from more than 200 blogs dealing with earth sciences. Topics covered include geology, the oil and gas industry, paleontology, geoinformatics and climate change.

links.title: Geology.com - News
links.description: A  daily updated list of earth science related news and events

links.title: BBC News - Science & Environment - UK Edition
links.description: BBC News for up-to-the-minute provides trusted World and UK news as well as local and regional perspectives (eventually including video, audio and feature stories).

links.title: iGeoInfo
links.description: The International Coalition for GeoInformatics was founded to build a community to promote data sharing concepts, and geoinformatics in general, at an international level in the fields of sedimentary geology and paleobiology.

links.title: Earth Science News -- ScienceDaily
links.description: Earth science research and news. Read science articles on air quality, geology, meteorology, oceanography, paleontology and science and the environment.

811711.title: Oceanography
811711.description:
Oceanography and marine science directory.

Oceanography, also known as oceanology, sea science, ocean science, and marine science, is the scientific study of the ocean, including its physics, chemistry, biology, and geology.

811714.title: Conferences
811714.description: Forthcoming and past conferences, symposia and workshops with an oceanographic theme.

links.title: Oceanology International
links.description: Aim is to establish a joint ocean forum, by enabling many complementary key events to be held in one place and at one time, therefore bringing together a range of the most highly respected societies, organizations and groups.

links.title: Offshore Technology Conference
links.description: Managers, engineers, operators, scientists, and students meet to review new technologies, establish international business relationships, enhance business development, and discover solutions to key issues in the offshore industry.

links.title: Gordon Research Conferences
links.description: Provides details of meetings and seminars scheduled for 2010 in a wide range of disciplines.

links.title: Polar Marine Science
links.description: Portfolio of Gordon Research Conferences on the changes taking place in the polar oceans covering the impacts of a changing climate on physical, chemical, biological and coupled systems.

links.title: Waves and Operational Oceanography, Brest, France.  June 23-24, 2003.
links.description: A scientific workshop to assess the current state of knowledge on waves in relation to currents, surface drifts and air-sea interactions hosted by the French Hydrographic and Oceanographic Service (SHOM).

links.title: Colour of Ocean Data Symposium, Brussels, Belgium. November 25-27, 2002.
links.description: Symposium on oceanographic data and information management with special attention to biological data.  Brussels, Belgium.

811712.title: Data Centers
811712.description: National and International Oceanographic Data Centres

links.title: National Oceanographic Data Center  (NODC)
links.description: The United States NODC archives and provides public access to global oceanographic and coastal data, products, and information. Popular items include beach temperatures, coastal buoy data, global sea temperature and salinity, a photo collection and the ocean data archive.

links.title: Japan Oceanographic Data Center (JODC)
links.description: Japanese National Oceanographic Data Center archiving and disseminating marine data obtained from various Japanese marine research institutes and organizations. View international project links and use J-DOSS, a system that aims to provide users with the data managed by the JODC via the internet.

links.title: British Oceanographic Data Centre (BODC)
links.description: UK national facility for preserving and distributing oceanographic and marine data. Staff have direct experience of marine data collection and analysis to ensure that the biological, chemical, physical and geophysical data handled are documented and stored for current and future use. View information on current and past projects, search data and cruise inventories, download and request oceanographic data and order data products.

links.title: Intergovernmental Oceanographic Data and Information Exchange (IODE)
links.description: Enhances marine research, exploitation and development by facilitating the exchange of oceanographic data and information between participating Member States and by meeting the needs of users for data and information products. View brochures and posters, reports and documents related to IODE activities.

links.title: South African Data Centre for Oceanography (SADCO)
links.description: Stores, retrieves and manipulates multi-disciplinary marine information from the areas around southern Africa.  Hosted by the South African CSIR Stellenbosch and funded by a number of marine organisations in South Africa and Namibia.

links.title: Physical Oceanography.Distributed Active Archive Centre (PO.DAAC)
links.description: The NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory PO.DAAC is responsible for archiving and distributing data relevant to the physical state of the ocean. Browse sea surface temperature, sea surface topography, and ocean vector winds data acquired by NASA instruments.

links.title: NOAA Tropical Atmosphere Ocean Project
links.description: Real-time data from moored ocean buoys for improved detection, understanding, and prediction of El Niño and La Niña.

links.title: National Data Buoy Center (NDBC)
links.description: Designs, develops, operates, and maintains a United States network of data collecting buoys and coastal stations. Search recent and historical data and observations.

links.title: Hellenic National Oceanographic Data Centre (HNODC)
links.description: The Greek national agency for processing, archiving and distributing marine data. HNODC develops techniques for oceanographic data processing and data base maintenance. Review European marine projects, and request and submit marine data.

links.title: CLIVAR & Carbon Hydrographic Data Office
links.description: CCHDO manages CTD, carbon and tracer data for the US Repeat Hydrography Program. Data can be searched geographically using an interactive map tool.

811754.title: Data and Information Resources
811754.description: Sites consisting of data and information resources in the field of Oceanography.

links.title: Sonia's Oceanographic Lessons
links.description: Familiarize yourself with the Antarctic marine ecosystem, hydrothermal vent communities and eelgrass habitats. The site contains lesson information, resource links, a student activity, and a self grading test with detailed answer sheet and remedial links, to help students assess their knowledge.

links.title: PBS Online: Savage Seas
links.description: Offers a collection of informative pieces and activities centered around the world's oceans. Divided into four principal sections, each of which features an article, brief sidebars, video clips, and in some cases, animations.

links.title: Sea Friends Oceanography
links.description: A complete tutorial about atmosphere, climate, waves, currents, tides, beaches, sediment transport, storms, tsunamis.

links.title: Marine Environmental Data and Information Network
links.description: Develops, coordinates, maintains, and makes available inventories of marine data; develops guidelines for oceanographic data management; improves mechanisms to facilitate data exchange and the availability of this data for research and wealth creation.

links.title: Ocean Biodiversity Information System
links.description: An online, open-access, globally-distributed network of systematic, ecological, and environmental information systems. Collectively, these systems operate as a dynamic, global digital atlas to communicate biological information about the worlds oceans.

links.title: GulfBase
links.description: Resource database for Gulf of Mexico research.  It includes research institutions, researchers, research projects, and other information about the Gulf, from the U.S., Mexico, and Cuba.

links.title: NOAA's Coral Reef Information System
links.description: Designed to be a single point of access to NOAA coral reef information and data products, especially those derived from NOAA's Coral Reef Initiative Program. CoRIS will evolve and grow in the months ahead to encompass an ever widening array of product and information offerings.

links.title: NOAA Ocean Explorer
links.description: An educational internet offering for all who wish to learn about, discover, and virtually explore the ocean realm.

links.title: Indian Ocean Oceanography and Climatology Gateway
links.description: Extensive links to Indian Ocean resources, bibliography, and FAQ.

links.title: European Centre for Information on Marine Science and Technology
links.description: The EurOcean Internet portal is a focal point of information for all actors with interest in marine science and technology. It provides information in three main domains: marine research infrastructures, national and European RTD programmes.

links.title: Marine Information Service (MARIS)
links.description: Organisation based in the Netherlands that provides systems and projects for information and data related to the sea. Explore current and planned projects.

links.title: Ocean Networks Canada
links.description: A cabled ocean observatory designed as an undersea laboratory for ocean researchers, led by the University of Victoria, BC, Canada. View real time data plots and image and video archives.

links.title: Deep Sea Waters
links.description: Provides information on the oceans, the creatures that live there, deep sea exploration and research.

links.title: Careers in Oceanography, Marine Science and Marine Biology
links.description: General career guides for oceanography and marine scientists including guides for marine biology, marine mammal work, zoos and aquariums.

links.title: Satellite Oceanography Laboratory
links.description: Aims to promote satellite oceanography as an essential tool to study large to meso scale dynamical features in the South Atlantic Ocean. Includes articles, data and course materials. In Portuguese and English.

links.title: Permanent Service for Mean Sea Level
links.description: The global data bank for long term sea level change information from tide gauges.

links.title: SeaLifeBase
links.description: Searchable directory of sea life. Sorted by topic, location, family, ecosystem, common and scientific name. Served by University of British Columbia, Canada and Swedish Museum of Natural History.

links.title: Tidal Bore Research Society
links.description: A catalog of known bores with details and photos for some. Solicits information from users to add to the list.

links.title: Sea Data Net
links.description: Pan-European site offering a directory of research projects, data sets and collection guidelines.

links.title: Tides & Currents
links.description: Provides immediate graphical and tabular water level and meteorological data from U.S. National Ocean Service water level stations located along the projected path of severe storms such as hurricanes.

links.title: Bridge Ocean Education
links.description: Offers a collection of teacher-reviewed marine education resources that provides educators with a source of information on marine science topics.

links.title: Argo
links.description: An international program using autonomous floats to collect temperature, salinity and current data. It aims to provide a quantitative description of the changing state of the upper ocean and the patterns of ocean climate.

links.title: CoastLearn
links.description: Multimedia distance training package on Integrated Coastal Zone Management. Includes documentation.

links.title: International Earth Rotation and Reference Systems Service
links.description: The IERS collects, calculates, analyzes, archives, and distributes data relating to non-tidal changes in oceanic processes affecting the Earth's rotation, deformation, gravitational field, and geocenter.

links.title: Geo-Seas
links.description: Geological and geophysical data from the ocean basins and European continental waters, held at European institutions.

links.title: Scripps Institution of Oceanography - News
links.description: Known for its preeminence in scientific disciplines relating to biology, physics, chemistry, climatology, geosciences, and geophysics. Includes articles, videos and archives.

links.title: Tide Gauge Readings
links.description: Access to the UK Tide Gauge Network data holdings maintained at the British Oceanographic Data Centre (BODC).

links.title: SeaLevel.info
links.description: Provides consolidated sea-level information and analysis from multiple sources. Resources and climate related links.

links.title: Aviso+
links.description: Distributes satellite altimetry data. Data is used to study ocean dynamics and geophysics in climate prediction, monitoring of mean sea level, global warming, El Niño and La Niña events, marine currents and ocean circulation, and marine modeling.

811755.title: Journals
811755.description: Oceanographic Journals, Magazines and other regular publications.

links.title: Bulletin of Marine Science
links.description: Publishes research dealing with the tropical and subtropical waters of the world's oceans and marine science. Published by the Rosenstiel School of Marine and Atmospheric Science, University of Miami.

links.title: Oceanologia
links.description: Quarterly journal of basic research in marine sciences with emphasis on Northern Europe. The complete texts of all articles are available in PDF format from No. 42(1)/00 onwards.

links.title: Ocean News & Technology Magazine
links.description: Reports on the latest ocean industry news, events and technology developments around the world. Published bi-monthly.

links.title: International Ocean Systems
links.description: European-based magazine which is distributed worldwide. It covers the field of ocean data gathering, underwater surveying, and instrumentation. Profile, current issue.

links.title: Limnology and Oceanography
links.description: Peer-reviewed journal publishing original articles about all aspects of limnology and oceanography, with a theme of understanding aquatic ecosystems. Published by The American Society of Limnology and Oceanography (ASLO). Includes some articles.

links.title: Marine and Freshwater Research
links.description: An international journal for marine, estuarine or freshwater research.  All content is online.

links.title: Oceanography
links.description: The official magazine of the Oceanography Society aims to promote and chronicle all aspects of ocean science and its applications. It publishes brief articles, news and reviews. Lists of contents and online archive of articles.

links.title: Acta Ichthyologica et Piscatoria
links.description: AIeP (founded in 1970) is an international, English-language journal for ichthyology and fisheries. Available online in PDF format.

links.title: Glaucus
links.description: Journal of the British Marine Life Study Society. Contents list and sample articles.

links.title: Deep Sea Research Part I
links.description: Takes an interdisciplinary approach to oceanography. Publishes the results of original scientific research, the solution of instrumental problems, and new laboratory methods in the marine sciences. Tables of contents and abstracts; full text by subscription.

links.title: Deep Sea Research Part II: Topical Studies in Oceanography
links.description: Publishes topical issues from international and interdisciplinary projects in oceanography and also collections of papers presented at conferences. Tables of contents and abstracts; full text available by subscription.

links.title: Oceanographic Literature Review
links.description: An annotated bibliography to the international research literature in all fields of oceanography including science, mathematics and methods as well as policy, laws, economics and resource management. It contains some 8000 citations per annum, all accompanied by an abstract.

links.title: Oceanologica Acta
links.description: A scientific journal of French origin, with an international audience. Articles in French and English, with abstracts in both languages.

links.title: Journal of Plankton Research
links.description: Publishes papers dealing with both zoo and phytoplankton, in marine, freshwater and brackish environments. Published by Oxford University Press.

links.title: Ocean Science
links.description: International online and open-access journal on all aspects of ocean science.

links.title: Marine Ecology Progress Series
links.description: Serves as a worldwide forum for all aspects of marine ecology, fundamental and applied. The journal covers: microbiology, botany, zoology, ecosystem research, biological oceanography, ecological aspects of fisheries and aquaculture, pollution, environmental protection, conservation, resource management.

links.title: Deep Diving in Submarine Canyons
links.description: Personal narrative of Delta submersible diving in Southern California's submarine canyons.

links.title: Journal of Geophysical Research: Oceans
links.description: An interdisciplinary journal containing original contributions on the physics and chemistry of the Earth, its environment, and the solar system. Publication of the American Geophysical Union (AGU).

links.title: Marine Biology
links.description: International journal on life in oceans and coastal waters. Print and online versions.

links.title: Ocean Dynamics
links.description: Publishes articles with an interdisciplinary character that encompass research in the fields of biological, chemical and physical oceanography from a theoretical, computational and/or observational perspective.

links.title: Marine Geophysical Research
links.description: An international journal for the study of the earth beneath the sea.

links.title: Geo-Marine Letters
links.description: An international journal for the publication of short, original studies and reviews dealing with all marine geological aspects. Online and print versions.

links.title: Ocean Challenge
links.description: The journal of the Challenger Society for Marine Science aims to keep its readers up to date with what is happening in oceanography in the UK and the rest of Europe.

links.title: Marine Geodesy
links.description: Topics cover topography and mapping, satellite altimetry, bathymetry, positioning, precise navigation, boundary demarcation and determination, tsunamis, plate/tectonics, geoid determination, acoustics and space instrumentation, ground truth, and system calibration.

links.title: Journal of Marine Systems
links.description: Aims to provide a medium of exchange for those engaged in marine research where there exists an interplay between geology, chemistry, biology, and physics. Tables of contents and abstracts; full text by subscription.

links.title: Dynamics of Atmospheres and Oceans
links.description: Publishes research articles on the fluid dynamics of atmospheres and oceans and their interactions, on related basic dynamical processes, and on climatic and biogeochemical problems in which the fluid dynamics play an essential role. Tables of contents and abstracts; full text by subscription.

links.title: Journal of Sea Research
links.description: An international and multidisciplinary periodical on marine research, with an emphasis on marine ecosystems. An Elsevier Science Journal published in collaboration with the Netherlands Institute for Sea Research (NIOZ).

links.title: Marine Geology
links.description: An international journal reporting on developments in the fields of marine geology, geochemistry and geophysics. Tables of contents and abstracts; full text by subscription.

links.title: Progress in Oceanography
links.description: Publishes the longer, more comprehensive papers on the topic. The articles cover the entire spectrum of disciplines within the science of oceanography.

links.title: Continental Shelf Research
links.description: Concentrates on the results of original research in physical oceanography, chemistry, ecology, and sedimentology together with contributions on more applied aspects of continental shelf research.

links.title: Marine Environmental Research
links.description: Publishes original research papers on chemical, physical, and biological interactions in the oceans and coastal waters. Tables of contents and abstracts; full text by subscription.

links.title: Ocean Modelling Online
links.description: A rapid-response refereed journal for the Marine Science community. Tables of contents and abstracts; full text by subscription.

links.title: Estuarine, Coastal and Shelf Science
links.description: An international multidisciplinary journal devoted to the analysis of saline water phenomena ranging from the outer edge of the continental shelf to the upper limits of the tidal zone. Tables of contents and abstracts; full text by subscription.

links.title: Applied Ocean Research
links.description: Encourages the submission of papers that advance the state of knowledge in a range of topics relevant to ocean engineering. Tables of contents and abstracts; full text by subscription.

links.title: Marine Pollution Bulletin
links.description: Concerned with the rational use of maritime and marine resources in estuaries, the seas and oceans, as well as with documenting marine pollution and introducing new forms of measurement and analysis.

links.title: Ocean Engineering
links.description: Publishes original research and development work in this field. Tables of contents and abstracts; full text by subscription.

links.title: Ocean and Coastal Management
links.description: An international journal published 12 times per year dedicated to the study of all aspects of ocean and coastal management at international, national, regional, and local levels. Tables of contents and abstracts; full text by subscription.

links.title: Hakai Magazine
links.description: Explores science, society, and the environment in narratives that highlight coastal life and phenomena.

links.title: Marine Science and Technology Bulletin
links.description: A double-blind peer-reviewed and open-access journal publishing a variety of marine information, data, products, services, careers and advice. Includes access to articles and archives.

811753.title: Libraries
811753.description: Libraries and virtual libraries concerned with oceanography. Also contains links to bibliographic sites.

links.title: Department of Environmental & Ocean Engineering Library, University of Tokyo
links.description: Contains limited information at this time (site under test).

links.title: National Marine Biological Library
links.description: The NMBL contains one of the world's major collections of literature on aquatic sciences and fisheries, and acts as a marine biological sciences resource for the UK.

links.title: National Academies - Marine
links.description: The National Academy of Sciences and National Research Council reports and summaries on marine-related topics. Includes reading and downloading options.

links.title: Clark, Jenifer
links.description: Realtime ocean charts for sailboat racing, boat deliveries, ocean cruising, and offshore fishing. Using infrared imagery, satellite altimetry data, and surface isotherm data, oceanographic analyses are produced and available for the Gulf Stream area and all the major currents of the world.

links.title: Ocean Expert (GLODIR)
links.description: Database, developed and maintained by the Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of UNESCO (IOC), containing information on individuals involved in all aspects of Marine or Freshwater Research and Management.

links.title: Pullen, Julie
links.description: Director of the Maritime Security Laboratory at Stevens Institute of Technology; uses high-resolution coupled ocean-atmosphere modeling with a particular emphasis on predicting chemical, biological, and radiological (CBR) dispersion in coastal cities.

links.title: Nof, Doron
links.description: Work focuses on the movement of fluids within the ocean and its relationship to the interaction with the atmosphere above.

links.title: Rahmstorf, Prof. Dr. Stefan
links.description: Professor of Physics of the Oceans at Potsdam University. Publications, lectures, CV and photograph album; contact information.

links.title: Holfort, Jurgen
links.description: Presents their research into freshwater transport from the Arctic into the Atlantic along the East Greenland current. Includes Matlab routines useful to oceanographers.

links.title: Klymak, Jody
links.description: Physical oceanographer interested in small scale physics and its impact on circulation and the transport of tracers in the ocean.

links.title: Sukardi, Yuliarko
links.description: Provides details of a study of the development of a high-order numerical model to solve incompressible water wave motion based on improved nonlinear dispersive Boussinesq equations.

links.title: Guillaume Maze
links.description: Access research interests, publications, technical reports, data, and toolboxes for physical oceanography, meteorology and climate studies.

links.title: Ruddick, Barry
links.description: Interests cover the areas of oceanic mixing processes, internal waves and geophysical flows.

links.title: Sheng, Jinyu
links.description: Ocean modeling and prediction and shelf circulation studies.

links.title: Thompson, Keith
links.description: Ocean and shelf circulation and sea level variation researcher.

links.title: Greatbatch, Richard
links.description: Interests within the fields of climate change and ocean/atmosphere circulation.

links.title: Louden, Keith
links.description: Interests are within the field of marine geophysics.  Publication list.

links.title: Metaxas, Anna
links.description: Benthic ecology, larval dispersal, physical/biological interactions

links.title: Beaumont, Chris
links.description: Interests include geodynamics of orogens.

links.title: Cullen, John
links.description: Interested in phytoplankton processes, optical measurements, ultraviolet radiation.

links.title: Grant, Jonathan
links.description: Benthic ecology, shellfish biology, aquaculture.

links.title: Lewis, Marlon
links.description: Phytoplankton ecology, bio-optical oceanography, upper ocean physics

links.title: Hill, Paul
links.description: Interests in sediment transport, includes a publication list.

links.title: Hay, Alex
links.description: Researcher in acoustical oceanography, sediment dynamics and nearshore and coastal processes.

links.title: Kelley, Dan
links.description: Dynamics of transport and mixing process research.

links.title: Taggart, Christopher
links.description: Involved in active research both in the field and laboratory, focusing on physical, ecological biochemical and genetic influences on early life history and recruitment in fish and on fish population structure and distribution.

links.title: Society for Underwater Technology
links.description: Multi-disciplinary learned society which brings together individuals and organisations from more than 30 countries who have a common interest in underwater technology, ocean science and offshore engineering.

links.title: American Society of Limnology and Oceanography (ASLO)
links.description: The purposes of ASLO are to promote the interests of limnology, oceanography and related sciences, to foster the exchange of information across the range of aquatic science, and to further investigations dealing with these subjects. ASLO is best known for its journal, Limnology and Oceanography, its interdisciplinary meetings, and its special symposia.

links.title: The Oceanography Society
links.description: Founded in 1988 to disseminate knowledge of oceanography and its application through research and education and to promote communication among oceanographers.

links.title: Cetacean Society International
links.description: CSI is an all-volunteer, non-profit conservation, education, and research organization based in the USA, with volunteer representatives in 26 countries around the world. Dedicated to the preservation and protection of cetaceans and the marine environment on a global basis.

links.title: Marine Technology Society
links.description: A non-profit international professional organization established in 1963 to promote the exchange of information in ocean and marine engineering, science, and policy. MTS has over 2000 current members.

links.title: Oceanic Society
links.description: A nonprofit, membership organization founded in 1972 to protect marine mammals and the marine environment through conservation-based research and environmental education. The Society coordinates and funds research projects, the results of which make a compelling case for ecosystem conservation.

links.title: Coastal Research and Education Society of Long Island
links.description: Information about CRESLI's research, education, and outreach programs to promote stewardship and conservation of coastal ecosystems, and especially their marine mammals and sea turtles.

links.title: Shaw Institute
links.description: Committed to the health and well being of marine mammals and their coastal habitats around the world.

links.title: The Hydrographic Society of America
links.description: Serves as the focal point for activities in America. Membership is open to any individual or organization with an interest in surveying afloat.

links.title: The International Federation of Hydrographic Societies (IFHS)
links.description: Membership is open to all with an interest in surveying at sea. It aims to promote the science of surveying over water as well as the fostering of recognised standards of education and training for those engaged in hydrographic work.

links.title: ANalyse Educatie en Marien Oecologisch ONderzoek (ANEMOON)
links.description: A society for people interested in marine biology near the coast of the Netherlands. The fact that ANEMOON is strictly for amateurs does not prevent a very professional approach. There are many people that help in the gathering and processing of data on the organisms that are found. ANEMOON already has an impressive database and a long list of publications to their credit.

links.title: Marine and Oceanographic Technology Network
links.description: MOTN is a regional association comprised of various members of the marine and oceanographic community located throughout the New England area.

links.title: Institute of Marine Engineering, Science and Technology (IMarEST)
links.description: International multi-disciplinary professional body established to meet the needs of engineers, scientists and technologists.

links.title: Whale and Dolphin Conservation

links.title: UK Marine Special Areas of Conservation
links.description: The vast coastline and seas around the UK have a remarkable marine natural heritage and provide rich resources for both work and recreation. These are treasures that need to be safeguarded and the UK Marine SACs Project is playing a major role in achieving this.

links.title: Continuous Plankton Recorder Survey (CPR)
links.description: Sir Alister Hardy Foundation for Ocean Science runs the Continuous Plankton Recorder survey, a long term plankton survey in the North Atlantic and North Sea. The database is online.

links.title: New Millennium Observatory Network (NeMO NeT)
links.description: Hydrothermal vent monitoring - links instruments and a camera located within the caldera of a submarine volcano to the Internet.

links.title: NEPTUNE Canada
links.description: The NorthEast Pacific Time-Series Undersea Networked Experiments project is a regional-scale ocean observatory for interactive, real-time, long term ocean and earth studies and is led in Canada by the University of Victoria.

links.title: Seasearch
links.description: UK project for volunteer sports divers who have an interest in what they're seeing under water, want to learn more and want to help protect the marine environment.  The main aim is to map out the various types of sea bed found in the near-shore zone, up to about 5 miles off the coast or 30m depth around the whole of the British Isles.

links.title: Guinea Current Large Marine Ecosystem (GCLME)
links.description: Aims to assist countries adjacent to the Guinea Current ecosystem to achieve environmental and resource sustainability.

links.title: Estimating the Circulation and Climate of the Ocean (ECCO)
links.description: A consortium formed by a group of scientists at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL), the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) and the Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO) with the technical goal of the sustained production and evaluation of continuing three-dimensional estimates of the global state of the ocean in near-real time in support programs such as GODAE and CLIVAR.

links.title: Future Earth Coasts
links.description: The LOICZ Project focuses on the area of the earth's surface where land, ocean and atmosphere meet and interact. The overall goal of this project is to determine at regional and global scales: the nature of that dynamic interaction; how changes in various components of the Earth system are affecting coastal zones and altering their role in global cycles; to assess how future changes in these areas will affect their use by people; to provide a sound scientific basis for future integrated management of coastal areas on a sustainable basis.

links.title: Atmospheric Deposition and Impact (ADIOS)
links.description: Created to study the impact of the atmosphere pollutants and natural substances affects the biochemistry of the Mediterranean Sea.  Page includes current problems, approach methods and objectives of the study.

links.title: Cornell Morocco Project
links.description: Cooperative research between Cornell University, Morocco and Spain to study the geodynamics of the western Mediterranean (Alboran) region.  Page includes current projects and completed research summaries.

links.title: RAPID Meridional Overturning Circulation data (RAPIDMOC)
links.description: Near real time data from key moorings, deployed as part of a monitoring array at 26.5°N to measure the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation. Part of the NERC Rapid Climate Change programme.

links.title: Coastal Observatory, Liverpool Bay (COBS)
links.description: Coastal Observatory built on real-time measurements and model predictions with particular focus on the Irish Sea and Liverpool Bay hosted by the Proudman Oceanographic Laboratory.

links.title: Acoustic Thermometry of Ocean Climate (ATOC)
links.description: Summary of research of experiments to record temperatures in the ocean in order to verify existing climate models by using sound.  An additional study was conducted to see what impact the underwater noise had on marine animals.

links.title: Coriolis
links.description: French project for operational oceanography with the objective of developing automatic and permanent observation networks. Find project description, news and contacts.

links.title: Significance of Anthropogenic Nitrogen for Central Baltic Sea N-cycling (SIGNAL)
links.description: Addresses the question of eutrophication sources and what impact additional nitrogen has on the productivity in remote regions. Find project objectives, methods, results and photos.

links.title: Global Sea Level Observing System (GLOSS)
links.description: GLOSS aims at the establishment of high quality global and regional sea level networks for application to climate, oceanographic and coastal sea level research. The programme became known as GLOSS as it provides data for deriving the 'Global Level of the Sea Surface'.

links.title: Joint Global Ocean Flux Study (JGOFS)
links.description: An international programme to assess more accurately, and understand better the processes controlling, regional to global and seasonal to interannual fluxes of carbon   between the atmosphere, surface ocean and ocean interior, and their sensitivity to climate changes.

links.title: Baltic Sea Experiment (BALTEX)
links.description: A cage experiment to assess the total heat and water flux divergence of the BALTEX area. The basic BALTEX programme elements include numerical modelling, data assimilation, experimental and numerical process studies, re-analysis of existing data sets, and application of remote sensing.

links.title: General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans (GEBCO)
links.description: Consists of an international group of experts who work on the  development of a range of publicly-available bathymetric data sets and seafloor topography products. View data and products and learn of the available training opportunities.

links.title: Nucleus for European Modelling of the Ocean
links.description: NEMO is a modeling framework for oceanographic research and operational oceanography. It allows ocean related components (ocean dynamics, ice, biogeochemisty) to work together and to be interfaced with the component of the earth system.

links.title: Marine Research Aquarium
links.description: Information on the building of a marine aquarium for propagation of coral. Site also tells how to collect specimens and create a chemical/biological/physical environment conducive to coral growth in an automated artificial environment.

links.title: ArcticNet
links.description: Collaborative effort joins Canadian university researchers and government officials with scientists from Japan, Europe, Russia and the US to study the impacts of climate change in the coastal Canadian Arctic.

links.title: Surface Ocean Lower Atmosphere Study (SOLAS)
links.description: A new international research initiative which has as its goal: 'To achieve quantitative understanding of the key biogeochemical-physical interactions and feedbacks between the ocean and the atmosphere, and how this coupled system affects and is affected by climate and environmental change'.

links.title: Alfred Wegener Institute: Marine, Coastal and Polar Systems
links.description: The PACES project aims to identify the role of processes at high latitudes on past, current and future changes of the Earth system.

811839.title: Paleozoic
811839.description: The Paleozoic, or "Old Life", Era is sometimes called the "Age of Fishes." It began with the Cambrian Explosion, a short period of time in which an enormous diversification of complex life occurred, and ended with the great Permian/Triassic mass extinction. It is composed of the Cambrian, Ordovician, Silurian, Devonian, Carboniferous (Mississippian and Pennsylvanian in North America), and Permian Periods.    This category is for any website dealing with the Paleozoic fossil record.

811847.title: Cambrian
811847.description: The Cambrian marks the beginning of the Phanerozoic, the age of complex life. While living things have a fossil record going back several million years, complex life forms diversified at a dizzying pace in the Cambrian. The Cambrian fauna includes many familiar groups, but also includes a large number of extinct, and very unusual, fossil taxa.    This category is for any website dealing with the Cambrian Period.

Submissions for this category should relate to the animal and plant life of the Carboniferous period.

811844.title: Devonian
811844.description: The Devonian Period, 410 to 360 million years ago, is best known as the "age of fishes".   While it's true that fish experienced an explosive radiation at this time, it also marked a major change in the terrestrial ecosystem as life began to move wholesale from the water to the land.   This period saw the widespread colonization of the land by vascular plants and the formation of the first forests, while beneath their spreading branches the newly evolved tetrapod animals took their first tentative steps out of the water.

811848.title: Proterozoic
811848.description: The Proterozoic, or the Age of First Life, encompasses most of the history of earth, from the time of the oldest preserved fossils to the Cambrian explosion. In general, the fossil organisms are less complex than those found later in life, and the preserved ecosystems are also simpler than later life assemblages.   Such economically important deposits as the various Banded Iron formations, and biologically important deposits as the first stromatolites, are Proterozoic in age.

links.description: University of British Columbia class with some very interesting "break-out" material (some pages require passwords to view figures).

812010.description: This category is for website for undergraduate and graduate classes in invertebrate paleontology.

links.title: Paleontology (U. Mass)
links.description: GEO 341, University of Massachusetts

links.title: Invertebrate Paleontology and Paleoecology
links.description: Constance M. Soja's class at Colgate covering the taxonomy, morphology and paleoecology of the organismal groups found in the geologic record.

links.title: Invertebrate Paleontology
links.description: Class in invertebrate paleontology at the United Arab Emirates University.

812012.title: Pre-College
812012.description: A list of sites with educational resources for elementary, middle, and high school teachers. Most sites contain suggestions for paleontology exercises geared toward K-12 classrooms, but many can also be adapted to home schooling.

links.title: Permian Park
links.description: A geology and earth science site with 'five minute geology lesson', the facts and figures,the pictures, and links to other geology sites.

links.title: Dinosaurs Lessons
links.description: Grade school lesson plans covering dinosaurs and extinction. With Spanish translations.

812013.title: Dinosaurs
812013.description: This category is for educational material about dinosaurs aimed toward primary, secondary, and high school students.

links.title: Dinosaurs and Us Unit
links.description: Elementary and middle school exercise

811853.title: Extinction
811853.description: Most animals and plants that ever lived died out long before the present. The fossil record reveals that there are several periods of time in the earth's past when the extinction rate was very high (e.g., at the Cretaceous/Tertiary boundary, and the Permian/Triassic boundary) - causing mass extinctions of a large percentage of the species.   This category contains sites dealing with the subjects of extinction and mass extinctions in the fossil record.

links.title: The Late Devonian Mass Extinction
links.description: A professional technical paper discussing whether the Late Devonian (Frasnian-Famennian) mass extinction was initiated by an extraterrestrial impact or an earth-bound event.

links.title: Extinctions: Cycles of Life and Death Through Time
links.description: Covers patterns and periodicity of extinction, with discussions of major mass extinctions and minor extinction events.

links.title: Animal Extinctions in the Fossil Record: A Developmental Paradigm
links.description: Article by Vaclav Petr discussing the possible causes of extinctions.

links.title: Our Nemesis?
links.description: Article on a paper by David Raup and John Sepkoski, two respected paleontologists, making the remarkable claim that great catastrophes occur on the Earth every 26 million years,

links.title: The Role of Extinction in Evolution
links.description: Paper by David M Raup, Department of Geophysical Sciences, University of Chicago.

links.title: The Cosmic Clock, the Cycle of Terrestrial Mass Extinctions
links.description: Paper by J. A. Marusek. A dual cycle of extinction events is observed and well ordered in geological time. Two primary mechanisms, Oort cloud comet impacts and nearby supernova events are synchronized to the passage of the solar system through the spiral arms of the Milky Way galaxy.

811854.title: Cretaceous-Tertiary
811854.description: This category is for websites dealing with the scientific study of the end-Mesozoic mass extinction.

links.title: The Great Mystery
links.description: Information on current and past hypotheses on dinosaur extinctions from the University of California Paleontology Museum.

links.title: Dinosaurs and Extinctions
links.description: From the Classroom of the Future website. Includes an introduction to the major theories on the Cretaceous-Tertiary extinction event.

links.title: Science Daily: A World Ruled By Fungi
links.description: After the extinction event, the dominant life form was the fungi that thrived in the dark. Researchers have constructed a timeline of the fungal takeover and eventual replacement by resurgent plant life.

links.title: Dinosaurs' End: The Gravitational Hypothesis
links.description: An original, serious and well-argued theory by F.Malmartel explaining dinosaur extinction, especially why dinosaurs disappeared when other reptiles survived.

links.title: The Cretaceous Extinction
links.description: 85 percent of all species died in the K-T extinction at the end of the Cretaceous period. This article provides information on the geological setting, the species affected and the possible causes of the event.

links.title: The K-T Extinction
links.description: Essay by Richard Cowen about the mass extinction of many species that occurred at the end of the Cretaceous Period and how the catastrophe hypotheses hold up to scrutiny.

links.title: Timing and Rate of the KT Extinction: What Else Died Out?
links.description: Article by Pete Goddard on this subject covering the sea, the land and the air, and coming to the conclusion that the evidence points to a single catastrophic event.

811855.title: Impact Theory
811855.description: This category is for websites dealing with the theory that the impact of an extraterrestrial object led to the end-Mesozoic mass extinction.

links.title: The Cretaceous-tertiary Extinction Bolide
links.description: Article from Science Frontiers Online arguing that the discovery of a worldwide iridium-rich layer is supporting evidence for the collision of an asteroid or comet with the earth about 65 million years ago.

811856.title: Permian-Triassic
811856.description: The extinction at the end of the Paleozoic was the largest recorded in the fossil record. Theories abound as to why this extinction occurred. The world was irrevocably changed after this event, which marked the end of many characteristically Paleozoic lineages. This category is for sites specifically dealing with this extinction.

links.title: Permian-Triassic Extinction
links.description: Short video showing rock layers being laid down during the Permian and Triassic periods, and background information on the mass extinctions that occurred at this time.

links.title: Big Crater Seen beneath Ice Sheet
links.description: The BBC provides news that what appears to be a 480km-wide crater has been detected under the East Antarctic Ice Sheet and may have been responsible for the extinction at the boundary of the Permian and Triassic.

links.title: Great Extinction Came in Phases
links.description: BBC News describes how Chinese rock evidence suggests that the biggest of the Earth's mass extinctions did not happen in one cataclysmic event.

links.title: ThoughtCo - The Permian-Triassic Extinction
links.description: Article by Andrew Alden proposing that new evidence and old, both support a volcanic explanation for this mass extinction when nine tenths of all species disappeared.

links.title: The Great Permian Extinction Debate
links.description: Paper by James A. Marusek, providing a hypothesis of the mechanisms behind the greatest mass extinction of life on Earth, the Permian extinction. The hypothesis is applicable to 5 of the 6 Great mass extinction events that occurred at the end of the Botomian, Devonian, Permian, Triassic and Cretaceous Ages.

811768.title: Famous Localities
811768.description: Some fossil localities have become famous because of their exceptional fossil preservation. Sites dealing with these paleontological treasures can be found in this category.

links.title: Fossil Localities
links.description: Kuban's Paleo Place provides links to a number of famous fossil sites and formations.

811779.title: Burgess Shale
811779.description: The famous Burgess Shale of British Columbia contains an exceptionally well preserved Cambrian fauna. This group of animals, which are preserved primarily as carbon films, is one of the earliest nearly complete record of the age of complex life, and opens a window into an ecosystem that died out hundreds of millions of years ago.

links.title: The Yoho-Burgess Shale Foundation
links.description: The world's most significant fossil find. High in the  Canadian Rocky Mountains is a fossil bed that details life on Earth - 520 Million years ago.

links.title: The Burgess Shale
links.description: The Department of Paleobiology, National Museum of Natural History, provides an impressive exhibit of fossils.

811777.title: Europe
811777.description: This category contains subcategories for famous fossil collecting localities in Europe.

811780.title: Green River
811780.description: The Green River Formation outcrops in western Colorado, eastern Utah and southwestern Wyoming. The unit was deposited during the Eocene, and contains fossil fish, insects, and especially beautifully preserved plant fossils.

links.title: Fossil Butte National Monument
links.description: This 50-million year old lake bed is one of the richest fossil localities in the world.

links.title: Green River Formation
links.description: From the U.C. Museum of Paleontology

811771.title: La Brea
811771.description: Rancho La Brea is located in downtown Los Angeles, and has yielded an amazing assemblage of Pleistocene (Ice Age) fossil mammals.

links.title: George C. Page Museum
links.description: The George C. Page Museum is located at the Rancho La Brea Tar Pits, one of the world's most famous fossil localities, recognized for having an unusually diverse assemblage of extinct Ice Age plants and animals. Visitors learn about Los Angeles as it was between 10,000 and 40,000 years ago, during the last Ice Age, when animals such as Saber-Toothed cats and Mammoths roamed the Los Angeles Basin.

links.title: La Brea Tar Pits
links.description: From the U.C. Museum of Paleontology

811770.title: Mazon Creek
811770.description: Mazon Creek in Illinois contains concretions which, when cracked open, frequently contain beautifully preserved fossils. Both terrestrial and marine fossils have been recovered from Mazon Creek, including the enigmatic "Tully Monster" which is also the state fossil of Illinois. The deposit is Pennsylvanian in age.

links.title: Mazon Creek Fossils
links.description: This is Illinois State Museum's online exhibit of the famous Mazon Creek fossils. The Mazon Creek fossils include many soft-bodied organisms that are not usually preserved.

811773.title: Messel Oil Shale
811773.description: This category is for websites dealing with the world-famous Messel Oil Shale.

links.title: UNESCO World Heritage in Germany: Pit at Messel
links.description: Eocene fossils, particularly those of early horses, can be found at Grube Messel.

811776.title: Morrison Formation
811776.description: This category is for websites dealing with the world-famous Morrison Formation of western North America.

811778.title: North America
811778.description: This category contains subcategories for famous fossil collecting localities in North America.

811772.title: Petrified Forest
811772.description: This category is for websites dealing with the world-famous Petrified Forest of Arizona.

811775.title: Rhynie Chert
811775.description: This category is for websites dealing with the world-famous Rhynie Chert.

links.title: Rhynie Chert, Scotland
links.description: From the U.C. Museum of Paleontology

links.title: The Rhynie Chert Research Group
links.description: Ongoing research into the strtaigraphy, sedimentology and paleontology of an Early Devonian hot spring system. From the University of Aberdeen.

811769.title: Solnhofen
811769.description: The Solnhofen Limestone is a lithographic limestone quarried in Germany because of its fine grained characteristics. The quarriers frequently come across fossils preserved in exquisite detail in this fine grain matrix. Based on the odd behavior recorded by some marine organisms (e.g., horseshoe crabs running around in circles and then dying, preserving both the trackway and the body fossil), and the level of preservation, it has been suggested that the Solnhofen was deposited in an anoxic environment. The deposit is Jurassic in age.  Such famous taxa as _Archaeopteryx_ were first described from the Solnhofen.

links.title: The Solnhofen Limestone of Germany
links.description: Introductory information from the University of California Museum of Paleontology.

links.title: Solnhofen Lithographic Limestone
links.description: Information about the paleontology of the formation from the Hooper Virtual Natural History Museum.

links.title: Stiegler Natural Stone
links.description: Information about the Solnhofen Natural Stone and Jura Marble products from the company that owns the quarry.

811788.title: Fossil Collecting
811788.description: Collecting fossils is an enjoyable hobby for many enthusiasts. This category is for any website dealing with recreational fossil collecting.

links.description: Promotes collaboration between amateur and professional paleontologists. Multiple forums and places to post pictures.

links.title: Discovering Fossils
links.description: Locations and resources for collectors. Includes a beginner's guide.

links.title: Collecting Fossils
links.description: Basic information on fossil collecting. Includes links to related sites and a calendar for fossil shows in the US.

links.title: The Fossil Forum
links.description: Forum with galleries, location map and a chat room. Boards include general, fossil discussion, locations, geology and the media.

links.title: US Fossil Sites
links.description: Find fossil localities, museums and clubs organized by state via Google Maps.

links.title: Fossils Galore
links.description: Jamie Jordan is a young enthusiast who has been collecting fossils since he was four years old. Besides photographs of his collection, there is much information here and a link to the Fossil Forum which he has set up.

811790.title: Fossils
811790.description: This category contains links to major fossil groups listed in other parts of the directory. Please submit your site to the most appropriate subcategory.

811789.title: Legal Issues
811789.description: The issue of who owns fossil resources has been the subject of debate in recent years, especially with very valuable vertebrate fossils. This category is for websites dealing with fossil collecting laws, discussions of cases, and related legal issues.

links.title: Florida Fossil Permit
links.description: Permit needed to collect vertebrate fossils in Florida.

links.title: Public Lands, Public Fossils

811786.title: History

links.title: A History of Evolutionary Thought
links.description: Biographies of paleontology and evolutionary thinkers from the UCMP.

links.title: A History of Dinosaur Hunting
links.description: Dinosaur hunters and their discoveries, from Gideon Mantell and the changing shape of the Iguanodon to the present day

links.title: Strange Science: The Rocky Road to Modern Paleontology and Biology
links.description: A collection of misguided attempts to explain natural history, including honest and dishonest mistakes.

links.title: The UnMuseum: Dinosaurs of the Victorian Era
links.description: Article describing the discovery of bones of giant reptiles in the 1800's and the growing interest and rivalry that followed.

811787.title: Bone Wars
811787.description: In the mid-nineteenth century a nearly-complete dinosaur skeleton was found in New Jersey. This sparked interest in the search for dinosaur bones and two men, Edward Drinker Cope and Othniel Charles Marsh, began a vicious competition to see who could make the most significant discoveries. This has been called the Bone Wars.

links.title: The UnMuseum: Whatever Happened to the Brontosaurus?
links.description: Explains that the brontosaurus is actually an apatosaurus  with the head of a camarasaurus. It recounts how this happened.

links.title: Wikipedia: Bone Wars
links.description: Tells how Edward Drinker Cope and Othniel Charles Marsh came to compete in the discovery of dinosaur bones, and the havoc they caused.

links.title: Wyoming: The Bone Wars
links.description: An illustrated history of the Bone Wars. It includes photos taken from 1904 - 1934 and includes reproductions of engravings from 1871.

links.title: Haddonfield and the 'Bone Wars'
links.description: Information about how the war of dinosaur discovery between Edward Drinker Cope and Othniel Charles Marsh began in Haddonfield, N.J. in 1868.

links.title: Crabs

links.title: The Dead Bug in Amber Club
links.description: For the lover of amber and the dead creatures encased in a golden tomb.

links.title: Did the Wood Roach or Prototermite Cause the Permian-Triassic Coal Hiatus?
links.description: Hypothesis that the symbiosis of the wood roach with a cellulose digesting protozoa caused the early Triassic coal hiatus.

links.title: Fossil Diptera Catalog

links.title: Palaeoentomology in Russia

links.title: Insect Fossils Classification and Hexapoda

links.title: Introduction to the Trilobita
links.description: UCMP Berkeley introduction to the trilobite fossil record,  ecology, systematics and morphology.

links.title: Trilobites - Utah Geological Survey
links.description: Trilobites and the Cambrian Environment of Utah, an essay by Rebecca L. Hylland.

links.description: The Natural History Museum's online exhibit of several well-preserved trilobite taxa discovered in 2003 in Morocco.

links.title: Rolled Trilobites
links.description: Photograpp of a collection of rolled up trilobites.

links.title: Calliprotonia sterlitamakensis
links.description: Photograph of a nice specimen showing the pattern of spine growth well.

links.title: Brachiopods

links.title: Rhombopora diaphragmata
links.description: Several photographs of this small twig bryozoan with rectangular chambers arranged in regular rows along the branch.

links.title: Tabulipora maculosa
links.description: Photographs of several nice specimens of branches of this bryozoan including a cross section.

811995.title: Echinoderms

links.description: Provides photographs and information on echinoids, or sea urchins, the arrival of regular species in the fossil record in the Cambrian and the appearance of irregular ones in the Jurassic.

links.title: Echinoderms

This category is for any website which deals specifically with the fossil record of sponges. Sponges are animals, most of which live in salt water, attached to another surface, so they remain in one place. Their scientific classification is kingdom animalia and phylum porifera.

811976.title: Paleobotany
811976.description: Paleobotany is the branch of paleontology dealing with the recovery and identification of plant remains from geological contexts, their use for the biological reconstruction of past environments and the understanding of the evolution of plants. Paleobotany includes the study of terrestrial plant fossils, as well as the study of prehistoric marine photosynthetic algae or seaweeds.

Palynology can be applied in many fields of study including geology, botany, paleontology, archaeology and geography.

Information in this category should help with  that, but it is not intended to provide shortcuts to do projects in the least amount of time (with the least effort) possible. 816948.title: Air Dispersion Modeling
816948.description: In the context of this "Air Dispersion Modeling" category, air dispersion models may be defined as computerized mathematical calculations for predicting the dispersion behavior of air pollutants emitted into the atmosphere.    The many types of air dispersion models include those for modeling: the continuous emission of buoyant pollutant plumes; the non-continuous accidental releases of either   buoyant or heavier-than-air (i.e., dense gas) pollutants;   puff emissions; point-source emissions; area-source or line-source emissions; mobile transportation-source emissions; fire and smoke emission models; etc. Air quality models for urban airsheds are probably best placed in the "Air Quality" category rather than in this "Air Dispersion" category.    Sources for air dispersion modeling information include governmental agencies, research institutes, university faculty and post-graduate students, environmental consultants, industrial dispersion modeling practitioners, and pollution meteorologists.

links.description: The activities of the Air Quality Research department at the Finnish Meteorological Institute (FMI) include atmospheric dispersion modeling for: urban air quality, regional and long-range transport, and accidents involving hazardous materials.

The ARL also supports other U.S. agencies. In particular, the ARL's Atmospheric Turbulence and Diffusion Division (ATTD) and Atmospheric Sciences Modeling Division (ASMD) support the U.S. EPA in developing regulatory air dispersion models.

816950.title: Software
816950.description: In the context of this "Air Dispersion Modeling/Software" category, air dispersion modeling software may be defined as computerized mathematical calculations for predicting the dispersion behavior of air pollutants emitted into the atmosphere.   The many types of air dispersion models include those for modeling: the continuous emission of buoyant pollutant plumes; the non-continuous accidental releases of either buoyant or heavier-than-air (i.e., dense gas) pollutants; puff emissions; point-source emissions; area-source or line-source emissions; mobile transportation-source emissions; fire and smoke emission models; etc. Air quality modeling software for urban airsheds are probably best placed in the "Air Quality" category rather than in this "Air Dispersion" category.   Sources for air dispersion modeling software include governmental agencies, research institutes, university faculty and post-graduate students, environmental consultants, industrial dispersion modeling practitioners, and pollution meteorologists.

817059.title: Biodiversity
817059.description:
Biodiversity is not easily defined. Try What is Biodiversity? and Defining The 'B' Word for approaches with differing emphases. Below is a definition adapted from the World Resources Institute, World Conservation Union, and United Nations Environment Programme in Global Biodiversity Strategy 1992.

"Biodiversity is the totality of genes, species, and ecosystems in a region... Biodiversity can be divided into three hierarchical categories -- genes, species, and ecosystems -- that describe quite different aspects of living systems and that scientists measure in different ways.

Genetic diversity refers to the variation of genes within species. This covers distinct populations of the same species (such as the thousands of traditional rice varieties in India) or genetic variation within a populations (high among Indian rhinos, and very low among cheetahs) ...

Species diversity refers to the variety of species within a region. Such diversity can be measured in many ways, and scientists have not settled on a single best method. The number of species in a region -- its species richness -- is one often- used measure, but a more precise measurement, taxonomic diversity, also considers the relationship of species to each other. For example, an island with two species of birds and one species of lizard has a greater taxonomic diversity than an island with three species of birds but no lizards ...

Ecosystem diversity is harder to measure than species or genetic diversity because the boundaries of communities -- associations of species -- and ecosystems are elusive. Nevertheless, as long as a consistent set of criteria is used to define communities and ecosystems, their numbers and distribution can be measured ..."

Resources related to biodiversity or conservation as an issue or a topic of debate belong primarily in the relevant subcategory of Society/Issues/Environment.

Related: (very comprehensive guide) Where should I submit my website about animals? Or, where will I find the animal topic I am looking for?

817062.title: Agricultural
817062.description: Agricultural Biodiversity, sometimes called 'Agrobiodiversity', encompasses the variety and variability of animals, plants and micro-organisms which are necessary to sustain key functions of the agro-ecosystem, its structure and processes for, and in support of, food production and food security.   Agricultural Biodiversity provides: i. Sustainable production of food and other agricultural products emphasising both strengthening sustainability in production systems at all levels of intensity and improving the conservation, sustainable use and enhancement of the diversity of all genetic resources for food and agriculture, especially plant and animal genetic resources, in all types of production systems.  ii. Biological or life support to production emphasising conservation, sustainable use and enhancement of the biological resources that support sustainable production systems, particularly soil biota, pollinators and predators.  iii. Ecological and social services provided by agro-ecosystems such as landscape and wildlife protection, soil protection and health (fertility, structure and function), water cycle and water quality, air quality, CO2 sequestration, etc.
