Illustrates how food sovereignty and security, livelihoods, landscapes and environmental integrity are underpinned by agricultural biodiversity and its component genetic resources for food and agriculture. Summarises an Action Agenda to confront threats.

links.title: Understanding Agricultural Biodiversity - Vol 1 (2003)
links.description: This first volume of the UPWARD three-volume publication is a global compilation by scientists, development specialists, academics, policy-makers and donors. Other volumes: Vol. 2: strengthening local management of agricultural biodiversity, and Vol. 3: ensuring an enabling environment for agricultural biodiversity.

links.title: Future Earth absorbs DIVERSITAS
links.description: DIVERSITAS and their core projects have now been absorbed by Future Earth. It was an international program that brought together biological, ecological and social scientists to consider how biodiversity evolved in space and time, how much diversity exists and how scientific investigation can support policy and decision making This work continues in, for example, Future Earth's Planetary Boundaries programne.

links.title: Biodiverse Agriculture for a Changing Climate
links.description: Briefing summarising solutions to climate change challenges through using more biodiverse, ecological approaches to food provision. Links to further papers on climate change adaptation and mitigation through agriculture.

links.title: FAO Soil Biodiversity Portal
links.description: Includes a framework under which soil biodiversity can be assessed, managed and conserved with pointers to research, capacity building and policy and programme development needs. Case studies and full information.

links.title: German Government Portal on Agricultural Biodiversity
links.description: Provides an overview of German organisations' know-how and projects on the conservation and sustainable use of agricultural biodiversity.

links.title: Navdanya: Research Foundation for Science,Technology and Ecology, India
links.description: Site provides information on agricultural biodiversity conservation and protection of people's rights, livelihoods and environment from centralised systems of monoculture in forestry, agriculture and fisheries. Links to many Indian and global movements. Navdanya is a program of the Research Foundation for Science, Technology and Ecology (RFSTE) set up by Vandana Shiva.

links.title: Seed Map
links.description: This page provides information about an online portal (temporarily down) on seeds, agricultural biodiversity and food. Through an interactive map it links to hundreds of case studies about agricultural biodiversity, its origins, threats, and development.

links.title: Supporting On-Farm Conservation in Eastern & Southern Africa
links.description: 2004 project report that includes information and case studies on the institutional conditions for 'successful' interventions, defined in terms of biological as well as economic parameters, derived from this GTZ / ODI / Darwin initiative project with African partners.

links.title: MS Swaminathan Research Foundation (MSSRF)
links.description: Indian programme on community based agricultural biodiversity conservation and management in Wayanad, in Kerala, the Kolli Hills and Namakkal in Tamil Nadu and the Jeypore Tract of Orissa. Also development of a community gene bank.

links.title: CBDC Mid-term evaluation report 2004
links.description: Report of 2004 mid-term evaluation of the Community Based Biodiversity Conservation (CBDC) Programme in Africa, Asia and Latin America that was a farmer-focused programme for agricultural biodiversity conservation, technology transfer and protection of farmer innovations.

817064.title: Aquatic Diversity
817064.description: Aquatic Diversity is an important component of agricultural biodiversity. The conservation and sustainable use of local aquatic ecosystems, ponds, rivers, coastal commons by artisanal fisherfolk and smallholder farmers is important to the survival of both humans and the environment. Since aquatic organisms, including fish, provide much of our food supply and income for coastal peoples, it is critical that fisherfolk and smallholder farmers have genetic reserves and sustainable ecosystems to draw upon as aquaculture and marine fisheries management continue to evolve.

links.title: World Fish Center
links.description: An international scientific and technical center, previously known as ICLARM and part of the CGIAR. Site has excellent content on all fisheries and aquatic ecosystem issues plus links to major resources including 'Fishbase' - the global aquatic organisms digital resource.

links.title: FishBase
links.description: A relational database with information to cater to different professionals such as research scientists, fisheries managers, and zoologists. FishBase on the web contains practically all fish species known to science.

links.title: Fish for All Summit
links.description: Call by Civil Society for more research on sustainable productive ecosystems at watershed, inland waters and marine levels and there to be no GMOs nor IPRs in Aquaculture and Fisheries. Links to the Summit website and report.

links.title: Salmon-Safe
links.description: Non-profit organisation site with information about reducing agriculture's impacts on endangered salmon and steelhead habitat in the Pacific Northwest. Links to concerned organisations promoting GM-free products in Oregon.

links.title: ICSF - The International Collective in Support of Fishworkers
links.description: This leading international think tank on artisanal fisheries, aquatic diversity and fishworkers, focuses on the majority, small-scale, artisanal sector. Links to relevant papers and all ICSF publications including SAMUDRA, their quarterly journal, and Yemaya, ICSF's newsletter on Gender and Fisheries.

links.title: South African Institute of Aquatic Biodiversity
links.description: The scientific 'home' of the Coelacanth. Information on programmes and research initiatives. Packed with databases and 10,000 photos on southern African fish species. Institute formerly known as the JLB Smith Institute of Ichthyology.

links.title: FAO pages on Aquatic Biodiversity
links.description: Provides definitions of types of aquatic ecosystems commonly used by capture fisheries and aquaculture in which aquatic biodiversity needs to be maintained; also refers to policies such as Code of Conduct on Responsible Fisheries, FAO programmes and links to key papers and related sites.

links.title: Fishing Out Aquatic Diversity
links.description: Paper on aquatic diversity from "Seedling" the quarterly journal of Genetic Resources Action International (GRAIN). Covers issues on the industrialisation of fishing and aquaculture that are destroying aquatic ecosystems and fisherpeoples' rights.

817065.title: Clearing Houses
817065.description: This category contains links to international, national or other Clearing House sites dealing specifically with Agricultural Biodiversity.

links.title: Netherlands Clearing House for Agricultural Biodiversity
links.description: Site provides information about The Netherlands approach to work on agricultural biodiversity. Links to details on specific programmes are being added.

links.title: Swedish Fourth National Report on Biodiversity including agriculture
links.description: Almost half of the red-listed species are found in the agricultural landscape and most are declining. The main threats to biodiversity in agricultural ecosystems are intensification on one hand, and abandonment on the other.

links.title: UK Clearing House for Access and Benefit Sharing
links.description: Provides summary of UK information on access and benefit sharing

links.title: German Agricultural Biodiversity Clearing House
links.description: This is the homepage of the National Inventory on Plant Genetic Resources in Germany (PGRDEU) hosted by the Information and Coordination Centre for Biological Diversity at the Federal Office for Agriculture and Food. The linked pages provide diverse information about agricultural and horticultural plants and their wild relatives.

817067.title: Domestic Animal Diversity
817067.description: Domestic Animal Diversity is an important component of agricultural biodiversity. The conservation and sustainable use of local breeds by farmers, pastoralists, breed societies and enthusiasts is important to the survival of both humans and animals. Since domesticated animals provide much of our food supply, it is critical that farmers, pastoralists and animal breeders have genetic reserves to draw upon as agriculture continues to evolve.  Livestock depend on forage and feed diversity and contribute, through nutrient recycling, to maintaining soil biodiversity.

links.title: Irish Moiled Cattle Society
links.description: Information about this rare traditional, dual purpose, hardy Irish breed of ancient lineage. Breed history and characteristics and current details of all registered Irish Moiled cattle and their breeders.

links.title: League for Pastoral Peoples
links.description: Supports local communities that share the care and raising of indigenous domesticated animals for commercial purposes.  Primary work is being done in India. Lists events, publications, photos and resource links.

links.title: Karen Commitment to Livestock Keepers Rights
links.description: Outcome of a conference of indigenous livestock breeding communities which concluded with the "Karen Commitment to Pastoralist/Indigenous Livestock Keepers' Rights" that calls for an international agreement to protect domestic animal diversity.

links.title: New Zealand Rare Breeds Conservation Society
links.description: It conserves, records and promotes rare and minority breeds of farm livestock in order to maintain genetic diversity. Website has information about breeds at risk; on-farm conservation projects and the development of a gene bank; and updated addresses to many other relevant organisations and websites in New Zealand and around the world.

links.title: Rare Breeds Survival Trust (RBST)
links.description: Founded in 1973 to conserve Britain's native livestock heritage - and since then, no breed of British farm animal has become extinct. Provides official summary of the annual RBST Watchlist with over 70 rare UK breeds, including cattle, goats, horses, pigs, poultry and sheep.

links.title: The Livestock Conservancy
links.description: Working to protect breeds of livestock and poultry from extinction. The Conservancy works with farmers, chefs, historians, consumers, and others around the nation to protect genetic diversity and heritage breeds in agriculture.

links.title: Ancient Cattle of Wales (ACW)
links.description: Website of the ACW promotes conservation and use of the colourful breeds of traditional Welsh cattle, which trace their recorded history back to the 10th century. Limited information but links to organiser. Site also in Welsh.

links.title: International Livestock Research Institute: Animal Genetic Resources
links.description: Documenting genetic diversity among indigenous livestock breeds of developing countries, fostering conservation of indigenous breeds and designing breeding programmes to improve productivity in low-input environments. Site under development

links.title: Ryeland Sheep
links.description: One of the oldest British sheep breeds and a rare breed in some countries. Earliest reference in 12th century of Herefordshire monks trading wool from these sheep grazed on ryegrass. Site provides breed history, details, news and links to other relevant rare sheep breed sites. Some commercial content.

links.title: Domestic Animal Diversity Information Service (DAD-IS)
links.description: The key communication and information tool for implementing the FAO Global Strategy for the Management of Farm Animal Genetic Resources (AnGR).

links.title: Rare Breeds International (RBI)
links.description: The only international non-governmental organisation (NGO) that aims to prevent the loss of diversity in global farm animal genetic resources (AnGR) through encouraging and supporting relevant activities and research by NGOs and governments. Information on events and links to national organisations

links.title: Rare Breeds Trust of Australia
links.description: This organisation the amalgamation of the Australian Rare and Minority Breeds Association and Rare Breeds Victoria. Site has breed profiles, including Australia's heritage breeds of camels and equines, events calendar, newsletter and educational project details.

links.title: Irish Draught Horse Conservation
links.description: Website describes the work of the Irish Draught Horse Society in encouraging the conservation of the breed's genetic diversity through use. Many links to helpful resources.

817066.title: On-Farm Crop Diversity
817066.description: On-farm conservation and sustainable use of crop biodiversity - both cultivated crops and wild relatives

links.title: Agricultural Biodiversity and Livelihoods: Issues and Entry Points for Development Agencies
links.description: Report reviews policy issues concerning the maintenance and development of agricultural biodiversity in farming systems emphasising need for greater involvement of farmers and their communities.

links.title: Crop Wild Relatives Portal
links.description: Portal on information on and programmes to maintain and enhance the in situ conservation of 'wild' relatives of crop plants. Programme profiles and reports on inventories and conservation projects in China, Turkey, India, and other countries.

links.title: A Training Guide for In Situ Conservation On-farm
links.description: Aims to give national programs basic technical skills and tools to build institutional capacity and partnerships to implement an on-farm conservation program. PDF or MS Word formats.

links.title: Syngenta
links.description: An agriculture company helping to improve global food security by enabling farmers to make better use of available resources. Committed to rescuing land from degradation, enhancing biodiversity and revitalizing rural communities.

817063.title: Seed Savers
817063.description: Links to principal non-profit, public interest seed saver organisations throughout the world which conserve and distribute heritage and heirloom varieties of seeds, often through volunteer seed guardians

links.title: Seed Savers Exchange
links.description: Founded in 1975, this non-profit organization was a pioneer in the heirloom seed movement. General information as well as an online catalog. Decorah, Iowa.

links.title: Seed Savers
links.description: Promoting and organising the preservation, free distribution and exchange of open-pollinated seeds. Based in Australia.

links.title: Seeds of Diversity
links.description: Canada's Heritage Seed Program preserving varieties of seeds from rare and unusual garden plants in a living gene bank. Based in Waterloo, Ontario, Canada.

links.title: Seedsaving and Seedsavers' Resources
links.description: Directory of web resources on seed saving. Includes a section on books on seed saving.

links.title: Irish Seed Savers
links.description: Preserving Ireland's special and disappearing varieties of fruit, grains and vegetables. Provides background information, details of projects, membership and sponsorship notes, and event and contact data. County Clare, Ireland.

links.title: Southern Exposure Seed Exchange
links.description: Workshops, information and links about heirloom and other open-pollinated vegetables that grow well in the southeastern U.S. Mineral, VA.

links.title: Native Seeds/SEARCH
links.description: Site records work of NS/S to conserve, distribute and document the adapted and diverse varieties of agricultural seed, their wild relatives and the role these seeds play in cultures of the American Southwestern and northwest Mexico. Project reports, seeds for sharing and links included.

links.title: Victory Horticultural Library
links.description: Dedicated to preserving rare seed varieties along with our collective horticultural heritage. Features include historical information and a forum for fostering community. Oregon, US.

links.title: The Spruce - Seed & Plant Exchanges
links.description: Resources for gardeners swapping seeds. Paid and free memberships listed.

links.title: Native Seed Network
links.description: Site covers much of the wild and domesticated flora of utility to humans, and their ecosystems,in the USA. Many links to sister sites of importance. Seed exchange facilitated through site.

links.title: Koanga Institute
links.description: To establish and maintain a collection of New Zealand heirloom plants (along with records of their history and culture) to ensure their survival and availability for future generations both as a resource for cultivation and genetic diversity.

links.title: BC Seed Security Program
links.description: Information about events, seed saving workshops and other activities in British Columbia for seed exchanges. Database of available varieties. BC, Canada.

links.title: Nelson Seed Library
links.description: Established at the "Top of the South" Nelson and Golden Bay, New Zealand to support genetic diversity at a time when it is under threat. Links to resources.

links.title: EU-seedlaw.net
links.description: Declaration to protect rights to save seeds in Europe and against (2013) European Commission proposals to change EU seed laws that would affect the food sovereignty, biodiversity, food security, and the health of European citizens.

links.title: Garden Organic's Heritage Seed Library
links.description: Details of UK's premier organic vegetable seed bank that aims to conserve and make available vegetable varieties that have been dropped from popular seed catalogues.

links.title: Seed Save
links.description: USA: programme working to promote regional seed solutions

links.title: Svalbard Global Seed Vault
links.description: Almost a million seed samples from all over the world, safeguarded inside a permafrost mountain.

links.title: Biodiversity and Dynamics of Ecosystems of Northern Eurasia
links.description: Workshop on the application of Information Technology to problems of biodiversity. Novosibirsk, Russia. 9-14 July,  2001.

links.title: Workshop on Information Technologies Application to Problems of Biodiversity and Dynamics of Ecosystems in North Eurasia
links.description: Concept is to research into biodiversity and dynamics of ecosystems in Northern Siberia.  RAS Institute of Cytology and Genetics.

817070.title: Conservation
817070.description: As humans, we have a large impact on ecosystems. Care must be taken, therefore, when we use and interact with these systems.

links.title: IUCN
links.description: The world conservation union, whose mission is to influence, encourage and assist societies throughout the world to conserve the integrity and diversity of nature and to ensure that any use of natural resources is equitable and ecologically sustainable.

links.title: The Whitley Awards Foundation
links.description: Offers a wide range of awards and grants for nature conservation projects worldwide. Applications are welcome from those working in nature conservation, botanical and habitat conservation and renewable energy.

links.title: World Conservation Monitoring Centre
links.description: Provides information services on conservation and sustainable use of the world's living resources, and helps others to develop information systems of their own.

links.title: WildCRU Wildlife Conservation Research Unit
links.description: Oxford University group develops practical solutions to conservation problems through research, implementation, education and local public involvement. Includes support and donation details.

links.title: Wildlife Conservation Society
links.description: USA organization managing national and international conservation projects, research and education programs.

links.title: Last Refuge Ltd.
links.description: Supporting endangered environments and species through films and images, with photo and sound galleries and information about films made and the awards won.

links.title: Temper of the Times Foundation
links.description: Provides funds to underwrite advertising designed to promote the conservation and restoration of native wildlife, plants, and ecosystems in the United States. Application guidelines and procedures are given.

links.title: Tropical Research and Conservation Centre
links.description: Research and education in biodiversity conservation and sustainable use of marine environments of East Malaysia.

links.title: Wild World
links.description: Provides maps identifying habitat types and areas that are identified as priority for conservation.

links.title: Conservation Breeding Specialist Group
links.description: An international conserveration organization whose mission is to assist conservation of threatened animal and plant species through scientific management of small populations in wild habitats, with linkage to captive populations where needed.

links.title: The Charles Darwin Foundation
links.description: Founded in 1959, under the auspices of UNESCO and the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources, the Charles Darwin Foundation is dedicated to the conservation of the Galapagos ecosystems.

links.title: Conservation Law Foundation
links.description: Uses law, economics and science to solve the environmental problems that threaten the people, natural resources and communities of New England.

links.title: Offwell Woodland and Wildlife Trust
links.description: Concerned with the conservation of species, habitats and biodiversity.

links.title: National Biodiversity Network
links.description: An information network of biodiversity data provided by a collaboration of organisations, such as the UK nature agencies, wildlife trusts, the Natural History Museum and others.

links.title: ESRI Conservation Program
links.description: Conservation information and links to organisations.

links.title: Natural Resources Defense Council
links.description: Information about the threats to endangered animals and their habitats.

links.title: Wildlife Conservation Network
links.description: Information about the network which focuses on funding and supporting independent and innovative conservationists who are creating and implementing new strategies for saving endangered wildlife and habitats and the projects in progress.

links.title: Native America
links.description: Information about the plants and animals of North America, research being undertaken, restoration/protection projects and membership details.

links.title: Conservation  Research Education  Action (CREA)
links.description: Works against tropical deforestation through creating sustainable environments and communities in Panama. It undertakes school expeditions and  research, and operates the  Cocobolo Nature Reserve.

links.title: The National Park Service
links.description: Charged with the trust of preserving the natural resources of America.

links.title: Wiltshire Wildlife Trust
links.description: UK based charity that promotes and manages natural preserves. Features mission statement, project descriptions, news, and contacts.

links.title: Biodiversity and Worldmap
links.description: Measuring biodiversity value and selecting priority areas for conservation.  Page includes graph and resource links.

links.title: Conservation International (CI)
links.description: Nonprofit applies innovations in science, economics, policy and community participation to protect the Earth's biodiversity around the world. Includes conservation regions and programs, strategies, newsletters, publications and how to get involved.

links.title: 2000 IUCN Red List of Threatened Species
links.description: Provides taxonomic, conservation status, and distribution information on taxa that are facing a high risk of global extinction.

links.title: Oryx
links.description: A journal that provides a comprehensive review of the conservation and status of fauna, flora and habitats, and of conservation policy and sustainable use.

links.title: Mangrove Action Project
links.description: Promotes responsible management of mangroves and coastal environments. Lists the relevant issues, news items, their programs, and pictures.

links.title: Biological Conservation Newsletter
links.description: A monthly publication of the Department of Systematic Biology, National Museum of Natural History, Smithsonian Institution.

links.title: Sea Shepherd Conservation Society
links.description: International non-profit, marine wildlife conservation organization. It uses direct-action tactics to investigate, document, and take action to expose and confront illegal activities. Includes details of campaigns and how members of the public can get involved.

links.title: Office of Protected Resources
links.description: Provides advice for national policy direction and conservation of marine mammals, endangered species and their habitats.

links.title: National Marine Sanctuaries
links.description: Provides information on the NOAA system of 14 marine protected areas encompassing more than 150,000 square miles of America’s oceans. The program aims to conserve, protect and enhance their biodiversity and ecological integrity.

links.title: Oceans Research
links.description: Network of marine research laboratories in South Africa, Namibia and Mozambique. Projects include the biology of marine mega-fauna including the white shark, bull shark, manta ray and turtles.

links.title: The Nature Conservancy
links.description: Conservation organization working around the world to protect ecologically important lands and waters. Includes details of campaigns and projects, and how members of the public can help.

links.title: RARE Conservation
links.description: Works globally in social marketing for biodiversity conservation, changing awareness, attitudes, and behaviors toward conservation at the local level to inspire people in the world's most threatened natural areas care for their natural resources.

links.title: Biodiversity Hotspots
links.description: An interactive world map of the places where plants and animals are most threatened. Includes a searchable database of all land-dwelling vertebrates.

links.title: People's Trust for Endangered Species
links.description: A conservation charity working to ensure a future for endangered and threatened species and habitats worldwide. UK based.

817078.title: Birds
817078.description: The survival of bird populations is threatened by habitat loss, with a reduction in plants and insects numbers. Habitat protection and restoration is often a key requirement in the conservation of bird species.

links.title: The Royal Society for the Protection of Birds
links.description: A charity that takes action for wild birds and the environment.

links.title: Great Lakes Bird Conservation
links.description: Dedicated to the conservation and management of forest birds in the Laurentian Mixed Forest region of the Western Great Lakes Basin. Includes a project description with management goals and information about bird ecology and conservation.

links.title: Black Redstart
links.description: Information on the habitat, distribution, threats and conservation efforts in the UK.

links.title: Indonesian Parrot Project
links.description: Information on trapping/trafficking in cockatoos and parrots, effects of illegal logging on habitat, and IPP's attempts to mitigate these problems through encouragement of sustainable economic development.

links.title: Wisconsin Bird Conservation Initiative
links.description: Coordinates bird-based projects for effective management of birds in Wisconsin. Includes the background of the organisation, their aims and objectives and a news letter.

links.title: American Bird Conservancy
links.description: ABC is a not-for-profit dedicated to the conservation of wild birds and their habitats in the Americas.

links.title: George Miksch Sutton Avian Research Center
links.description: Dedicated to finding cooperative conservation solutions for birds and the natural world through science and education.

links.title: North American Breeding Bird Survey, Results and Analysis 1966 - 2003
links.description: Monitoring program to estimate population changes for breeding birds in the continental United States and southern Canada. Recently expanded to include Alaska and northern Mexico.

links.title: Rocky Mountain Bird Observatory
links.description: Mission is the conservation of Rocky Mountain and Great Plains birds and their habitats through research, monitoring, education, and outreach.

links.title: Hopper Mountain National Wildlife Refuge Complex
links.description: Information on the California Condor and the recovery program for this endangered bird. Includes information on each of 3 refuges set aside to protect habitat for the condor and a fourth refuge with an active western Snowy Plover management program.

links.title: Bird Conservation International
links.description: A quarterly peer-reviewed journal focusing on the conservation issues affecting birds and their habitats.

links.title: Conservation Through Birding
links.description: The American Bird Conservancy provides information on bird conservation and how birders can get involved.

links.title: Avian Genetics
links.description: Krissy Bush provides information on research into avian genetics and avian ecological genetics.

links.title: ProAves Colombia
links.description: Colombian NGO dedicated to the conservation of birds and their habitats through research, outreach and direct conservation actions in collaboration with local communities. In Spanish and English.

links.title: BirdLife International
links.description: Global partnership of conservation organisations that aims to conserve birds, their habitats and global biodiversity,

817079.title: Raptors
817079.description:
Description:
This category is for political and social issues concerning loss of endangered raptor species.

Related:
Where should I submit my website about animals?
Or, where will I find the animal topic I am looking for?

links.title: Peregrine Fund
links.description: Works to conserve wild populations of birds of prey.

links.title: Hawk Mountain Sanctuary
links.description: An international center for conservation, education, and research about raptors.

links.title: Flight to Freedom
links.description: Group's mission is to provide a sanctuary for injured raptors and to help re-introduce them to their natural environment.

links.title: Hawks Aloft, Inc.
links.description: Works to conserve raptors and their habitat through education, field studies, and cooperation with other organizations.

links.title: HawkWatch International
links.description: Promoting the preservation of raptors and the ecosystems they inhabit.

links.title: The Hawk Conservancy - Introduction
links.description: A look at its history, work, and some of the rare and endangered raptors being bred in captivity as an aid to global conservation.

links.title: Santa Cruz Predatory Bird Research Group
links.description: Founded to restore California's endangered Peregrine falcon population, has expanded its research focus to include other raptor species.

links.title: Raptor Education Foundation
links.description: Promoting environmental literacy using non-releasable  raptors.

links.title: Last Chance Forever
links.description: L.C.F. is a non-profit organization dedicated to the rehabilitation and release of injured and orphaned raptors, birds of prey such as hawks, owls, eagles, falcons, and vultures.

links.title: Peregrine Falcon Page
links.description: Contains information as well as photos and live full-motion video of peregrine falcons.

links.title: Raptor Resource Project
links.description: A non-profit group located in Bluffton, Iowa working to restore the Midwestern US population of Peregrine Falcons and other raptors by captively breeding birds for release in the wild.

links.title: Canadian Peregrine Falcon Foundation
links.description: Dedicated to assisting the recovery of the Peregrine Falcon and other Canadian raptor species. Includes 3 nest webcams.

links.title: Wingspan Birds of Prey Trust
links.description: New Zealand charity for research, captive management, and public awareness of New Zealand raptors, especially the endangered New Zealand Falcon.

links.title: American Bald Eagle Foundation
links.description: An educational foundation in Alaska dedicated to the protection and preservation of Bald Eagle habitat by sponsoring and facilitating research activities.

links.title: American Eagle Foundation
links.description: Not-for-profit organization dedicated to preserving  bald eagles and protecting their environment. Also cares for eagles that are injured or orphaned at a facility at Pigeon Forge, Tennessee.

links.title: NZ Falcon
links.description: Membership offers the opportunity to become involved and aid in the conservation and research of raptors in New Zealand.

links.title: Wirral & Ellesmere Port Barn Owl Trust
links.description: Registered charity aiming to conserve wild Barn Owl populations. Gives information about the Barn Owl, the activities of the trust and how to become a member.

links.title: The Alberta Birds of Prey Foundation
links.description: Helps conserve birds of prey with the rehabilitating and releasing injured birds of prey back to the wild, captive breeding and release of endangered species, studying and monitoring wild birds of prey populations and encouraging  increased public environmental awareness.

links.title: Southwestern Bald Eagle Management Committee
links.description: Provides information on the nestwatch program, the sub adult migration study and plenty of information on the bird in Arizona.

links.title: Hawk Migration Association of North America
links.description: HMANA is a membership-based organization committed to the conservation of raptors through the scientific study, enjoyment and appreciation of their migration behavior.

links.title: Soarin' Hawk Raptor Rehabilitation
links.description: Providing care to injured hawks, owls, eagles and falcons in Northeast Indiana.

links.title: Russian Raptors Research and Conservation Network
links.description: The site of society raptor biologists and raptor conservationists of the northern Eurasia.

817080.title: Captive Breeding
817080.description: There has been a major shift of emphasis of zoos from recreation to conservation. Information gathered through research undertaken at zoos assists in conservation and management decisions.  Captive breeding programmes conducted in zoological parks produce individuals for release into the wild in reintroduction programmes, so boosting wild populations.

links.title: American Zoo and Aquarium Association
links.description: Promoting the welfare of zoological parks and aquariums and their advancement as public educational institutions, as scientific centers, as natural science and wildlife exhibition and conservation agencies, and as cultural recreational establishments dedicated to the enrichment of human and natural resources.

links.title: Black-footed Ferret (Mustela nigripes)
links.description: 1998 recovery update results from captive breeding programs in Wyoming, USA.

links.title: Snakes
links.description: The Captive Breeding of Colubrid Snakes

links.title: Captive Breeding and Species Re-introductions
links.description: Explanation of captive breeding programs and their use in conservation.

links.title: Zoos Victoria: Fighting Extinction
links.description: Contributing to the conservation of wildlife and natural  habitats.

links.title: British Columbia Wildlife Park
links.description: Assists the preserving the threatened and endangered species through education, captive breeding and rehabilitation.

links.title: The International Centre for Birds of Prey
links.description: Has been successful in the captive breeding of 50 raptor species.

links.title: Pittsburgh Zoo: Conservation
links.description: Explains the Zoo's approach to conservation including research, living green, breeding programs and the International Conservation Center.

links.title: Ecology and Society
links.description: A peer-reviewed, electronic, scientific journal published by the Resilience Alliance.

links.title: The National Audubon Society
links.description: The mission of the National Audubon Society is to conserve and restore natural ecosystems, focusing on birds and other wildlife for the benefit of humanity and the earth's biological diversity.

links.title: International Mire Conservation Group
links.description: Promoting the conservation of mires and related ecosystems, giving information on the sustainable use of mires, red lists of European wetland plants and a link to the IMCG newsletter.

links.title: Friends of Ecological Reserves
links.description: Information about ecological reserves, the not-for-profit charitable organization and products and membership to purchase to support ecoreserves.

links.title: Ecological Society of America
links.description: A non-profit organization of scientists founded in 1915, conducting research, teaching, and working to provide the ecological knowledge needed to solve environmental problems.

817088.title: Fish
817088.description: Streams, lakes and oceans exist in a fragile balance. Predators maintain the population of the species they prey upon at the level which the environment can support. If humans are to harvest from these ecosystem, the effect of removing animals from the ecosystem must be understood.

links.title: Fish Conservation
links.description: Working with professionals and communities to protect fish and fisheries.

links.title: Trout Unlimited
links.description: A private, non-profit organization whose mission is to conserve, protect and restore North America's trout and salmon fisheries and their watersheds.

links.title: Fish Conservation
links.description: Streams, lakes, estuaries, bays and oceans exist in a fragile balance. If we are careful, understanding how removing animals will affect the ecosystem, these habitats can be enjoyed by us and our descendants.

links.title: Wild Salmon Center
links.description: Non-profit organization dedicated to dedicated to protecting Pacific salmon, steelhead, char, and trout stocks and their ecosystems in the northern Pacific rim.

links.title: Atlantic Salmon Federation
links.description: Information about the Atlantic Salmon, the threats to its survival, research being undertaken, the journal produced by the society and membership.

links.title: Tuna-org
links.description: Informal network of intergovernmental organizations that carry out data collection, scientific monitoring and management of tuna resources. Includes information on authorised and unauthorised vessels and a calendar of meetings.

links.title: North Atlantic Salmon Conservation Organisation
links.description: NASCO aims to contribute to the conservation, restoration, enhancement and rational management of salmon stocks taking into account the best scientific evidence.

links.title: Western and Central Pacific Fisheries Commission
links.description: International organization that aims to conserve and manage fish stocks in the Pacific Ocean.

links.title: International Commission for the Conservation of Atlantic Tunas
links.description: ICCAT is an inter-governmental fishery organization responsible for the conservation of tunas and tuna-like species in the Atlantic Ocean and its adjacent seas.

links.title: Commission for the Conservation of Southern Bluefin Tuna
links.description: CCSBT is an international organization that aims to ensure, through appropriate management, the conservation and optimum utilisation of the global SBT fishery.

links.title: Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission
links.description: IATTC is responsible for the conservation and management of fisheries for tunas and other species taken by tuna-fishing vessels in the eastern Pacific Ocean.

links.title: Indian Ocean Tuna Commission
links.description: IOTC is an intergovernmental organization that manages tuna and tuna-like species in the Indian Ocean and adjacent seas.

links.title: Native Fish Conservancy
links.description: A non-profit organization committed to conservation of native fishes of the midwestern United States.

817089.title: Sharks
817089.description: Sharks comprise about 1% of all living fish, with approximately 350 species occurring globally. Most sharks feed on other fish or marine mammals, while some are plankton feeders.    Threats to sharks include incidental capture during net fishing and hunting due to an increase in trade for shark products and persecution.

links.title: Bite-Back
links.description: Information about the species and the threats to their survival imposed by consumer demands. Discover news, information and links.

links.title: Sharkkbait's Shark Conservation and Home Page
links.description: Essay dispels common myths and misconceptions about attacks. Also discusses the role the predator plays in maintaining balance in ecosystems.

links.title: The Shark Trust
links.description: Organization dedicated to the conservation of species in general, including rays and skates. Find news, photos, information on joining and making donations.

links.title: BBC News: Increase in Shark Sightings
links.description: Article provides information on research from the Marine Conservation Society suggesting that basking shark populations may be beginning to recover in British waters.

links.title: Shark Foundation
links.description: International organization dedicated to the protection and   preservation of endangered species. Find mission statement, information on lectures, tours and current research projects.

links.title: Watching Out for Sharks
links.description: Article describes the research and conservation efforts of the California  Pelagic Shark Tagging Program. Includes a discussion of population status in California waters.

links.title: Pelagic Shark Research Foundation
links.description: To help address the lack of data, and contribute to public awareness of the issues involved in shark conservation, the Pelagic Shark Research Foundation (PSRF) was formed as a nonprofit research and education group in 1990.

links.title: Shark Research Institute
links.description: Shark research and conservation worldwide. Programs include ocean advocacy, education, satellite tracking and DNA studies.

links.title: The Thresher Shark Research and Conservation Project
links.description: A five year scientific study on the behaviour of thresher sharks which frequent Malapascua Island. Details include volunteer internship expeditions, conservation objectives, current results and partnerships.

817090.title: Great White Sharks
817090.description: This category is dedicated to sites that have information on the protection and conservation of the Great White Shark.

links.title: Sympathy for the Devil (White Shark Conservation)
links.description: Article by R. Aidan Martin discusses international conservation efforts aimed at protecting the species. Includes a summary of species ecology and photographs.

links.title: Star - Poachers set Sights on Great  Whites
links.description: Melanie Gosling describes how the species in South African waters is becoming fodder for the tourist trade and how this effects preservation efforts.

links.title: White Sharks
links.description: Provides information on research being undertaken at CSIRO Marine and Atmospheric Research, Australia. Includes a description of species physiology, movement patterns, and population status and protection measures.

817091.title: Whale Sharks
817091.description: This category is dedicated to sites containing information on the protection and conservation of the whale shark species.

links.title: Biodiversity International
links.description: An international non-profit organization devoted to the conservation and promotion of agricultural biodiversity. Includes information about genetic resources conservation and use.

links.title: EDGE of Existence
links.description: Raises awareness of the conservation of the world's most evolutionarily distinct and globally endangered (EDGE) species. Features detailed information, photographs, videos and blogs about EDGE species.

817087.title: Invertebrates
817087.description: Invertebrates have suffered a lack of attention from conservation professionals and the general public in the past. Scientists, however, are gaining a better understanding of the role of invertebrates in natural systems and the need to protect them.   Habitat loss is one of the main threats to invertebrate populations. Over collecting of some invertebrate groups, such as beetles and butterflies, can also pose a threat.

links.title: Invertebrate Images
links.description: Images of invertebrates from the tropical rain forest, deserts and coral reefs.

links.title: Invertebrate Diaries
links.description: Blog focusing on the author's own study of invertebrates and the rearing of many species.

links.title: Spider Conservation
links.description: Information about the threats to US spiders and their conservation.

links.title: Coleopterists Society
links.description: An international organization devoted to the study of the  systematics, biology and conservation of beetles.

links.title: Bumble Bee Watch
links.description: Citizen science project to track and conserve North America's bumblebees. Form for recording sightings, descriptions of species, and maps.

817092.title: Mammals
817092.description: Many species of mammals have undergone a decline in distribution and population size over the last few decades, due to habitat loss and fragmentation.     Mammals often attract more public interest than other groups of animals, due to the larger species such as elephants and the big cats. There are, however, many small, inconspicuous mammals also in need of conservation.

links.title: International Rhino Foundation
links.description: A non-profit corporation of institutions and individuals worldwide whose sole purpose is the conservation of Black, White, Sumatran, Javan and Indian Rhinos.

links.title: The American Society of Mammalogists
links.description: Promotes the study of mammals and involved in providing information for public policy, resources management, conservation, and education.

links.title: Seals and Sea Lions
links.description: Information on Australian Seals and Sea Lions, including photographs and the Australian Seal Action Plan.

links.title: The Buffalo War
links.description: A show examining the clash between Native Americans, ranchers, environmentalists and government officials over the yearly slaughter of wild bison in Yellowstone National Park.

links.title: Action Plan for Australian Marsupials and Monotremes
links.description: Reviews the conservation status of 209 taxa of Australian monotremes and marsupials: one species and three sub-species of monotremes and 112 species and 93 subspecies of marsupials.

links.title: Wild Camel Protection Foundation
links.description: Conservation of the wild Bactrian camel -- details of education resources, news, Lop Nur Reserve.

links.title: The David Shepherd Conservation Foundation
links.description: Raises funds and works for the survival of tigers, elephants, rhinos and other critically endangered mammals in the wild.

links.title: Yorkshire Mammal Group
links.description: Aims to promote the scientific study and conservation of mammals and to encourage a wider public interest in them.

links.title: EDGE of Existence
links.description: A project to conserve the world's most Evolutionarily Distinct and Globally Endangered (EDGE) species. Features photographs and details of the 100 most threatened animals, and explains the research and protection measures undertaken by scientists. Includes donation facility.

links.title: Wombat Protection Society of Australia Ltd
links.description: Includes photographs of adults and babies, advice for treating injured animals, research findings, and children's activities.

links.title: Defenders of Wildlife: Sea Otter
links.description: Provides information on the sea otter conservation and advocacy program organized by the North American conservation group, Defenders of Wildlife.

links.title: Irrawaddy Dolphin
links.description: The Wildlife Conservation Society provides a factsheet on this endangered species, the threats and challenges it faces and the conservation efforts being made.

links.title: Rhino Resource Center
links.description: Provides a searchable database of information on the five endangered species of rhinoceros with the aim of assisting research and conservation of the rhinoceros worldwide.

links.title: Mammal Species of the World
links.description: A database of mammalian taxonomy providing an on-line reference for identifying or verifying recognized scientific names and for taxonomic research.

links.title: Carolina Tiger Rescue
links.description: Nonprofit organization that rescues animals, primarily wildcats, and provides conservation education to the public. Includes animal descriptions, information about volunteerism and donations, hours, and directions. Located in Pittsboro, North Carolina.

links.title: Bat Conservation Trust
links.description: The UK's only organisation solely devoted to the conservation of bats and their habitats. It is a highly respected and established organisation combining the strengths of professionals and amateur experts.

links.title: Eurobats
links.description: The EUROBATS Secretariat administers the European Bat Agreement and is active in international media, and sponsoring of national and international events.

links.title: Bat Conservation and Management
links.description: Research, supply, and install bat house products. Also bat exclusions, bat control, cave/mine gating, harp/mist net surveys, and Indiana bat management.

links.title: Bat Conservation International
links.description: Information about bats, their conservation and how to get involved.

links.title: Horseshoe bat research and conservation
links.description: A forum to disseminate information about bat species of the family Rhinolophus and conservation projects.

Where should I submit my website about animals?

links.title: Spirit Bear Defender
links.description: Learn about spirit bears (sub-species of black bears), their habitat on BC's coast, and how to help protect them from poaching and habitat destruction.

links.title: Free The Bears Fund Inc
links.description: This organization raises funds for projects supporting bear conservation and rescue, such as dancing bears in India, sanctuaries in Laos, Cambodia, Thailand and Indonesia, and alternative livelihoods and environmental education to prevent the illegal trade in bears and bear parts.

links.title: Canid Specialist Group
links.description: Part of the IUCN's Species Survival Commission, dedicated to co-ordinating and conducting research and conservation activities worldwide to conserve endangered canid species.

links.title: Wild Dog Foundation
links.description: A project of The World Carnivore Society, dedicated to promoting wolf restoration, supporting captive breeding and promoting conservation of endangered canines.

Description:

links.title: Timber Wolf Information Network
links.description: Educational resource focussing on conservation of the timber wolf in the USA.

links.title: Wolf Conservation Center
links.description: Education about the importance of the wolf in the environment. Scheduled visits can be arranged to the center in Salem, New York.

links.title: Gray Wolf
links.description: U.S. Fish and Wildlife news and information about the gray wolf and a recovery project for the Midwest and Great Lakes area.

links.title: Wolf Haven International
links.description: Dedicated to public support for wolves and wolf recovery.

links.title: Wolf Conservation and Management Policy for Alaska
links.description: To provide for the conservation of Alaska's wolves and their prey populations.

links.title: International Wolf Center
links.description: Information about wolf biology, environmental issues, and human interaction. Also has webcams of their ambassador wolves.

links.title: Lobos of the South West
links.description: News about Mexican gray wolves, recovering from extinction.

817101.title: Ethiopian Wolf
817101.description: This category deals with the Ethiopian wolf.

links.title: Wikipedia - Claudio Sillero-Zubiri
links.description: Profile of the academic and field experience of this zoologist working to save the Ethiopian wolf from extinction. Includes pdf copies of some of his research on them.

links.title: African Elephant Conservation Trust
links.description: The goal of the African Elephant Conservation Trust is the successful conservation of Africa's elephants within the context of human needs and pressures.

links.title: Save The Elephants
links.description: Securing a future for elephants and sustaining the beauty and ecological integrity of the places where they live.

links.title: The Elephant Listening Project
links.description: A project which assesses the potential of acoustic monitoring for evaluating the abundance and health of elephants living in the dense forest.

links.title: African Elephant Specialist Group
links.description: Resources on elephant conservation, including African Elephant Database online, Pachyderm journal online, tools for the study and mitigation of human-elephant conflict, methods of counting and studying elephants and the African Elephant Bibliography.

links.title: African Forest Elephant
links.description: The Wildlife Conservation Society provides a factsheet on this species, the threats and challenges it faces and the conservation efforts being made.

links.title: Asian Elephant
links.description: The Wildlife Conservation Society provides a factsheet on this species, the threats and challenges it faces and the conservation efforts being made.

817104.title: Felines
817104.description: Feline conservation is a careful preservation and protection or planned management of a feline species to prevent exploitation, destruction, neglect, or extinction.

links.title: International Society for Endangered Cats (Canada)
links.description: This organization concentrates on the 30 smaller wild cat species from the clouded leopard to the black footed cat.

links.title: The Snow Leopard Conservancy
links.description: Demonstrating innovative, grassroots measures leading local people toward effective stewardship of the endangered snow leopard and its habitat. Projects in action, educational materials, and news.

links.title: Cat Action Treasury (CAT)
links.description: A non-profit fund for conservation of wild cats in their natural habitats. News, links, photos, and an informational research library.

links.title: The Cat House Feline Conservation Center
links.description: A non-profit organization dedicated to the protection and preservation of the world's endangered felines, with information on volunteering, a schedule of events, an online store, and a photo gallery of their cats.

links.title: Big Cats Felid Research, News, and Commentary
links.description: Research and news, photos, artistic prints and posters for sale, cat classification charts, fossil history, and related links.

links.title: National Cheetah Management South Africa
links.description: A non-government organization focusing on the conservation of the cheetah outside of protected areas in South Africa.

links.title: Big Cat Rescue
links.description: Focusing on freeing big cats from commercial exploitation. Consists of photos and the sounds of wild cats; with games, a gift shop, how to help, news, legal advice, a slideshow, and educational programs and tours.

links.title: Feline Conservation Federation (FCF)
links.description: A group of enthusiasts interested in the propagation and preservation of all wild feline species. Supports responsible private captive husbandry of exotic felines. Contains resources for breeders, legal advice, and news.

links.title: Small Wild Cat Conservation Foundation
links.description: Of the 36 species of wild cats, 22 are small cats often no bigger than house cats. Most conservation efforts are directed at the largest members of the family, the big cats. SCCA seeks to put the spotlight on the small wild cats of the world.

links.title: Friends of the Florida Panther Refuge
links.description: The support organization of the Florida Panther National Wildlife Refuge. Panther information, action alerts, volunteer information, links, and an online store.

links.title: Cheetah Conservation Fund (CCF)
links.description: Focuses on researching and implementing strategies for cheetah conservation in its natural habitat. Features cheetah facts and threats, current projects, news, photos, an online store, and a kid's section.

links.title: Eastern Cougar Foundation
links.description: A non-profit group concerned with scientific and cultural aspects of cougar recovery in eastern North America. Research, news, an online store, links, and a hotline to call for cougar sightings.

links.title: Snow Leopard Trust
links.description: They protect the endangered snow leopard and its Central Asian habitat.

links.title: NOAH Feline Conservation Center
links.description: Specializes in the captive husbandry of cougar, bobcat, Canadian lynx, serval, caracal and Geoffroy's cat; with information on building enclosures, pet ownership, responsible breeding and kittens for sale.

links.title: Cat Survival Trust
links.description: A UK charity conserving all species of wild cats. Provides information about the cats of the world and how members of the public can help.

links.title: Wildcat Haven
links.description: Protecting and conserving the very rare Scottish wildcat. Promoting area feral and pet cat spaying. Preventing exploitation of the Clashindarroch Forest.

links.title: Scottish Wildcat Action
links.description: The official wildcat conservation project delivering a national action plan to save the Scottish wildcat. Find out about Scottish wildcats, their habitats, and why they are one of the most endangered mammals in Britain.

links.title: WildCats Conservation Alliance
links.description: A wild tiger and Amur leopard conservation organization. Supports breeding programs held in European, Australasian and American zoos and contributes to protect wild populations.

links.title: Project Survival's Cat Haven
links.description: Helping researchers and conservationists in their efforts to study and protect wild cats. Group history, project funding, current projects and achievements, and how to get involved. Dunlap, California.

links.title: Jaguar - WCS
links.description: The Wildlife Conservation Society provides a factsheet on this species, the threats and challenges it faces and the conservation efforts being made.

links.title: Snow Leopard - WCS
links.description: The Wildlife Conservation Society provides a factsheet on this mountain species, the threats and challenges it faces and the conservation efforts being made.

links.title: Cheetah Conservation Botswana
links.description: Set up in 2003 with the assistance of the Mokolodi Wildlife Foundation, it aims to be a long term conservation project, incorporating scientific research, practical species management and community education.

817105.title: Tigers
817105.description:
Description:
This category is for links to resources about conservation of tigers or tiger populations as a political or social issue.

Related:
Where should I submit my website about animals?
Or, where will I find the animal topic I am looking for?

links.title: Save China's Tigers
links.description: Dedicated to in-situ conservation of native cat species in China, particularly the South China tiger. Chinese culture information, action plans, how to help, photos, and rewilding training progress.

links.title: Tigers in Crisis
links.description: Information about endangered tigers, their conservation status, and solutions. General information, a newsletter, image gallery, and an online action taking program.

links.title: Tiger Creek
links.description: A non-government organization working in tiger genetics with the private sector tiger owners to preserve tiger biodiversity. Genetics research, educational info, a press kit, and a links directory.

links.title: Global Tiger Forum
links.description: Inter-governmental organization protecting tigers in the wild and strengthening tiger conservation.

Description:

Related:
Where should I submit my website about animals?
Or, where will I find the animal topic I am looking for?

links.title: Buffalo Field Campaign
links.description: Organization aiming to stop the slaughter and harassment of the wild buffalo in and around Yellowstone National Park. Includes information on buffalo, on volunteering and a FAQ.

links.title: WCS - Bison
links.description: The Wildlife Conservation Society provides a fact sheet with the threats and challenges it faces and the conservation efforts being made.

links.title: WCS - Caribou
links.description: The Wildlife Conservation Society provides a factsheet on this species, the threats and challenges it faces and the conservation efforts being made.

links.title: InterTribal Buffalo Council
links.description: Efforts by numerous Indian tribes to return the buffalo to its historic range.

817094.title: Marine Mammals
817094.description:
Description:
This category is for links to resources about conservation of marine mammals or marine mammal populations as a political or social issue.

Related:
Where should I submit my website about animals?
Or, where will I find the animal topic I am looking for?

links.title: Save the Manatee Club
links.description: A membership-based, national nonprofit organization in through which the public can participate in conservation efforts to save endangered manatees from extinction.

links.title: The Marine Mammal Center
links.description: Involved in rescue, research and education. You can read about all of these activities on their website. Also features Adopt-A-Seal program, virtual tour of the centre and How You Can Help page.

links.title: NOAA Fisheries - National Marine Fisheries Service
links.description: Promotes sustainable fisheries, recovery of protected species, and the health of coastal marine habitats in the USA.

links.title: IOSF - International Otter Survival Fund
links.description: Dedicated to the conservation of all 13 species of otter. We fund conservation programmes in endangered species

links.title: Texas Marine Mammal Stranding Network
links.description: The Network rescues and rehabilitates marine mammals that strand along the Texas Coast, providing food, medical treatment, and 24-hour-a-day observation.

links.title: Marine Mammal Stranding Center
links.description: A private non-profit organization based in Brigantine, New Jersey. Since the Center's founding in 1978, it has responded to over 1500 calls for stranded whales, dolphins, seals, and sea turtles that washed ashore on New Jersey beaches.

links.title: Animal Tracks
links.description: An interactive site containing images of marine life collected and contributed by the user community. Data includes tagged images of whales, dolphins, seals, sea turtles and other marine and coastal life.

links.title: Dolphins and the Tuna Industry
links.description: Complete text of the book that presents key conclusions about the controversial killing of thousands of dolphins each year during tuna fishing in the eastern tropical Pacific.

links.title: Killer Whales: Conservation and Research
links.description: Outline provided by Sea World describes the importance of legal protections, research and marine zoological parks for species preservation.

links.title: Save The Whales
links.description: Organization dedicated to the conservation and preservation of the species. Includes news, information on research and contacts.

links.title: New Zealand Whale and Dolphin Trust
links.description: Dedicated to fostering effective preservation and protection through research. Discover species profiles, information on projects, contacts and news.

links.title: Whale and Dolphin Conservation
links.description: International charity dedicated to the worldwide conservation and protection of whales, dolphins and porpoises.

links.title: BBC News: Extinction Nears for Whales and Dolphins
links.description: Alex Kirby reports that some species are now so endangered they may not survive another 10 years. Features photos and related links.

links.title: Reviewing Scientists Say Proposed Conservation Measures Unlikely To Help Whales
links.description: Science Daily article discusses doubts raised by scientists charged by  the International Whaling Commission (IWC) to review the effectiveness of  sanctuaries for conservation.

links.title: Earthtrust - Wildlife Conservation Worldwide
links.description: An environmental organization based in Hawaii. ET works to save the dolphins and whales, against whaling, driftnets, and tuna fisheries.

links.title: Irish Whale and Dolphin Group (IWDG)
links.description: Dedicated to the conservation and better understanding of cetaceans in Irish waters.

links.title: The Ocean Alliance
links.description: Dedicated to the conservation of whales and their ocean environment through research and education.

links.title: Humpback Whale
links.description: The Wildlife Conservation Society provides a factsheet on this species, the threats and challenges it faces and the conservation efforts being made.

links.title: The Bottlenose Dolphin Research Institute
links.description: BDRI undertakes scientific research and education to contribute to the conservation of dolphins. Includes details of courses, research, resources and support.

links.title: Saving Freshwater Dolphins Means Saving Their Rivers
links.description: Article by Debra Boyce of the Christian Science Monitor describes the ecological challenges caused by humans that threaten the species group. Features links to related sites.

links.title: American Society of Primatologists
links.description: The conservation mission of the Society is: to establish liaison between the Society, conservation groups, and research resources development agencies, provide information on the status of wild populations of nonhuman primates, monitor primate trade, research the success of captive breeding programs and enactment of legislation aimed at conservation of nonhuman primates.

links.title: Primate Conservation Inc
links.description: Learn more about how to protect endangered monkeys, apes, lemurs and lorises from extinction.

links.title: The Douc Langur Foundation
links.description: Douc Langurs (Pygathrix nemaeus) are colobine monkeys found most frequently in the primary evergreen forests of Vietnam and Laos. Despite efforts by local , provincial and state authorities, little or no effective protection of the endangered Douc Langur population exists at the present time.

links.title: The Simian Society of America
links.description: A non-profit organization founded in 1957 to improve the welfare of primates in captivity.

links.title: International Primate Protection League
links.description: The International Primate Protection League works for the well-being of primates. IPPL has Field Representatives in 31 countries. Its Advisory Board is composed of experts from the fields of zoology, anthropology, medicine, biology, veterinary medicine, and psychology.

links.title: Orangutan Foundation International
links.description: Orangutan conservation, rainforest preservation, education and wildlife research.

links.title: Sumatran Orangutan Society
links.description: Information about the Sumatran orangutan (Pongo abelii), the threat to their survival and membership details.

links.title: Ape Alliance
links.description: The Ape Alliance is an international coalition of organisations and individuals, working for the conservation and welfare of apes.

links.title: Jane Goodall Institute for Wildlife Research, Education and Conservation
links.description: Leads visitors on a tour through our global conservation, and environmental education programs; provides a glimpse into the lives of the chimpanzees of Gombe National Park and in our African sanctuaries; and introduces visitors to Jane Goodall -- her childhood, her work, and her current activities.

links.title: The Orangutan Foundation UK
links.description: Orangutan conservation organisation, saving Asia's endangered great ape by protecting their tropical forest habitat, working with local communities and promoting research and education.

links.title: Pacific Primate Sanctuary, Wailuku, Maui
links.description: Sanctuary for endangered and distressed species of New World Primates such as the Cotton-top Tamarin. Facts about these endangered species, personal stories of rescue, and many ways you can help including volunteering.

links.title: The Wild Chimpanzee Foundation
links.description: chimps, wild, chimpanzees, save the chimpanzees. WCF is dedicated to saving the last of the wild chimpanzees and their habitat, the African forests.

links.title: Bonobo Conservation Initiative
links.description: BCI is a non-profit organisation which conducts bonobo surveys, establishes protected areas and works to increase global awareness about bonobos.

links.title: AWARE Africa
links.description: Animal Wild Aid, Rehabilitation and Education supports the Lwiro primate sanctuary in The Democratic Republic of Congo. Includes a blog about what's happening there.

links.title: OrangAid: Save the Orangutans
links.description: A non-profit volunteer organization to promote awareness and conservation of endangered orangutans. Includes videos and photos.

Related:
Where should I submit my website about animals?

links.title: Dian Fossey Gorilla Fund
links.description: Information about protecting the mountain gorillas.

links.title: Gorilla 100
links.description: Celebrates the original discovery of the mountain gorilla -- details of events in Rwanda.

links.title: Cross River Gorilla
links.description: The Wildlife Conservation Society provides a factsheet on this critically endangered species and the conservation efforts being made.

817083.title: Plants
817083.description: All life depends on plants.    Threats to plant communities range from the destruction of large areas of trees through logging, to pollution from fertilisers, car exhausts, factory emissions and sewage.    Increased fertility as a result of fertiliser pollution and nitrogen deposition  results in a decline in the diversity of plant species with vegetation becoming increasingly dominated by fewer, more competitive species

links.title: Plant Talk
links.description: A magazine providing information, encouragement and advice on plant conservation.

links.title: California Native Plant Society
links.description: The CNPS is a non-profit organization dedicated to the appreciation and conservation of California native plants through education, science, horticulture and advocacy.

links.title: Maryland Native Plant Society
links.description: Dedicated to Protecting, Conserving, and Restoring Maryland's Native Plants and Habitats.

links.title: Plantlife
links.description: The wild plant charity, which carries out plant species and habitat conservation, owns and manages nature reserves, campaigns, and raises awareness through education.

links.title: Center for Plant Conservation
links.description: A national consortium of 28 botanical gardens and arboreta dedicated to saving America's endangered plants.

links.title: Botanic Gardens Conservation International
links.description: Provides technical guidance, data and support for botanic gardens in almost 100 countries worldwide.

links.title: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew
links.description: Housing the largest living plant collection in the world, Kew Gardens also undertakes research into taxonomy, economic and ethnobotany and conservation.

links.title: Native Plant Trust
links.description: Owns and manages seven sanctuaries, protecting rare species as well as examples of New England habitats. In the wild, they monitor the survival of hundreds of rare plants and provide habitat management advice and information.

links.title: Plant Conservation Unit
links.description: A small unit within the University of Cape Town's Faculty of Science, undertaking research and extension and post-graduate teaching directed at improving the conservation status of the Cape Floristic Region.

links.title: Washington Rare Plant Conservation Program
links.description: Dedicated to conserving Washington's native rare plants through methods including ex situ conservation, rare plant monitoring, research, reintroduction and education.

links.title: Plant Ecology and Nature Conservation Group
links.description: Carries out ecological research aimed at gaining insight into processes at the ecosytem and population level and uses those insights to optimise nature conservation.

links.title: Orchid Conservation Coalition
links.description: The OCC is an organization made up of people, orchid societies, and orchid businesses, dedicated to raising awareness and money for orchid and habitat preservation.

links.title: Far Reaches Botanical Conservancy
links.description: Engages in horticultural expeditions with the aim of introducing and preserving plants that are at risk of extinction in their native habitats. Based in Washington, USA.

links.title: International Tree Foundation
links.description: Plant and preserve trees. Information is given about the society, tree preservation orders, the ribbon campaign and events.

links.title: Ecosia
links.description: A green search engine which donates at least 80% of its advertising revenue to a rainforest protection programm run by the WWF.

links.title: Vietnam Biodiversity & Conservation Research
links.description: Information about the research undertaken by the Institute of Ecology and Biological Resources, Vietnam, including a project overview, description of research sites and future plans.

links.title: Frontier: Matt Stead Vietnam Rainforest Research
links.description: Details and results of Matt's part in a Frontier expedition to study and conserve biodiversity in northern Vietnam's rainforest.

links.title: Ceiba Foundation for Tropical Conservation
links.description: Nonprofit organization dedicated to the preservation and rehabilitation of tropical habitats, and the conservation of their plants and animals. Details on four projects in Ecuador.

links.title: Falkland Islands
links.description: Information about the Falkland Islands, its wildlife and conservation issues.

links.title: Canadian Department of Fisheries and Oceans
links.description: Conservation and sustainable resource use of marine and freshwater habitats.

links.title: Slovak Wildlife Society
links.description: An Anglo-Slovak initiative supporting conservation projects in Slovakia.

links.title: CEEweb
links.description: A network of organizations committed to the conservation of biodiversity in Central and Eastern Europe.

817137.title: Invasive Species
817137.description:
Invasive species are organisms (usually transported by humans) which successfully establish themselves in, and then overcome, otherwise intact, pre-existing native ecosystems. Expanding global trade and communication have contributed to the mixing of faunas and floras across biogeographical boundaries. This process, together with habitat destruction, has been a major cause of extinction throughout the world in the past few hundred years.

The scientific investigation of invasive species includes chronicling their spread and impact, but also study of why and how some species are successful invaders.

Biologists are trying to characterize the ability to invade, in the hope that incipient invasions can be predicted and stopped.

816899.title: Impacts and Indicators
816899.description: The effects and influences of climate change are transmitted through air, land, water, animal and plant life, and human health.   Evidence of ecological impacts - gathered by observation, modeling and experimentation - is provided by indicators that measure things such as temperature, precipitation, storms, sea levels, atmospheric ozone, crop yields, human health, and the appearance, behavior and abundance of insects, birds, and animals in the wild.  "Indicators are designed to provide clear signals about something of interest. Indicators communicate information about the status of things, and, when recorded over time, can yield valuable information about changes or trends. The values of an indicator over time can inform decisions about whether intervention is desirable or necessary, which of various interventions might yield the best results, and how successful interventions have been. Indicators therefore can and should guide policy and help direct research." Commission on Geosciences, Environment and Resources (CGER)

816974.title: Impact Assessment
816974.description:
Simply stated, impact assessment is identification of future consequences of a current or proposed action.
Environmental impact assessment is currently required by laws in many nations of the world. Environmental impact assessment is an intensely interdisciplinary process that utilizes the biological, physical, and social sciences in analyzing the potential impacts of an action and in devising strategies for minimizing or preventing such impacts.
Closely related fields that are also covered in this category include life cycle analysis of products and social impact assessment.

816958.description: The World Commission on Environment and Development (the Brundtland Commission), defined "sustainable development" as follows in the report Our Common Future (Oxford : Oxford University Press, 1987):      "Sustainable development is development that meets the     needs of the present without compromising the ability of      future generations to meet their own needs. It contains      within it two key concepts: the concept of "needs", in particular the essential needs of the world's poor, to which overriding priority should be given; and the idea of limitations imposed by the state of technology and social organization on the environment's ability to meet present and future needs."     Sustainability can encompass many things and can be pursued on several different levels and scales. This section of the Open Directory addresses global-scale sustainability, regional and community sustainability, and sustainable living in daily lives. ("Think globally, act locally.")

816960.title: Brownfields Utilization
816960.description: Areas of the physical environment, typically a piece of real estate previously owned and used by a chemical or related manufacturing or processing business, that have become contaminated to such an extent that they are not granted permits for use in the town or city where they are located.  However, brownfields may be able to be "rehabilitated" or used wisely, in such a way as to minimize dangers to new users. These are brownfields.   Brownfield utilization can be extremely important for any given town or city because the site may be at the heart of the industrial center of the old city or town.  For an example of a city where the corporation left the site and refuses to permit brownfield use, see Schenectady, NY. For a site that is the opposite and has had corporate cooperation with local authorities and environmental engineers see "Positive Example."
