links.title: ICDBL
links.description: International Committee for the Defense of the Breton Language, with branches in the US and Canada.

814885.title: Cornish
814885.description: Cornish is a Brythonic-Celtic language of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 2000 fluent speakers in the Duchy of Cornwall in England.  Cornish is also known as Kernowek, Kernewek and Curnoack.

links.title: Cornish Language Page
links.description: Brief history, current state and advice on learning the language in Australia, plus information on Kevren, a Cornish newsletter for Australians.

links.title: Warlinenn (Online)
links.description: Online magazine devoted to the study and revival of the Cornish language. It includes a dictionary, a phrasebook, and a glossary of Cornish placenames.

links.title: A Small Taste of the Cornish Language
links.description: Contains phrases, counting words and a song in Modern Cornish.

links.title: Languages-On-The-Web: Best Cornish Links
links.description: Collection of links to sites dealing with Cornwall, its culture and the Cornish language, from a language portal.

links.title: An Bibel Kernewek
links.description: Project translating the bible into Cornish. It is hoped to publish the New Testament in 2004.

links.title: Cornish Language Course, Kernewek dre Gesroesweyth (KDG)
links.description: Texts and slides referring to an online course in Cornish. By Leslie Sitek in the Netherlands.

links.title: Agan Tavas - Our Language
links.description: Organization in Cornwall, England, promoting the use of the Cornish language. Includes information about membership, classes and conversation groups.

814874.title: Gaulish
814874.description: Gaulish is an extinct Celtic member of the Indo-European language family formerly spoken in Northern Italy, France and Britain.

814873.title: Irish
814873.description: Irish is a Goidelic-Celtic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 260,000 people living in Ireland, Isle of Mann, Scotland and a handful of countries outside the British Isles.  Irish is also known as Erse, Irish Gaelic and Gaeilge.

links.title: Muintearas
links.description: Organization based in Tír an Fhia, Leitir Móir, County Galway, Ireland. It is dedicated to the survival of the Irish language with particular attention to the Gaeltacht, or areas of Ireland where Irish is still spoken widely. Details on the teaching of Irish to children.

links.title: Old-Irish-L
links.description: Mailing list for the discussion of Old Irish.

links.title: Irish Gaelic Reference Documents and Links
links.description: Irish language teaching and reference materials, flashcards, books, and lessons, from a teacher based in Portland, Oregon.

links.title: IrishSayings.com
links.description: Sample audio files of Irish everyday phrases and proverbs.

814883.title: Manx
814883.description: Manx is a nearly extinct Goidelic-Celtic member of the Indo-European language family spoken on the Isle of Man.  Manx is also known as Gaelg, Gailck and Manx Gaelic.

links.title: Manx: Bringing a language back from the dead
links.description: The BBC reports on the revival of a once-extinct Celtic language.

814875.title: Scottish Gaelic
814875.description: Scottish Gaelic, also known as Gaidhlig and Gaelic, is a Goidelic-Celtic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 94,000 people.  Most speakers are located in the North and central counties of Ross and the islands of Hebrides and Skye with smaller numbers in Australia, Canada and the United States.

links.title: Rampant Scotland: Gaelic and Scots Language
links.description: Links to web pages related to Gaelic, with description. Also includes links to Scots language information.  Part of the Rampant Scotland directory.

links.title: Slighe nan Gaidheal
links.description: Seattle's Scottish Gaelic language and cultural society. Educational events, concerts, networking.

links.title: CNAP
links.description: Comann nam Pàrant provides information on Gaelic medium education and the opportunity to communicate with parents on the message board and is bilingual.

links.title: Comunn na Gàidhlig
links.description: Bilingual site of the main Scottish Gaelic language development agency.

links.title: Comunn Gàidhlig Astràilia - The Scottish Gaelic Association of Australia
links.description: A non-profit organisation which supports the language and culture of Scottish Gaels in Australia. Members include native speakers and learners. Welcomes contact from anyone with an interest in these subjects.

links.title: Scotland FAQ - Scottish Gaelic information
links.description: The Gaelic section of Craig Cockburn's Scotland guide. Information about Gaelic and learning Gaelic for newcomers to the language.

links.title: Scotland FAQ - Gaelic song and music
links.description: The Gaelic song and music section of Craig Cockburn's Scotland guide. This section covers Gaelic song and music, including bands, musical styles, traditional music and singing information

links.title: Wikipedia: Scottish_Gaelic_Language
links.description: An introduction and overview, with many links

links.title: Gaelic Society of Moscow
links.description: The Gaelic Society of Moscow is the Scottish Gaelic not-for-profit organisation in Russia. It studies Gaelic Scotland, its language, its people and its culture.

links.title: Gàidhlig (Scottish Gaelic) Local Studies
links.description: On the Linguae Celticae site by Kurt Duwe.  These studies deal with local communities which were predominantly Gaelic-speaking at the end of the 19th century. Based mainly (but not exclusively) on local population census information the reports strive to examine the state of the language through the ages from 1881 until today.

links.title: An Comunn Gàidhealach America
links.description: (The Gaelic Society of America) Organization promoting and supporting Gaelic language, music and culture in North America.  Information about events, activities, learning opportunities, and membership.

links.title: Sorley MacLean Online
links.description: Home of "Urras Shomhairle", the Sorley MacLean Trust.  A huge amount of information on the world famous 20th century Gaelic poet Sorley MacLean, his life, poetry, etc.

links.title: Fòram na Gàidhlig
links.description: Bulletin board with Gaelic discussion, news and help to learners.  In Gaelic and English.  Questions about the language from learners are welcomed.

links.title: Celtic Lyrics Corner
links.description: Includes the lyrics for hundreds of Scottish Gaelic and Irish Gaelic songs, mostly from album covers.  Includes a good port à beul section.

links.title: Tobar an Dualchais
links.description: Thousands of archive sound recordings of Gaelic and Scots from the School of Scottish Studies, the BBC, and the Canna Collection

814876.title: Lessons Online
814876.description: Gaelic lessons through the medium of English available on the Internet

links.title: Beag air Bheag
links.description: The BBC Alba Gaelic learning website with ten learning topics, extensive audio examples, conversations, self-assessment quizzes and Gaelic songs.

links.title: Scottish Gaelic learners' materials online
links.description: Links to many different online lessons sites

links.title: Save Scottish Gaelic
links.description: Information on Scottish Gaelic including an online forum for Gaelic supporters.

links.title: Gaidhlig Language News
links.description: Blog with news about the Gaelic language in Scotland.

814880.title: Singers
814880.description: Singers singing in Gàidhlig, and groups with Gàidhlig singers

links.title: Dàimh
links.description: A group with fluent Gaelic speakers playing Scottish, Irish and Cape Breton music

links.title: Mairead NicAonghais
links.description: Maggie MacInnes - Gaelic singer and clàrsach player from Barra

links.title: Mairead Bennett
links.description: Gaelic singer, folklorist, writer, lecturer, and storyteller.  Originally from Skye.

links.title: Margaret Stewart
links.description: Traditional Gaelic singer from Lewis

links.title: Runrig
links.description: Scottish/Gaelic rock band, often in UK Top Ten, gold disc winners, with large international fan-base especially in Denmark and Germany, cult status

links.title: Fiona NicCoinnich
links.description: Fiona Mackenzie - Gaelic singer and teacher, from Morayshire, living in Dingwall

links.title: Maggie Carchrie
links.description: Gaelic singer and teacher of Scottish dance and song, from Massachusetts, USA.

links.title: Christina Stewart
links.description: Home website of a traditional Highland singer, exploring her passion for Scotland's traditions of song. Includes details of workshops, project, performances and albums.

links.title: Beathag Mhoireasdan
links.description: Gàidhlig singer, actress and teacher from Uig, Lewis.

links.title: An Introduction to the Gaelic Music Tradition
links.description: An article exploring the history and development of Gaelic music, song and dance.

links.title: The Island Tapes
links.description: Silent black and white movies from the 20's and 30's with new live performances by four Gaelic musicians.

814881.title: Translation Services
814881.description: English to Gaelic and Gaelic to English translation or interpreting services

links.title: Eadar-Theangachadh Akerbeltz
links.description: Gaelic<>English translation service based in Glasgow

814886.title: Welsh
814886.description: Welsh is a Celtic member of the Proto-Indo-European language family spoken by over 20% of the population of Wales.      Welsh is closely related to Cornish, known as Kernowek, Kernewek and Curnoack.      The Welsh language subcategory is focused on the language itself - grammar and history. This category does not offer dictionaries.  Rather, the user can use the @link to find Welsh dictionaries and/or language programs.

links.title: Cymdeithas Madog
links.description: Cymdeithas Madog (Welsh Studies Institute in North America), based in Duvall, WA (USA), is a non-profit organization dedicated to helping North Americans learn, use and enjoy the Welsh language.

links.title: Geiriadur Prifysgol Cymru - A Dictionary of the Welsh Language
links.description: The first standard historical dictionary of the Welsh language (prepared at the University of Wales). The site has information on the history of the project, statistics, bibliography, as well as a sample page and a list of publications. On 6/12/2001 the final draft entry for the Dictionary was made.

links.title: Acen Welsh Learners' Resource
links.description: Information for learners, tutors and teachers about learning Welsh as a second language.

links.title: gwales.com
links.description: Database of Welsh language and Welsh interest books from the Welsh Books Council. Books can be ordered through the council for delivery from a bookstore of choice. Bilingual site (Welsh-English).

links.title: LLyfrgell Owen
links.description: An initiative which aims to collaboratively build an on-line library of Welsh-language texts.

links.title: Catchphrase 2002
links.description: Audio clips and free language lessons to download, to be used in conjunction with a BBC radio programme of the same name.

links.title: National Language Centre for Wales
links.description: Full-time residential Welsh language teaching centre, based in Nant Gwrtheyrn (Wales). Course descriptions, frequently asked questions, accommodation and curriculum information. Bilingual site (Welsh-English).

links.title: Not Since School
links.description: A Welsh learner's diary and practice writing.

814732.title: Germanic
814732.description: Germanic languages are a subgrouping of the Indo-European language family and are broadly divided into the Eastern branch consisting of Gothic, the Northern branch which encompasses the Scandinavian languages and the largest branch, Western-Germanic, subgrouped into English, Frisian, German and Low Saxon/Low Franconian languages.

links.title: Society for Germanic Linguistics
links.description: Founded in 1968 to serve scholars teaching and researching in Germanic Linguistics and Philology. Journal of Germanic Linguistics, newsletter, and conference updates.

links.title: Anglogermanica
links.description: This online electronic journal will focus on linguistic and literary themes, both general and specific, within the fields of English and German studies.

links.title: Germanic Lexicon Project
links.description: The site contains digitized versions of dictionaries and grammars of the early Germanic languages, including Gothic, Old English, Old Icelandic, Old High German, Old Saxon, and reconstructed Proto-Germanic.

814737.title: Afrikaans
814737.description: Afrikaans is a Low-Franconian-Germanic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by at least 6.3 million speakers worldwide though mainly concentrated in South Africa but also found in Botswana, Malawi, Namibia and Zambia.

links.title: Afrikaans Language Museum - Afrikaanse Taal Museum
links.description: Information about the museum (where the Association of True Afrikaners was founded in 1875) and a survey of the social history and present-day role of the language.

814742.title: Danish
814742.description: Danish is an East Scandinavian member of the Germanic subgroup of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 5.3 million people, principally concentrated in Denmark but also found in Canada, Germany, Greenland, Norway, Sweden, United Arab Emirates and the United States.  Danish is also known as Dansk, Central Danish and Sjaelland.

links.title: Learn to Speak Danish
links.description: Origin of Danish orthography, phonology, and grammar.

814745.title: Dutch
814745.description: Dutch is a Low Franconian member of the Western-Germanic subgroup of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 20 million people worldwide, slightly more than half of which live in the Netherlands with the remainder spread across at least 12 other countries.  The Dutch terms for the language are "Nederlands", or, informally, "Hollands".

links.title: Learn Dutch
links.description: Well presented language course combining texts, pictures and sound, including forums and tests.

links.title: D4E (Dutch for English) Homepage
links.description: Mailing list on Dutch language learning and related items for English speakers.

links.title: Dutch Online Grammar Course
links.description: A thorough introduction to all aspects of Dutch grammar.

814747.title: English
814747.description: English is a West-Germanic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by 341 million people as a first language and more that 508 million in at least 104 countries.

links.title: The Xtag Project
links.description: Lexicalized Tree Adjoining Grammar (TAG) project, a geometric method for analysing English grammar.

links.title: The American Language by H.L. Mencken
links.description: Online publication of the full text of a classic book on the history and nature of American English, with particular attention paid to the discrepancies between British and American English.

links.title: World Wide Words
links.description: More than 1400 pages which explore the history, evolution, byways, quirks, and curiosities of the English language. A weekly newsletter is sent by e-mail and RSS.

links.title: Survey of English Usage
links.description: University College (London) researchers focusing on grammar and linguistics, plus world-wide usage. Includes the "Internet Grammar of English".

links.title: The American Dialect Homepage
links.description: Resource for both linguistic and literary scholars about regional varieties of English in the United States and Canada. Includes maps, annotated link directory, and dialectology bibliography.

links.title: A Study of the Formants of the Pure Vowels of British English
links.description: MA Thesis (1960) of Prof. J.C. Wells of the University of London concerning the pronunciation of vowels in "Received Pronunciation".

links.title: Loosely Speaking
links.description: Requests that the reader take a quick, 5-question survey to determine usage in various geographical locations.

links.title: International Dialects of English Archive
links.description: Extensive collection of freely downloadable recordings of real people speaking English in their own native accents and dialects.

links.title: Neologism Cliche Aphorism and Novel Language Pattern
links.description: Extensive list of new sayings, cliches, aphorisms, and neologisms. Has additional pages  on related language matters.

links.title: Guardian Unlimited - Notes and Queries: Anorak
links.description: Discusses the meaning and derivation of the term anorak as applied to a person.

links.title: Lake Superior State University - Banished Words List
links.description: Started in 1976 by W.T. (Bill) Rabe as a tongue-in-cheek safeguard against misuse, overuse, and uselessness of the English language. New words are chosen each year.

814760.title: American Dialects
814760.description: Sites concerning variations and dialects of English spoken in the United States.

links.title: Lexicon of Bawlamarese
links.description: A collection of alternative pronunciations and local jargon from Baltimore, Maryland.

links.title: Pittsburghese.com
links.description: A guide to pronunciation, phrases, and local terminology if Pittsburgh and western Pennsylvania. Audio quiz and 'translator' available.

links.title: Organization of Dialect Diversity in North America
links.description: Full text of the paper by William Labov. Sociolinguistic research on linguistic change in urbanized areas of North America, leading to increased dialect diversity.

links.title: North American  Dialect Links
links.description: Includes American, Canadian, Native American and Bermudan.

links.title: American Dialect Society
links.description: A scholarly association dedicated to the study of the English language in North America.

links.title: Pop vs. Soda
links.description: Plots the geographic distribution of the different terms used to refer to carbonated soft-drinks in the United States. Requests participation in the survey.

links.title: The Big Apple
links.description: Barry Popik, Author/ editor of an online dictionary investigating the origins of American words, names, quotations and phrases.

links.title: Dictionary of American Regional English
links.description: Word usage across the United States is shown in the results of a language survey of American English undertaken between 1965 and 1970 and supplemented by written materials.

links.title: The Best of British: The American's Guide to Speaking British
links.description: The differences between American and British English, explored by a Brit living in Texas.

links.title: English Usage in the UK and USA
links.description: A light-hearted look at some differences between English as spoken on both sides of the Atlantic.

814761.title: Manual Forms
814761.description: Forms of English that are communicated through the hands, but are not separate languages. For distinct languages, see Sign Languages.

links.title: S.E.E. Center
links.description: Instruction and resource materials for families interested in teaching their children using Seeing Exact English.

links.title: National Cued Speech Association
links.description: National nonprofit organization providing advocacy for Cued Speech.

links.title: Cued Speech Association UK
links.description: Facts, publications, and news. Also provides a listing of classes in the United Kingdom.

links.title: Language Matters
links.description: Agency providing cued language transliterators and classes for Cued Speech.

links.title: DailyCues
links.description: Community-driven website for cued speech including news, events, testing preparation, connecting with other cuers and learning from experts.

links.title: Northern Virginia Cued Speech Association
links.description: Advocacy and education organization supporting Cued Speech in Northern Virginia.

links.title: TECUnit
links.description: Known as the Testing, Evaluation, and Certification Unit, this organization is responsible for establishing and maintaining national standards for the profession of cued language transliteration.

814748.title: Neologisms
814748.description: Neologisms are words that have been recently created, and may sometimes find their way into general use. Some arise because of new circumstances or inventions for which no word previously existed, but others are created for purely humorous purposes.

links.title: Lexicopoeia
links.description: Provides a definition, and examples created by Professor Mikhail Epstein.

links.title: Neologism Competition
links.description: A long-running monthly competition for readers, by Bob Levey of "The Washington Post". Includes links to past results.

links.title: Cyber-Neologoliferation
links.description: Article by James Gleick in "The New York Times" explains how new words are added to the Oxford English Dictionary.

814758.title: Old English
814758.description: Old English is a member of the Germanic family of the Indo-European languages. It is the earliest form of the English language. It was written and spoken in England up to approximately 1150 CE. Its written records include the earliest known poems in the English language and a considerable body of prose.

links.title: Old English Alphabet
links.description: Shows the form, pronunciation, and Modern English equivalent of each letter in the Old English alphabet. Includes a sample text from an Old English manuscript, a transcription of the text, and a modern English translation of the text. Also includes several videos. From the Omniglot site.

links.title: Changes in the English Language: a Comparison of Old, Middle, and Modern English
links.description: Displays Old English, Middle English, and Modern English versions of each verse in Luke 2:1-19.

links.title: Old English Word Search Engines
links.description: Provides two search tools. One finds all occurrences of a word or words in the Anglo-Saxon Poetic Records (ASPR). The other finds all occurrences of a word or words in the entire Old English corpus.

links.title: Prosody of Old and Middle English
links.description: Explains the poetic principles and techniques employed in Old English and Middle English poetry. Covers the distinctive features of Old English verse, the transition from Old English to Middle English poetic forms, foreign influences on Middle English poetry, and the alliterative revival.

links.title: Changes in the Language to the Days of Chaucer
links.description: Studies the development of Old English and Middle English. Covers grammar, pronunciation, spelling, vocabulary, and dialects.

links.title: Old English: An Overview
links.description: An introduction to the key features of Old English. Covers the historical context, distinguishing features of Old English, the beginning of Old English, the end of Old English, dialects, verbs, derivation of large groups of words from the same base words, and sound changes.

links.title: Old English Compared to Modern English
links.description: Merriam-Webster Online article uses a passage from Aelfric's Homily on St. Gregory to show the similarities and differences between Old English and Modern English. Also compares Middle English to Modern English and describes the Germanic roots of Old English.

links.title: History of English
links.description: Describes the development of the English language from pre-history to the present. In addition to Old English, covers the Indo-European language family, the Germanic branch of this family, the Celts and Romans, Middle English, early modern English, late modern English, and English today.

links.title: Anglo-Saxon Runes
links.description: Gives a detailed account of runes, including a table that summarizes information about each rune, a history of runes, a description of the role of runes in Anglo-Saxon culture, and other topics. From Wikipedia.

links.title: Parable of the Prodigal Son in Different Stages of English
links.description: Gives Old English, Middle English, Early Modern English, and Modern English versions of Luke 15:11-32 and allows side-by-side comparisons of different versions.

links.title: Beginner's Guide to Old English Metre
links.description: Explains the metrical features common to all Old English poetry. Includes exercises and answers, a glossary of terms, and a bibliography. By Alaric Hall and Sheryl McDonald.

links.title: Old English Metre: A Brief Guide
links.description: An introduction to the metrical features shared by all Old English poems. By Daniel Paul O'Donnell.

links.title: Old English Pronunciation
links.description: A video that shows how to pronounce the letters of the Old English alphabet.

links.title: Old English
links.description: Wikipedia article on the Old English language. Covers the history of Old English, word borrowings, dialects, sound system, grammar, alphabets, and other topics. Includes examples of the language taken from Old English literature.

links.title: History of English
links.description: Wikipedia article on the history of the English language. Covers Proto-English, Old English, Middle English, Early Modern English, and Modern English and gives examples of writing from each stage. Each section of the article contains a link to a full Wikipedia article on the given stage.

links.title: Old English in the Lord of the Rings
links.description: Shows how J.R.R. Tolkien used Old English words to name people, places, and things in his famous trilogy. By Dave Wilton.

links.title: Alliterative Verse
links.description: Wikipedia article on the characteristics of alliterative verse and the use of alliteration in Old English, Middle English, Old Norse, Old Saxon, and Old High German poetry.

links.title: Old English Glossaries: Creating a Vernacular
links.description: An introduction to Old English glossaries. Covers the origin and purpose of Old English glossaries, describes the different types of glossaries, and explains their relationship to later dictionaries. Includes bibliography. By Antonette diPaolo Healey.

links.title: Anglo-Saxon Runes
links.description: Shows the form, name, and modern English equivalent of each letter in the runic alphabet. Also includes a sample runic text, the equivalent text in the Old English alphabet, and a modern English translation. From the Omniglot site.

links.title: Old English Glosses (a Collection)
links.description: Provides lists of Old English glosses that appear in manuscripts of Latin works by Aldhelm, Bede, Prudentius and other authors (one list for each manuscript). Each list shows Latin words and equivalent Old English words side by side. Includes introduction and notes. By Herbert Dean Meritt.

links.title: Anglo-Saxon Glosses and Glossaries: an Introduction
links.description: An exposition of Old English glosses and glossaries by Patrizia Lendinara.

links.title: The English-Speaking Union
links.description: An international, charitable, membership organization which works through exchanges, scholarships, speaking competitions, conferences and English language programs worldwide.

814763.title: Slang
814763.description: Sites found in this category will generally be listings of English that is not considered to be standard.  This means that the language is free from the grammar and spelling restrictions of mainstream English and has been shaped by the idiosyncrasies of a particular culture or group of people.

links.title: American Slanguages
links.description: Talk like the locals in cities in America and around the world. The hick to hip translation guide.

links.title: Filters Magazine Slang Repository
links.description: Late 20th-century urban slang with pop culture influences.  Alphabetized and includes definitions.

links.title: Urban Dictionary
links.description: The vocabulary of everyday life.

links.title: Australian Slang Dictionary
links.description: Collection of Australian slang words.

links.title: Twists, Slugs and Roscoes: A Glossary of Hardboiled Slang
links.description: Definitions of the lingo used in the crime fiction and movies of the '30's and '40's.

814765.title: Idioms
814765.description: Sites in this category should focus on expressions in English whose meaning can not be understood if taken literally.  This language is called the 'idiom' and is actually comprised of real words found in standard English.

links.title: American Idiomatic Expressions
links.description: A comprehensive list of idioms, browsable through alphabetical links.  Includes parts of speech, definitions and example sentences.

links.title: The Idiom Connection
links.description: Listed alphabetically and by subject, along with quizzes.

814764.title: Quizzes
814764.description: Sites found in this category should provide English slang quizzes.  Slang is English that is not considered to be standard.  This means that the language is free from the grammar and spelling restrictions of mainstream English and has been shaped by the idiosyncrasies of a particular culture or group of people.

links.title: Unifon--one sound per symbol--phonetic transcription
links.description: The Unifon site contains several Phonemic transcription systems for English. A 40-phonogram ascii-bet changeable to a more pleasing extended alphabet with the installation of the Unifon font. A good, simple place to start a study of phonemic writing systems.

links.title: Simplified Spelling Society
links.description: Aims and objectives, literature of the society and leaflets, practicalities, reform proposals, computer programs, membership. Also issues "Journal of the Simplified Spelling Society". Related sites and links.

links.title: Shavian ConScript Unicode Standard
links.description: Unicode listing under U+E700 - U+E72F for Shavian, also known as the "Shaw Alphabet"

814744.title: Faroese
814744.description: Faroese is the official language of the roughly 50,000 people living in the Faroe Islands, an archipelago about half-way between Scotland and Iceland. Faroese is closely related to Icelandic, and less closely to the other Scandinavian languages (Danish, Norwegian, and Swedish), but definitely distinct from all of them.

814766.title: Frisian
814766.description: Frisian is a West Germanic language still widely spoken in parts of the northern Netherlands (where it has official status), as well as by two very small (and disappearing) communities in northern Germany. Frisian is the continental Germanic language most closely related to English.

links.title: Fryske Akademy (Frisian Academy)
links.description: Institution (headquarters in Ljouwert/Leeuwarden) devoted to the standardization and preservation of the Frisian language. Trilingual site (Frisian, English and Dutch).

814739.title: German
814739.description: German is a Western-Germanic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 100 million first-language speakers and as many as 128 million people in as many as 40 countries.   German is also known as Deutsch, Hochdeutsch and High German.   This category is for noncommercial sites about German. This includes scientific considerations, educational resources, and reference materials.

links.title: ThougthCo - Learning and Teaching German
links.description: Language-learning tips and lessons and a library of links to resources online.

links.title: Web German
links.description: A center for learning with the Internet. Interactive exercises, audio files, literature, games, comics, news, fiction and other useful resources to help you learn online.

links.title: BBC: Languages: German
links.description: Includes courses, phrases, and travel information.

links.title: German Words and Phrases
links.description: Basic words and phases for studying German.

links.title: Deutsch Lernen
links.description: Beginner's and advanced German lessons, mainly focusing on grammar.

links.title: Gene Moutoux's Home Page
links.description: Fairy tales and letters (correspondence) for intermediate students, as well as a course for beginners.

links.title: Toms Deutschseite
links.description: Collection of exercises, grammar rules, hints and links for learners of German as a Foreign Language.

links.title: Deutsche Welle: German Courses
links.description: German language courses for teachers and students in more than 30 languages.

links.title: GermanPod101
links.description: Podcasts and learning resources that teach German from beginning to advanced levels. Sign-up is required.

links.title: German Dialects on the Internet: Web Resources for German Language Teachers
links.description: Collection of selected and filtered resources for use as a teaching aid by high school teachers and college instructors.

814741.title: Grammar
814741.description: This category is for sites exclusively about German grammar. Sites with more general information including grammar can be found in the parent category Science/Social_Sciences/Language_and_Linguistics/Natural_Languages/Indo-European/Germanic/German.

links.title: Internet Handbook of German Grammar
links.description: Topics covered include adjectives, auxiliary verbs, verb inflections and the subjunctive. Features extensive explanations and examples.

links.title: Learn German Grammar
links.description: Online manual of German language for English speakers, with an emphasis on grammar rules

814738.title: Gothic
814738.description: Gothic is an East-Germanic member of the Indo-European language family formerly spoken in Bulgaria, central Europe and Ukraine.  The last known language communities survived into the 18th century.

links.title: Gothic Verbs

814781.title: Catalan

Catalan is also known as Català, Bacaves and Catalonian and is one of the group of western neo-Latin languages, together with French, Portuguese and Spanish, the most widely-spoken languages in the same family. Catalan is spoken in a large area (68,000 km2) in the east of Spain (Catalonia, the Balearic Islands, Valencia, the Franja - the area in Aragon bordering on Catalonia - and other municipalities in Murcia that border on Valencia), Andorra, the south of France (North Catalonia – the Department of Pyrénées Orientales) and in the Sardinian city of l'Alguer (Alghero). Catalan in all its variants is spoken over an area with a population of 10 million.

Romansh is also known as Romansch, Rheto-Romance, Rhaeto-Romance and Romanche. Rumantsch Grischun is the common written language of the Romansh people: It is based to a large extent on the three written idioms used in the Romansh-speaking Grisons, Sursilvan (Surselva), Vallader (Lower Engadine) and Surmiran (Surmeir/Albula Valley). In many cases, however, it also considers the two minor idioms Sutsilvan (Val Schons) and Put?r (Upper Engadine), as well as the various regional and local variants. [Adapted from: Lia Rumantsch]

814870.title: Proto-Indo-European
814870.description: English, Spanish, Russian and Hindi, just to take four common examples, are languages that can be derived from a common ancestor. This ancestor is usually called Proto-Indo-European (PIE). The web pages collected in this category are concerned with one or several aspects of the study of PIE. This is a multi-disciplinary area. Linguists are interested in the reconstructed phonology, grammar and vocabulary of PIE. Archaeologists and historians debate the question of where and when PIE was spoken, and which archaeological culture can be identified with its speakers. Finally, ethnographers and scholars of comparative religion wonder about the culture and religion of these speakers, as reconstructable from the myths and religions of known Indo-European-speaking peoples, and from the archaeological sites associated with them.

links.title: The Spread of the Indo-Europeans
links.description: Scholarly article by Frederik Kortlandt on the dating of the spreading of the Indo-Europeans based on information obtained from both linguistic and archaeological research.

links.title: Indo-European: Possible Homeland & Migrations Slideshow
links.description: Introductory page on the homeland problem, and slideshow of homeland and possible migrations after mainstream opinion.

814853.title: Slavic
814853.description: The Slavic family is divided into three branches: East Slavic including Belarusan, Russian and Ukrainian; West Slavic including Czech, Polish, Slovak and Sorbian; South Slavic including Bulgarian, Macedonian, Old Church Slavonic, Serbo-Croatian and Slovenian.

links.title: Slavic Languages in Head-Driven Phrase Structure Grammar
links.description: Publications, mailing list, and links related to the linguistic work carried out within the formal linguistic (generative) framework.

links.title: Balto-Slavic Accentuation: Some News Travels Slowly
links.description: Scholarly article (1994) on the history of Balto-Slavic accentuation patterns, by Frederik Kortlandt.

links.title: Bad Theory, Wrong Conclusions: M. Halle on Slavic Accentuation
links.description: Discussion of accentuation in the Slavic languages, through criticism of Mr Halle's work on the subject. Paper by Frederik Kortlandt, presented to a congress of Slavists held in Ljubljana, Slovenia, in 2003.

links.title: From Proto-Indo-European to Slavic
links.description: Scholarly article (2002) Frederik Kortlandt, tracing the development of Slavic phonology from its Proto-Indo-European origins.

links.title: Early Dialectal Diversity in South Slavic II
links.description: Scholarly article (2003) on variations in the historical phonology of south Slavic languages, by Frederik Kortlandt.

links.title: Early Dialectal Diversity in South Slavic I
links.description: A first attempt by Frederik Kortlandt (1982) to present a survey of dialectal phonology in the south Slavic languages.

links.title: Slavic Accentuation: A Study in Relative Chronology
links.description: Electronic version of a 1974 monograph by Frederik Kortlandt concerning the history of the Slavic accentuation system.

links.title: Wikipedia: Slavic Languages
links.description: Article about the closely related languages of the Slavic peoples, with speakers in most of Eastern Europe, much of the Balkans, parts of Central Europe, and the northern part of Asia.

814863.title: Academic Departments
814863.description: Academic departments devoted to the study of Slavic languages. If only Russian is taught, look for the site under the Russian subcat. For convenience, departments teaching East/Central European languages may be classified here, even though some languages spoken there (e.g. Hungarian, Romanian) are not Slavic.

links.title: Arizona State University  (Tempe, AZ, USA) - Russian and East European Studies Consortium (REESC)
links.description: Department involved in research, training, and outreach programs covering the lands and people of eastern Europe and Eurasia.

links.title: Hokkaido University (Japan) - Slavic Research Center
links.description: Japan's only research institute for the study of the Slavic countries. It is Japan's national center to lead and coordinate research activities in the area.

814857.title: Belarusan
814857.description: Belarusan is an Easter-Slavic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 10.2 million people principally in Belarus with smaller populations in 15 other countries.    Belarusan is also known as Belarusian, Belorussian, Bielorussian, White Russian, White Ruthenian and Byelorussian.

814858.title: Bulgarian
814858.description: Bulgarian, also known as Balgarski, is a South Slavic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 9 million people mainly in Bulgaria with smaller populations in Canada, Greece, Hungary, Israel, Moldova, Romania, Turkey, Ukraine, the United States and the region of the former Republic of Yugoslavia.

links.title: Bulgar Words and Expressions
links.description: Features of the old (Turkic) Bulgar language that have been preserved in the modern (Slavic) language.

links.title: HPSG-Based Syntactic Treebank of Bulgarian
links.description: Project to create a high quality set of syntactic structures of Bulgarian sentences within the framework of HPSG.

links.title: FASL 18 - Formal Approaches to Slavic Linguistics 18
links.description: May 15-17, 2009, Cornell University. Includes call for papers, conference program and a list of invited speakers.

814869.title: Czech
814869.description: Czech is a Western-Slavic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 12 million people mainly in the Czech Republic with 2 million speakers located in other regions and countries including Western Bohemia, Moravia, Silesia, Austria, Bulgaria, Canada, Israel, Poland, Sokvakia, Ukraine and the United States.  Czech is also known as Cestina and Bohemian.

links.title: Institute of Czech Studies, Charles University, Prague
links.description: Masters Degree program for foreigners in the language and literature, and Summer School of Slavonic Studies.

links.title: History and Czech
links.description: Short history of the language with discussion of its differentiation from other Slavic languages.

links.title: The Czech Language
links.description: Covers overview of Czech and its spoken form, alphabet and pronunciation, fiction, poems, songs, words and their forms, translations, sentences and their structure, and Czech National Corpus.

links.title: Czech
links.description: A very complete reference grammar of the Czech language, by Laura A. Janda and Charles E. Townsend. Part of the Reference Grammar Network of the Slavic and East European Language Resource Center.

links.title: Little Czech Primer in Pictures
links.description: A collection of everyday words with illustrations. Divided into verbs, nouns, and adjectives, and also indexed alphabetically.

links.title: Czech National Corpus
links.description: An academic project founded in 1994. The aim of the project is systematic mapping of Czech and other languages in comparison with Czech. Features several applications, a wiki, support centre, and repository.

links.title: Online Czech Lessons
links.description: Offers virtual lessons on Skype for learners at all levels, accompanied with YouTube channel and an iOS app.

links.title: Czech for Foreigners Portal
links.description: Features information on the Examination in the Czech language on the Level A1 as a condition for permanent residence in the CR.

links.title: CLT: Czech for Foreigners
links.description: A language studio offering courses and placement tests for foreigners.

links.title: Learn 101: Learn Czech
links.description: Offers free lessons with learning the alphabet, simple grammar rules, practice common phrases, vocabulary lists, and audio samples.

814868.title: Journals
814868.description: Academic journals devoted to the study of Slavic languages and literatures.

links.title: Slavic Studies
links.description: Annual publication devoted to Slavic and Central European studies (mostly history, politics, literature) issued by the Slavic Research Center at Hokkaido University in Japan. Full versions of the articles (in Japanese) are available in pdf files. Detailed abstracts in English online.

links.title: Journal of Slavic Linguistics
links.description: Contents and abstracts from past issues, profiles of future issues, information for authors, and subscription rates.

814867.title: Kashubian
814867.description: Kashubian (also spelled Kaszubian, Cashubian, or Cassubian) is one of the Pomeranian languages, a subset of the Slavic languages.  It is related to Polish and is still used daily by about 50,000 people today in Poland, primarily in rural areas in north central Poland.

links.title: Wikipedia: Kashubian language
links.description: General information on the history and current status of the language.

814864.title: Macedonian
814864.description:
Macedonian is a South Eastern-Slavic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 2 million people in North Macedonia as well as Greece, Albania, Bulgaria, Canada, Hungary and Slovenia.

Macedonian is also known as Makedonski, Slavic and Macedonian Slavic.

links.title: The Macedonian Language
links.description: A brief introduction to the language's history and alphabet, with a few greetings.

links.title: Macedonian
links.description: A very thorough reference grammar of the Macedonian language, by Victor Friedman. Part of the Reference Grammar Network of the Slavic and East European Language Resource Center.

links.title: Font Squirrel: Fonts that support the Macedonian language
links.description: Collection of free web fonts, suitable for writing in Macedonian.

links.title: The Future Prospects of the Macedonian Literary Language
links.description: Otto Kronsteiner asserts that the language was created in Yugoslavia in 1944 to divide Bulgarian-speaking Slavs of the region from the people of Bulgaria.

links.title: Learn 101: Macedonian
links.description: Learn through online lessons such as alphabet, adjectives, nouns, plural, gender, numbers, phrases, grammar, vocabulary, verbs, exam, audio, and translation.

814865.title: Old Church Slavonic
814865.description: Old Church Slavonic is a South Eastern-Slavonic member of the Indo-European language family formerly used as a liturgical language by members of various Orthodox and Byzantine Catholic churches.  Church Slavonic became extinct sometime between 1500 and 1800.

814854.title: Polish
814854.description: Polish, also known as Polski and Polnisch, is Lechtic member of the West-Slavic subgroup of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 44 million people, 36 million of which are in Poland, the remainder across Europe and as many as 20 countries in total.

links.title: A Concise Polish Grammar
links.description: A very thorough reference grammar of the Polish language, by Ron F. Feldstein. Part of the Reference Grammar Network of the Slavic and East European Language Resource Center.

814861.title: Russian
814861.description: Russian language, also known as "русский язык" (transliteration: russkiy yazyk), is an Eastern-Slavic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 278 million people in Russia and 30 other countries.

links.title: Russian Alphabet Tutorial
links.description: Introduces the Russian alphabet; includes some practice exercises and sound files.    Does not require Russian fonts to be installed.

links.title: Learn Russian
links.description: Vocabulary and alphabet practice, quizzes, sound files.

links.title: Wikipedia - Russian Language
links.description: A collaboratively edited article covering classification, geographic distribution, writing system, sounds, grammar, vocabulary and history of the language.

links.title: Russian
links.description: A very thorough reference grammar of the Russian language, by Edna Andrews. Part of the Reference Grammar Network of the Slavic and East European Language Resource Center.

links.title: An On-line Russian Reference Grammar
links.description: Sections organized by parts of speech. Includes Java exercises.

links.title: Russian Lessons .Net
links.description: Beginners' lessons on Russian grammar and vocabulary. Includes verb conjugations, dictionary, dual-language books and exercises.

links.title: Learn Russian Free.com
links.description: Frequency lists for over 2,000 Russian words. Sorted by parts of speech and accompanied with quizzes. English translations available.

links.title: Russian Word of the Day
links.description: Discover a new Russian word every day along with its English translation, example sentences, related words and pronunciation samples.

links.title: Russian For Everyone
links.description: Grammar lessons and exercises for elementary learners of Russian. Includes audio files, summary tables and language games.

links.title: WayToRussia.net
links.description: Get help with Russian letters, basic grammar, and key phrases for travel to Russia.

links.title: Study Russian Online
links.description: Topical lessons for beginners, word lists with exercises, articles on phonetics, tests and games.

links.title: Russian-Plus.com
links.description: Video lessons, grammar, and quizzes for beginning and intermediate learners.

links.title: Russian Word of the Day
links.description: Daily analysis of the Russian vocabulary in blog format. Authored by Don Livingston, a professor from Arizona State University.

links.title: Russian Morphological Analysis
links.description: A database that analyzes/synthesizes forms and whole paradigms of Russian words. Entry by English translations also available. Best viewed with special fonts (downloadable onsite).

links.title: Gramota.ru
links.description: A reference and information portal for the Russian language available fully in Russian. It provides a free Question & Answer service on Russian stylistic, a series of standard dictionaries, online textbooks and publications, news about the Russian language, educational games and a forum.

links.title: Online Russian Grammar at Cornell
links.description: Grammar and vocabulary explanations from the second edition of Beginning Russian adapted by the author. It presents all the major grammatical categories of Russian.

links.title: Russian National Corpus
links.description: A searchable 150 million word collection of samples of written and spoken Russian from a wide range of texts in electronic form. The corpus represents modern Russian in all the variety of genres, styles, territorial and social variants of usage.

links.title: MasterRussian.com
links.description: Lessons on grammar, vocabulary, alphabet and pronunciation. For both beginning and advanced students of Russian. Includes verb conjugation tables, dictionary, culture articles, and Russian literature with side-by-side English translations.

links.title: Russian National Corpus-based Dictionaries
links.description: A collection of dictionaries prepared by the RAS Institute of the Russian language based on the Russian National Corpus. Includes the Grammatical dictionary of Russian neologisms, the New Russian frequency dictionary, the Combinatory dictionary of Russian intensifiers, the Verbal combinatory dictionary of Russian abstract nouns.

links.title: Transparent Language's Russian Blog
links.description: Multiple bloggers write on language and culture in Russia. Topics cover Russian holidays, history, travel, current events and food. New Russian vocabulary is introduced and explained inside blog posts.

links.title: Russnet
links.description: Thematic modules for language instruction that can be used in the classroom or for independent study. Free registration required.

links.title: Russian for Free
links.description: Online Russian lessons, texts, grammar tables, dialogues and videos.

links.title: Everyday Russian
links.description: Free online Russian lessons with audio. Includes word and phrase of the week, dictations, verb conjugations, error correction exercises, tests and quizzes. [English, French, Spanish]

links.title: Очень по-русски
links.description: Russian language podcasts with transcripts for intermediate and advanced learners. Covers slang, idioms and common expressions.

links.title: TITUS Font for Slavisch-Kyrillisch
links.description: Download the TITUS font from here.

814855.title: Serbo-Croatian
814855.description: Serbo-Croatian is a South-Western Slavic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by 21 million people in Macedonia, the former Republic of Yugoslavia and 23 other countries.  Serbo-Croatian is also known as Serbian, Croatian and Montenegrin.

links.title: Serbian and Croatian Alphabets
links.description: The Cyrillic and Latin alphabets with phonetic transcription.

links.title: Sociolinguistic Analysis of Serbo-Croatian
links.description: Paper by Sean McLennan, published as part of the Calgary Working Papers in Linguistics, and covering the history, dialectology, and politics of the Serbo-Croatian language.

links.title: A Handbook of Bosnian, Croatian, and Serbian
links.description: A very thorough reference grammar of these three languages, using the Latin alphabet (although the Cyrillic equivalents are provided in the section on orthography). Authors: Wayles Brown and Theresa Alt. Part of the Reference Grammar Network of the Slavic and East European Language Resource Center.

links.title: Croatian Language - Pronunciation
links.description: Covers dialects, orthography, accent (stress), vowels and consonants.

814860.title: Slovak
814860.description: Slovak, also known as Slovakian, is a Western-Slavic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 5.5 million speakers mainly in Slovakia but also in Canada, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Ukraine, the United States and the former Republic of Yugoslavia.

links.title: Introduction to the Slovak Language
links.description: Includes an overview of the language, alphabet, numbers, greetings, calendar, and phrases.

814866.title: Slovenian
814866.description: Slovenian, also known as Slovenscina and Slovene, is a Southwestern-Slavic member of the Indo-European language family spoken mainly in Slovenia and at least 9 other countries by more than 2 million people.

links.title: Slovene for Travelers
links.description: An on-line course with sound samples.

links.title: Reverse Dictionary of the Slovenian Language
links.description: Search of more than 115,000 headwords. Interface is in English. Results give inflection and part of speech (in Slovenian).

814856.title: Sorbian
814856.description: Sorbian is a Western-Slavic member of the Indo-European language family spoken by approximately 55,000 people in Upper Saxony in eastern Germany.  Sorbian is also known as Obersorbisch, Haut Sorabe, Upper Lusatian, Wendish, Hornjoserbski and Hornoserbski.

814859.title: Ukrainian
814859.description: Ukrainian is an East-Slavic member of the Indo-European language spoken by 31 million people in Ukraine and 47 million people across 25 countries globally. This category is for sites about the Ukrainian language. Sites written in Ukrainian are listed in World/Ukrainian/.

links.title: University of Alberta (Edmonton, Canada) - Ukrainian Language Education Centre
links.description: Developers and publishers of primary and secondary materials for second-language development.

814846.title: Tocharian
814846.description: A dead language that was spoken in Chinese Turkestan (Xinjiang) during the first millennium A.D. and written in a North Indian script. It has two distinct forms, known as Tocharian A and B.

links.title: Tocharian Alphabet
links.description: GIF and JPG images with information on its origin and notable features.

links.title: Tocharian
links.description: A Tocharian-to-English dictionary with nearly 200 words. Often provides etymologies as well.

links.title: Tocharian A Texts
links.description: A very coarsely annotated collection of texts.

links.title: Tocharian B Texts
links.description: A very coarsely annotated collection of texts.

links.title: TITUS: Tocharian Manuscripts: THT
links.description: Includes transliterations and translations as well as scans of Tocharian A and Tocharian B manuscripts, from TITUS (Thesaurus Indogermanischer Text- und Sprachmaterialien [Compendium of Indo-European texts and linguistic materials])

815069.title: Cayuga
815069.description: Cayuga is one of the languages of the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois Confederacy). Only about 350 people still speak Cayuga, most in Ontario (though there are still a few Cayuga-speaking elders in New York State.)

links.title: Cayuga Language and the Cayuga Indian Tribe
links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.

links.title: Goyogohó:nǫ’
links.description: Information on Cayuga orthography, including keyboard mapping and a text example.

links.title: Wikipedia: Cayuga language
links.description: Article on the Cayuga language including a phonological inventory.

815063.title: Mingo
815063.description: Mingo is a dialect of Seneca spoken by a tribe of Seneca who left the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois confederacy) and settled in the West Virginia area. Mingo is nearly extinct now, though some in the community are trying to revive it.   Though Mingo and Seneca are mutually comprehensible, political distinctions have caused many to view them as separate languages rather than merely dialects. The Mingo call their own language Ökwe'öwé, Unötawa'ká', or Unyääsháôt.

815067.title: Mohawk
815067.description: Mohawk, called Kanien'kehaka by its own speakers, is the most-spoken languageof the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois Confederacy). It is spoken by about 3000 people, half in Canada and half in New York state.

links.title: Mohawk Language
links.description: Language-learning books, tapes, software, and video, also with some background information about the language and a writing sample.

links.title: Mohawk Language and the Mohawk Indian Tribe
links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.

links.title: Kanienʼkéha Owén:na
links.description: Information on Mohawk orthography, including keyboard mapping and a text example.

links.title: Wikipedia: Mohawk language
links.description: Article on the Mohawk language including a phonological inventory and grammatical sketch.

815066.title: Oneida
815066.description: Oneida is one of the languages of the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois Confederacy). There are around 250 speakers of Oneida in Canada and New York State.

links.title: Oneida Language Lesson
links.description: Some Oneida words, with audio files of their pronunciation.

links.title: Oneida Language and the Oneida Indian Tribe
links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.

links.title: Wikipedia: Oneida language
links.description: Article on the Oneida language including a phonological inventory.

links.title: Onyota'a:ka
links.description: Information on Oneida orthography, including keyboard mapping and a text example.

815062.title: Onondaga
815062.description: Onondaga is one of the languages of the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois Confederacy). Only around 100 speakers of Onondaga remain, most in Canada.

links.title: Onondaga Language and the Onondaga Indian Tribe
links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.

links.title: Wikipedia: Onondaga language
links.description: Article on the Onondaga language including phonology and grammatical information.

links.title: Ononda'gega'
links.description: Information about Onondaga orthography, including keyboard mapping and a text example.

815068.title: Seneca
815068.description: Seneca is one of the languages of the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois Confederacy). Around 200 speakers of Seneca remain, most in New York state.   Mingo, a dialect of Seneca, is spoken in the West Virginia region by a group of Seneca who left the Haudenosaunee. Though Mingo and standard Seneca are mutually comprehensible, political distinctions have led many to treat it as a separate language.

links.title: Seneca
links.description: Background information and a legend in the Seneca language.

links.title: Seneca Language and the Seneca Indian Tribe
links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.

links.title: Onödowága
links.description: Information on Seneca orthography, including keyboard mapping and a text example.

links.title: Wikipedia: Seneca language
links.description: Article on the Seneca language including a phonological inventory.

815065.title: Tsalagi
815065.description: Cherokee--more properly spelled Tsalagi--is an Iroquoian language with an innovative written syllabary invented by the Cherokee scholar Sequoyah. It is spoken by about 22,000 people primarily in Oklahoma and North Carolina. Though Cherokee is one of the healthier Indian languages of North America and the one in which the most literature being published, it is still in imperilled condition because of government policies as late as the fifties which enforced the removal of Cherokee children from Tsalagi-speaking homes, reducing the number of young Cherokees being raised bilingually from 75% to less than 5% today.

links.title: Noksi Press
links.description: Preservation and literary resources of Cherokee language books. Basic vocabulary and links.

links.title: Freeware Cherokee Font Information
links.description: A "rustic" Cherokee font available for download.

links.title: Tsalagi (Cherokee) Language
links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.

links.title: Wikipedia: Cherokee language
links.description: Article including a phonological inventory and grammatical information.

815070.title: Tuscarora
815070.description: Tuscarora is one of the languages of the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois Confederacy). It is spoken by no more than two dozen elders now, most in New York State.

links.title: Methods of Madness: The Tuscarora Language Committee
links.description: Article on Tuscarora language loss and preservation.

links.title: Tuscarora Language and the Tuscarora Indian Tribe
links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.

links.title: Skarù∙rę’
links.description: Information on Tuscarora orthography, including keyboard mapping and a text example.

links.title: Wikipedia: Tuscarora language
links.description: Article on the Tuscarora language including a phonological inventory.

815064.title: Wyandot
815064.description: Huron (Wendat) and Wyandot are dialects of the same, unfortunately extinct language. It was last spoken by the Huron people in Quebec in the 1910's and by the Wyandot in Oklahoma in the 1960's.

links.title: B.N.O. Walker's Wyandot Vocabulary
links.description: Short list of phonetic transcriptions.

links.title: Wendat Dialects and the Development of the Huron Alliance
links.description: Historical linguistic treatment by John Steckley of Humber College.

links.title: Vocabularies of the Shawanoese and Wyandott Languages
links.description: Report by Indian Agent Colonel John Johnston, originally published in 1858. Includes some phonetic transcriptions.

links.title: Wyandot Language and the Wyandotte/Huron Tribe
links.description: Language profile, wordlists, and cultural information.

links.title: Wikipedia: Wyandot language
links.description: Brief article including orthographic information and sample words.

815078.title: Japanese
815078.description: This category is dedicated to the Japanese language, its complicated written structure of Kanji, Katakana, and Hiragana; its numerous dialects, grammar, and all other aspects of communication in Japanese.

links.title: Osaka Shoin Women's College
links.description: The Japanese Language Research Center.

links.title: All the Japanese Slang You Can Stand
links.description: Dictionary of slang terms, with an introductory page offering general advice and book recommendations to people interested in learning Japanese.

links.title: Japanese wa, mo, ga, wo, na, no
links.description: Scholarly study of the syntax of the six most common post-nominal particles in Japanese, by Frederik Kortlandt.

links.title: Kanji Names Project
links.description: Descriptions of Japanese names in English with kanji image files, and information on kanji books.

links.title: Nihongo: Japanese Language
links.description: Articles reflecting on miscellaneous aspects of the language, thorough resources for Japanese numbers and counters, and lengthy list of summaries of books for learning Japanese.

links.title: Origins of the Japanese Language

links.title: Otake Japanese Calligraphy
links.description: Pictures of kanji characters and their meanings in several categories.  Also features a list of many common English names transliterated into kana characters.

links.title: Learn Japanese
links.description: Learn to speak Japanese from these online lessons.

815081.title: Dialects
815081.description:
This category is for sites on Japanese dialects.

Websites submitted here must be Japanese dialect related and in English. Sites in Japanese should be submitted to the appropriate World/Japanese subcategory.

日本語のホームページはこちら.

links.title: The Regional Dialect in Nosaka Town
links.description: Examples of regional speech in Nosaka, Chiba Prefecture.

links.title: How to Speak Nagoya Dialect
links.description: Several sample sentences demonstrating Nagoya-ben, from The Nagoya Misonikomi Magazine.

links.description: Shows accent, grammar, and vocabulary differences of the Japanese dialect in Miyagi Prefecture.

links.title: Fun With Fukui-ben
links.description: Offers example words and sentences of dialect used in Fukui.

815079.title: Learning
815079.description: Japanese language resources focusing on learning: online courses, teacher resources, etc. Language schools should be submitted to Reference/Education/International/Language_Schools/Japanese or Regional/Asia/Japan/Education/Language/Japanese_Language_Schools.

links.title: Kana Flashcards
links.description: Kana online learning tool.

links.title: Japanese-Online
links.description: Free Japanese language lessons and translated math story problems from Japan's jr. high math placement tests.

links.title: The Japanese Page
links.description: Learn interesting Japanese while having fun.  Grammar, kanji, culture and a little bit of everything Japanese for free.

links.title: Mainichi-Kanji

links.title: Charles Kelly's Web-based Japanese Language Study Materials
links.description: Free online quizzes, flashcards and word lists. Covers romaji, hiragana, katakana, kanji, Japanese newspaper words, and reading signs.

links.title: Real Kana

links.title: Web Japanese

links.title: Nihongo o Narau - Learn Japanese

links.title: Japanese Podcasting Lessons

links.title: Rikai
links.description: Free site that allows you to read Japanese kanji on any webpage by passing your mouse cursor over the characters.

links.title: The Quick and Dirty Guide to Japanese
links.description: Webpage version of the sci.lang.japan guide to basic Japanese grammar and syntax.

links.title: Japanesepod101.com
links.description: Daily podcasts that teach Japanese from beginning to advanced levels. Requires registration. Only some content is available free.

links.title: CosCom Japanese Language School
links.description: Offers introductory study materials including audio files and grammar lessons.  Also has books, e-books, and picture cards for sale.

links.title: Japanese Verb Conjugator
links.description: Provides a conjugation table for the dictionary form of Japanese verbs. Includes a list of basic verbs.

links.title: infocobuild | Learning Japanese
links.description: A collection of online resources designed to help people learn Japanese.

links.title: NHK Japanese Lessons for English Speakers
links.description: Japan's publicly-funded broadcasting corporation offers free audio lessons.

links.title: Tagaini Jisho

links.title: Erin's Challenge! I can speak Japanese.
links.description: A website by The Japan Foundation for Japanese learners with educational videos and interactive exercises.

links.title: Skritter
links.description: Write Japanese and Chinese characters with a mouse or a tablet and get a score and suggestions on how to improve your handwriting.

links.title: Jim Breen's Japanese Page

links.title: Bilingual Japanese/English Computing Notes
links.description: Japanese keyboard support on English Windows9x/NT/2K/XP, view Japanese documents, browse Japanese web pages, input Japanese characters, print Japanese text, and other bilingual Windows tips.

links.title: Nihongo Resources
links.description: Free online dictionaries (J/E-E/J, kanji, particles, names, onomatopoeia), detailed jouyou kanji lists, Japanese grammar explained up to intermediate level and online lessons.

links.title: Open Japan
links.description: Online tool that enables viewing of Japanese language websites with any graphical browser.

links.title: Open Japan Kana Writer
links.description: Allows you to convert typed romaji to either katakana or hiragana. The resulting converted message has a distinct URL which can then be sent to another person to receive a message in Japanese.

links.title: POPjisyo.com
links.description: Program for viewing Japanese websites, in which hovering the mouse over any word or character brings up a box with definitions and helpful information.  Requires no download or installation.  Can also generate study lists.

links.title: Ethnologue:Achuar-Shiwiar
links.description: Basic demographic and linguistic information.

links.title: Achuar Language and the Achuar Indian Tribe
links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.

links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.

links.title: Shuar Language and the Jivaro Indians
links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.

links.title: Introduction to Korean
links.description: Introduction to Korean alphabet (Hangul) and grammar by J. David Eisenberg.

links.title: Sogang Korean Program
links.description: Offers introductory, novice and intermediate online courses. All lessons include Hangul text, romanizations, and sound files. Requires free registration.

links.title: Let's Learn Korean
links.description: Offers a detailed look at Korean grammar and phonics, along with situational vocabulary.

links.title: Task-Based Language Teaching
links.description: Set of task-based worksheets for teaching Korean as a foreign language.  In PDF and JPEG formats.

links.title: Learn Korean
links.description: Provides a site for learning Korean online, includes tutorials and a student help forum.

links.title: Korean Language Online Exercises
links.description: Has beginning and intermediate lessons with sound.

links.title: Learn Korean @ Aeria Gloris
links.description: Interactive game that teaches the approximate sounds of Hangul letters.

links.title: Mr. Oh's LearnKorean.com

links.title: Learn to Read, Write and Pronounce Korean
links.description: Introduces characters of the alphabet and teaches how to read written syllables.

links.title: HanGhoul
links.description: Web game for learning the Korean alphabet and basic vocabulary.

links.title: Virtual Korean Keyboard
links.description: Onscreen keyboard emulator for typing Korean letters without a Korean operating system or keyboard.

links.title: Infocobuild: Learning Korean
links.description: Provides a collection of on-line resources for learning such as language courses, alphabet, grammar lessons, vocabulary quizzes, and useful phrases.

links.title: Korean Travel Phrases
links.description: A brief list of useful words and phrases.

815071.title: Languages of Africa
815071.description: Web pages dealing with languages belonging to more than one language family in Africa.

links.title: African Language.com
links.description: Interactive multimedia programs from a California company, teaching Amharic, Tigrinya, Somali, and Swahili. Catalog, order form, demos, links.

links.title: African Languages
links.description: Annotated collection of links to web pages providing information on the grammar, pronunciation or vocabulary of various African languages,

links.title: African Languages: An Introduction
links.description: Introduction extracted from a textbook on the major African language groups including coverage of phonology, morphology, syntax, typology and comparative linguistics.

815052.title: Languages of Eurasia
815052.description: Linguistically oriented web pages devoted to languages belonging to more than one language family of Europe and/or Asia. When the languages are restricted to the Middle East (possibly including Anatolia, Egypt and adjacent parts of Africa), the site should be classified in the Languages of the Middle East cat.

links.title: Korais: Editor and E-mail for Ancient Languages
links.description: Editor and E-mail Application for Ancient Languages (Ancient Greek, Coptic, Aramaic, Hieroglyphic Egyptian, Luwian and others). OpenSource Project. To run the application, the Java Virtual Machine (VM), version 1.4.0 or later, must be installed.

links.title: Sound Materials of the Nivkh Language
links.description: Offers sound materials and texts of the Nivkh language spoken on the island of Sakhalin.

814942.title: Languages of the Americas
814942.description: Linguistic material related to languages belonging to more than one native language family of North, Central, or South America, or of the Caribbean.

links.title: The First Nations Languages of British Columbia
links.description: Bibliographic and other information on the native languages of British Columbia.

links.title: Native Languages of the Americas: Preserving and Promoting American Indian Languages
links.description: Portal to a very large number of internet resources devoted to the native languages of North, central and South America.

links.title: Teaching Indigenous Languages
links.description: Papers from endangered languages conferences and short articles on the teaching of native American languages. Topics include policy, promotion, curriculum, schools, and community.

links.title: Southeastern Languages
links.description: Article by Jack B.Martin on languages spoken in the Southeast of the United States, linguistic situation in the past and now.

814889.title: Languages of the Middle East
814889.description: This subcat should be reserved to sites discussing languages belonging to more than one family that are spoken, or used to be spoken, in the Middle East (today's Iran, and all parts of Asia to the west and/or southwest of Iran, including Anatolia and adjacent islands) as well as in Egypt and other parts of the Nile valley. If the languages discussed extend to Central Asia, the Caucasus or parts of Africa outside the Nile valley, this subcat should no longer be considered appropriate.

links.title: Cuneiform Digital Library Initiative
links.description: Document transliterations, text glossaries, digitized originals and photo archives of ancient languages using the cuneiform script.

links.title: Mayan Epigraphic Database
links.description: A relational database of Mayan glyphs, images, phonetic values and semantic values.

links.title: Cakchiquel Language and the Kaqchikel Mayan Tribe
links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.

links.title: Kaqchikel Mayan at KU

links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.

links.title: A Grammar of the Yucatecan Mayan Language
links.description: Online book on Yucatec grammar.

815141.description: Misumalpan languages is a small family of American Indian languages, spoken mostly in eastern Nicaragua and in some adjacent areas of Central America. The biggest and the most know language of this family is Miskito.

links.description: Outline of the context of language loss on the Cold Lake First Nations reserve with description of the collaborative research project between the academic community and regional efforts to revitalize the Dene Suline language.

815301.title: Diné
815301.description: Open to sites related to the language of the Navajo Native American tribe.

links.title: Surveying Attitudes Towards the Navajo Tribe's Language and  Culture Initiative
links.description: Describes the results of a survey of attitudes about the implementation of the Navajo Tribe's mandate to teach Navajo language and culture in all schools in the Navajo Nation.

links.description: Article including a phonological inventory and grammatical information.

links.title: Ethnologue: Navajo
links.description: Basic demographic and linguistic information.

links.description: Pronunciation guide, language learning worksheets, and cultural information.
