804746.title: Gemini
804746.description: NASA's Gemini missions (1965-1966) featured longer flights, spacecraft maneuverability, and multiple pilots.

links.title: Project Gemini: A Chronology
links.description: NASA book detailing all aspects of Project Gemini, including design, development, and flight tests.

804748.title: Mercury
804748.description: NASA's Mercury missions were the first American manned flights into space (1961-1963).

links.title: Project Mercury: A Chronology
links.description: NASA book detailing all aspects of Project Mercury, including prior events, research and development, and mission operations.

804747.title: Skylab
804747.description: Skylab was the United States' first space station. Launched on May 14, 1973, it was manned by three separate crews (May 25 to June 22, 1973;  July 28 to September 25, 1973; and November 16, 1973, to February 8, 1974) who conducted an array of scientific, medical and technical experiments and observations. Skylab was destroyed in controlled re-entry (like Mir) on July  11, 1979.

links.title: Skylab: A Chronology
links.description: The NASA History Office presents an online version of this authoritative book.

804660.title: Unmanned
804660.description: Unmanned Earth orbiting satellites and robotic exploratory spacecraft to the planets, comets, asteroids, and the sun.  Sites pertaining to past, current, and future or proposed missions may be included in this category.

links.title: Space Science Missions of the European Space Agency
links.description: Information and data on those of ESA's past, present, and future satellite missions related to astronomy and astrophysics.

links.title: Canberra Deep Space Communications Complex
links.description: One of the three Deep Space Network stations, CDSCC provides critical communications and tracking information to interplanetary space probes.

links.title: RXTE Mission
links.description: Rossi X-Ray Timing Explorer is a Goddard mission which was  launched on December 30th, 1995. RXTE is designed to facilitate the study of time variability in the emission of X-ray sources with moderate spectral resolution.

links.title: The Wide Field Infrared Explorer (WIRE)
links.description: A spaceborne, cryogenically-cooled imaging telescope designed to explore the evolution of starburst galaxies and to search for protogalaxies.

links.title: XMM-Newton
links.description: The European Space Agency's XMM satellite official home page. News updates and multimedia.

links.title: Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE)
links.description: Offers project and scientific information on a coming infrared observatory mission to observe stars and galaxies.

links.title: Interball
links.description: Provides overview of Russian participation in a mission studying plasma processes with several spacecraft at the L1/L2 Sun/Earth libration points.

links.title: CYGAM
links.description: Offers description and data on a gamma-ray telescope flown on several space missions.

links.title: GAIA: The Galactic Census Project
links.description: A European Space Agency astrometry satellite mission designed to determine the composition, formation and evolution of our Galaxy, and create a detailed 3D map of over a billion stars.

links.title: A History of Unmanned Space Missions
links.description: Chronological listings of unmanned missions from 1957-2004. Includes dates and mission highlights.

804687.title: Asteroids and Comets
804687.description: Unmanned spacecraft sent primarily to observe asteroids and comets.

links.title: ANTS Asteroid Survey
links.description: Study on Autonomous Nano Technology Swarm, a novel concept to survey the asteroid belt using an autonomously operating spacecraft swarm.

links.title: Giotto
links.description: Information on the European mission to Halley's Comet (1985-1992).

links.title: Rosetta
links.description: Mission to rendezvous with the comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko and deploy a lander on its surface. News, mission overview and scientific data compiled by the project team.

804691.title: Deep Impact
804691.description: Deep impact is a NASA Discovery mission scheduled for a 2004 launch and a 2005 encounter comet Tempel 1.  The encounter involves two vehicles.  The main spacecraft will fly by the nucleus of Tempel 1, while an impactor, released from the main spacecraft about 24 hours prior, will impact the comet nucleus at about 10 kilometers per second.  Study of the crater formed and fresh material uncovered will provide an unparalleled opportunity to gain additional understanding of some of the most primitive objects in the solar system.

links.title: Cometography.com: 9P/Tempel 1
links.description: History of 9P/Tempel 1, the Deep Impact target.

804688.title: Deep Space 1
804688.description: Launched by NASA on October 24, 1998, Deep Space 1 is the first of the New Millennium Program missions, testing a variety of advanced spacecraft technologies.

804690.title: Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous
804690.description: NASA's Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous (NEAR) Shoemaker spacecraft was launched in 1996 and conducted the first long-term, close-up study of an asteroid (Asteroid 433 Eros).  NEAR Shoemaker touched down on the surface of Eros on February 12, 2001, and ceased communications on February 28, 2001, marking the end of the very successful mission.

links.title: Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous Mission
links.description: NEAR - First spacecraft to orbit an asteroid, to answer fundamental questions about the nature and origin of near-Earth objects, such as the numerous asteroids and comets in the vicinity of Earth's orbit. First launch in the Discovery Program, a NASA initiative for small planetary missions.

links.title: Boulders Seen on Asteroid
links.description: An image from NEAR's low orbit showing massive boulders on the surface of Eros.

links.title: NEAR Science Update
links.description: A scientific news briefing summarizing the discoveries made by NEAR.

links.title: NEAR Team Deactivates Spacecraft's Near-Infrared Sensor
links.description: Status report on the Near-Infraed Sensor and implications for the mission.

links.title: Mission Archive: NEAR Encounter at Eros
links.description: A large collection of news stories and images, from Space.com.

links.title: NEAR Information
links.description: Detailed mission information, images, and links related to the Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous.

links.title: Gold rush in space?
links.description: Article on NEAR's first encounter with Eros. Suggests that the asteroid may contain trillions of dollars worth of precious metals.

links.title: How Asteroids Work
links.description: Illustrated description of the Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous (NEAR) spacecraft.

804689.title: Stardust
804689.description: A launched NASA mission planning on collect material surrounding the comet P/Wild 2 in 2004.

links.title: Stardust
links.description: Homepage for the space mission that will fly close to a comet and, for the first time ever, bring cometary material back to Earth for analysis by scientists worldwide.

links.title: Stardust Mission
links.description: NASA's mission information and related links.

804695.title: Deep Space
804695.description: Missions studying the universe beyond the solar system.

804696.title: Kepler
804696.description: Launching in 2008, Kepler will explore the structure and diversity of planetary systems, with a special emphasis on the detection of Earth-size planets. It will survey the extended solar neighborhood to detect and characterize hundreds of terrestrial and larger planets in or near the "habitable zone," defined by scientists as the distance from a star where liquid water can exist on a planet's surface. The results will yield a broad understanding of planetary formation, the frequency of formation, the structure of individual planetary systems, and the generic characteristics of stars with terrestrial planets.

804697.title: Earth Observing
804697.description: This category contains space missions with the primary purpose of studying the Earth.

links.title: Earth Observing System (EOS)
links.description: EOS is the centerpiece of NASA's Earth Science Enterprise (ESE). Includes a science component and a data system supporting a coordinated series of polar-orbiting and low inclination satellites for long-term global observations of the land surface, biosphere, solid Earth, atmosphere, and oceans.

links.title: Cluster
links.description: Four ESA spacecraft orbiting the Earth to investigate the small-scale structure (in three dimensions) of the Earth's plasma environment. News, orbital position, mission overview and scientific resources.

links.title: TIMED
links.description: Extensive press kit for NASA's planned two-year TIMED (Thermosphere Ionosphere Mesosphere Energetics and Dynamics) mission, aimed at studying the Mesosphere and Lower Thermosphere/Ionosphere (MLTI).

804698.title: A-Train
804698.description: The "A-Train" is a NASA satellite formation consisting of seven satellites flying in close proximity: Aqua, Aura, CloudSAT, CALIPSO, PARASOL, OCO, and Glory.

804699.title: Aqua
804699.description: Aqua carries six state-of-the-art instruments in a near-polar low-Earth orbit. The six instruments are the Atmospheric Infrared Sounder (AIRS), the Advanced Microwave Sounding Unit (AMSU-A), the Humidity Sounder for Brazil (HSB), the Advanced Microwave Scanning Radiometer for EOS (AMSR-E), the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer (MODIS), and Clouds and the Earth's Radiant Energy System (CERES). Each has unique characteristics and capabilities, and all six serve together to form a powerful package for Earth observations.

subcategories.title: Cloud's and the Earth's Radiant Energy System

links.title: Earth Observatory Library: Aqua
links.description: Offers an overview of the program, discussion of science results, and instrument details.

links.title: Wikipedia - Aqua (satellite)
links.description: Includes an overview of the program and summary of specifications.

links.title: AIRS - DAAC
links.description: Offers data and images from the AIRS/AMSU/HSB suite of instruments which constitute an atmospheric sounding system of infrared, microwave and visible sensors.

804701.title: Cloud's and the Earth's Radiant Energy System
804701.description: The first CERES instrument was launched on the Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM) satellite in November 1997; the second and third CERES instruments were launched on the Terra satellite in December 1999; and the fourth and fifth CERES instruments are on board the Aqua satellite.

804700.title: Moderate-resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer
804700.description: MODIS (Moderate-resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer) is a payload scientific instrument launched into Earth orbit by NASA in 1999 on board the Terra (EOS AM) Satellite, and in 2002 on board the Aqua (EOS PM) satellite. The instruments capture data in 36 spectral bands ranging in wavelength from 0.4 µm to 14.4 µm and at varying spatial resolutions (2 bands at 250 m, 5 bands at 500 m and 29 bands at 1 km).

links.title: MODIS (the MODerate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer)
links.description: Provides extensive and updated information about the Moderate Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer, flown on two NASA spacecraft (Terra and Aqua).

links.title: Wikipedia - Moderate-Resolution Imaging Spectroradiometer
links.description: Offers an overview of the instrument.

links.title: MODIS Rapid Response System
links.description: Provides rapid access to MODIS data, with initial emphasis on 250m color composite imagery and active fire data.

804711.title: Aura
804711.description: Aura (Latin for breeze) was launched July 15, 2004. The design life is five years with an operational goal of six years. Aura flies in formation about 15 minutes behind Aqua. Aura is part of the Earth Observing System (EOS), a program dedicated to monitoring the complex interactions that affect the globe using NASA satellites and data systems.

links.title: Earth Observatory Library: Aura
links.description: Offers an overview of the program, discussion of science results, and instrument details.

links.title: Wikipedia - Aura (satellite)
links.description: Includes an overview of the program and summary of specifications.

links.title: Tropospheric Emission Spectrometer (TES)
links.description: Information about the project, instrument specifications, data products, images and animations.

links.title: Microwave Limb Sounder (MLS)
links.description: Measures naturally-occurring microwave thermal emission from the limb (edge) of Earth's atmosphere to remotely sense vertical profiles of atmospheric gases, temperature, pressure, and cloud ice. Find instrument background, data, and images.

804712.title: High Resolution Dynamics Limb Sounder
804712.description: A multi-channel limb-viewing infrared (IR) radiometer for high resolution monitoring of upper tropospheric, statospheric, and mesospheric temperature, trace chemicals, and geopotential height gradients.

804718.title: CALIPSO
804718.description: CALIPSO is a joint U.S. (NASA)/French (Centre National d’Etudes Spatiales/CNES) mission. Observations from spaceborne lidar, combined with passive imagery, will lead to improved understanding of the role aerosols and clouds play in regulating the Earth’s climate, in particular, how aerosols and clouds interact with one another.

links.title: Earth Observatory Library: CALIPSO
links.description: Offers an overview of the program, discussion of science results, and instrument details.

links.title: Wikipedia - CALIPSO
links.description: Includes an overview of the program and summary of specifications.

links.title: Ball Aerospace & Technologies Corp. - CALIPSO
links.description: Payload manufacturer. Includes a spacecraft overview and information about the LIDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) instrument.

804709.title: CloudSAT
804709.description: CloudSAT, a cooperative mission with Canada, uses advanced radar to "slice" through clouds to see their vertical structure, providing a completely new observational capability from space. CloudSAT will look at the structure, composition, and effects of clouds and is one of the first satellites to study clouds on a global basis.

links.title: CloudSat
links.description: Uses radar to study clouds and precipitation from space. Includes mission information, instrument specifications, news, data products, cloud art, and images.

links.title: Wikipedia - CloudSat
links.description: Includes an overview of the program and summary of specifications.

links.title: Ball Aerospace & Technologies Corp. - CloudSAT
links.description: Payload manufacturer. Includes a spacecraft overview and instrument details.

links.title: CloudSat Data Processing Center
links.description: Satellite status, data products, latest images, and data ordering.

804702.title: Glory
804702.description: Glory’s remote sensing mission is designed to collect data on the optical, microphysical, and chemical properties, and spatial and temporal distributions of aerosols and clouds and to continue the long-term total solar irradiance climate record.

804703.title: Images
804703.description: This category is for NASA and other official sites offering processed data and images of the Earth (Level 3 products). This includes primary authorized distributors of images but does not include third party vendors selling publicly available images and data.

links.title: The Landsat Program
links.description: NASA page describing the program. Landsat satellites provide repetitive coverage of continental Earth surfaces in the visible, near-infrared, short-wave, and thermal infrared regions of the electromagnetic spectrum.

links.title: United States Geological Survey (USGS) - Landsat
links.description: Find project facts, history of Landsats 1 through 7, images, technical details, and resources.

links.title: Landsat Program
links.description: Landsat information from the Ecosystem Science and Technology Branch of the Earth Science Division at Ames Research Center. Includes news, mission status, laws, and policies on data use.

links.title: Earth Observatory Library: Landsat 7
links.description: Offers an overview of the program, discussion of science results, images, and validation information.

804707.title: OCO
804707.description: The Orbiting Carbon Observatory (OCO) provides space-based observations of atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2), the principal anthropogenic driver of climate change. This mission uses mature technologies to address NASA's carbon cycle measurement requirement. OCO generates the knowledge needed to improve projections of future atmospheric CO2.

804710.title: Orbview2-SeaWiFS
804710.description: The Orbview-2 (aka SeaStar) spacecraft, developed by Orbital Sciences Corporation, carries the SeaWiFS instrument and was launched to low Earth orbit on board an extended Pegasus launch vehicle on August 1, 1997.  The purpose of the Sea-viewing Wide Field-of-view Sensor (SeaWiFS) Project is to provide useful data on ocean color to the Earth science community. Subtle changes in ocean color indicate various types and numbers of marine phytoplankton (microscopic marine plants), knowing this information can have both scientific and practical uses.

links.title: Wikipedia - SeaWiFS
links.description: Find a summary of information about this scientific sensor on the Orbview-2 satellite.

804705.title: PARASOL
804705.description: PARASOL (Polarization and Anisotropy of Réflectances for Atmospheric Sciences coupled with Observations from a Lidar) is a French's CNES microsatellite project. Its main purpose is to improve the characterization of the clouds and aerosols microphysical and radiative properties, needed to understand and model the radiative impact of clouds and aerosols.

804708.title: QuickBird
804708.description: QuickBird was manufactured by Ball Aerospace and launched in October 2001. It collects high resolution imagery  - panchromatic (black & white) imagery at 60-70 centimeter resolution and multispectral imagery at 2.4- and 2.8-meter resolutions.

links.title: Wikipedia - QuickBird
links.description: Find an overview and specifications for this commercial earth observation satellite.

links.title: Ball Aerospace & Technologies Corp. - Quickbird
links.description: Offers information from the manufacturer about the satellite.

804706.title: SORCE
804706.description: The Solar Radiation and Climate Experiment (SORCE) is a NASA-sponsored satellite mission that is providing state-of-the-art measurements of incoming x-ray, ultraviolet, visible, near-infrared, and total solar radiation.

links.title: Solar Radiation and Climate Experiment (SORCE)
links.description: Measures the x-ray, ultraviolet, visible, near-infrared, and total solar radiation incident on the Earth. Includes science background, data, instrument details, and images.

links.title: Earth Observatory Library: Solar Radiation and Climate Experiment (SORCE)
links.description: Includes a description of the impact of solar radiance on Earth's climate and an overview of SORCE data and images.

links.title: Wikipedia - Solar Radiation and Climate Experiment
links.description: Includes program background and satellite specifications.

804717.title: TRMM
804717.description: The Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM), is the first mission dedicated to measuring tropical and subtropical rainfall through microwave and visible infrared sensors, and includes the first spaceborne rain radar.

links.title: Wikipedia - Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission
links.description: Includes an overview of the program and summary of specifications.

links.title: Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission (TRMM)
links.description: A joint NASA and JAXA mission to monitor and study tropical rainfall. Includes mission background, news, publications, current images, and data access.

links.title: JAXA - TRMM
links.description: Information, photos, and data from the Earth Observation Research Center of Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency.

links.title: Earth Observatory Library: Tropical Rainfall Measuring Mission
links.description: Offers an overview of the program, discussion of science results, and instrument details.

804713.title: Terra
804713.description: The Terra (formerly called EOS AM-1) satellite is the flagship of NASA’s Earth Science Missions. Terra is the first EOS (Earth Observing System) platform and provides global data on the state of the atmosphere, land, and oceans, as well as their interactions with solar radiation and with one another.

links.title: Earth Observatory Library: Terra
links.description: Offers an overview of the program, discussion of science results, and animations.

links.title: Wikipedia - Terra (satellite)
links.description: Includes an overview of the program and summary of specifications.

804716.title: ASTER
804716.description: The Advanced Spaceborne Thermal Emission and Reflection Radiometer (ASTER) is an imaging instrument  flying on Terra, a satellite launched in December 1999 as part of NASA's Earth Observing System (EOS).

804714.title: MISR
804714.description: MISR (Multi-angle Imaging SpectroRadiometer) is a scientific instrument on the Terra satellite launched by NASA on December 18, 1999. The device is designed to measure the solar radiation reflected by the Earth system (planetary surface and atmosphere) in various directions and spectral bands.

links.title: Wikipedia - Multi-angle Imaging SpectroRadiometer
links.description: Provides an overview of the instrument.

804715.title: MOPITT
804715.description: Measurements of Pollution in the Troposphere (MOPITT) is a payload scientific instrument launched into Earth orbit by NASA on board the Terra satellite in 1999. It is designed to monitor changes in pollution patterns and its effect in the lower atmosphere of the Earth.

links.title: Wikipedia - MOPITT
links.description: Offers an overview of the instrument.

links.title: MOPITT from the University of Toronto
links.description: Includes news, photo gallery, publications, and campaigns.

804686.title: Sputnik
804686.description: Launched at the height of the Cold War, the Soviet Union's Sputnik program marked the first successful launch of a man-made satellite. The Sputnik launch was an historically significant event; it is the first entry in many Space Age and Internet timelines.

804723.title: Mars
804723.description: Space missions to the planet Mars.

804731.title: 2001 Mars Odyssey
804731.description: Launched on April 7, 2001 and scaled down from the planned Mars Surveyor 2001 mission, NASA's 2001 Mars Odyssey is planned to map the mineralogy and terrain of the Martian surface. It successfully entered Mars orbit on October 23, 2001.

links.description: NASA's latest news from Spirit and Opportunity. The primary goal of the robots is to search for and characterize a wide range of rocks and soils that hold clues to past water activity on Mars.

links.title: NPR : Mars Rover Marks Second Anniversary of Landing
links.description: On the two-year anniversary of mars rover Spirit's landing,   both rovers (Spirit and Opportunity) are going strong. The robotic geologists have provided invaluable data about whether Mars could once harbor life.  [7:33 streaming audio broadcast]

804727.description: Among the NASA Mariner missions, Mariner 4, 6, 7 and 9 were sent to Mars.

804733.title: Mars Climate Orbiter
804733.description: Launched in 1998 and intended to relay Mars mapping data, soon after entering the Martian atmosphere, the Mars Climate Orbiter was declared lost by NASA in September 1999.

804730.title: Mars Express
804730.description: A European Space Agency mission that arrived to Mars end of 2003. The spacecraft included a lander called Beagle 2. However, the lander failed to produce scientific results.

804722.title: MESSENGER
804722.description: MErcury Surface, Space ENvironment, GEochemistry and Ranging (MESSENGER) is a NASA Discovery mission launched in August 2004. The primary objectives of MESSENGER are to study Mercury from orbit for a period of one Earth year. MESSENGER is equipped with an imaging system, x-ray, ultraviolet, energetic particle and plasma, gamma-ray and neutron spectrometers, laser altimeter, magnetometer and radio science experiments.

804665.title: Voyager
804665.description: The twin Voyager 1 and 2 spacecraft were launched in 1977 to explore the outer solar system.  More than 25 years later they are approaching the solar system boundary region -- the heliopause -- where the Sun's dominance of the environment ends and interstellar space begins.  The primary mission was the exploration of Jupiter and Saturn. After making a string of discoveries there -- such as active volcanoes on Jupiter's moon Io and intricacies of Saturn's rings -- the mission was extended. Voyager 2 went on to explore Uranus and Neptune, and is still the only spacecraft to have visited those outer planets. The adventurers' current mission, the Voyager Interstellar Mission (VIM), will explore the outermost edge of the Sun's domain.

Get details about current and former group members, ongoing research, publications, and view some models and animations.
